items.description: Joomla Extension - vi-solutions - Stored XSS via SQL field labels in Visforms extension 1.0.0-5.6.4, 6.0.0-6.2.1 - Labels and values of SQL field options were returned unescaped by the reload task and inserted into the page as HTML, allowing stored XSS if the statement reads user-supplied data.

items.title: NLTK: Uncontrolled recursion in WordNet Synset hypernym walkers (max_depth/min_depth/hypernym_paths/hypernym_distances) causes DoS
items.description: NLTK (Natural Language Toolkit) is a suite of open source Python modules, data sets, and tutorials supporting research and development in Natural Language Processing. Prior to 3.10.4, WordNet Synset.max_depth, min_depth, hypernym_paths, and hypernym_distances recursively follow attacker-controlled corpus pointers without a visited-node set or depth cap. A cyclic or excessively deep hypernym graph can raise RecursionError and terminate traversal APIs and similarity operations that depend on them. This issue is fixed in version 3.10.4.

items.title: NLTK: Quadratic-time DoS in SeekableUnicodeStreamReader.readline on an unterminated corpus line via per-iteration full-buffer rescan
items.description: NLTK (Natural Language Toolkit) is a suite of open source Python modules, data sets, and tutorials supporting research and development in Natural Language Processing. Prior to 3.10.4, SeekableUnicodeStreamReader.readline appends each new block to a growing character buffer and reruns splitlines over the entire buffer on every iteration. An attacker-controlled corpus file containing one very long unterminated line therefore causes quadratic CPU consumption in line-oriented corpus readers and can deny service. This issue is fixed in version 3.10.4.

items.title: NLTK: StreamBackedCorpusView constructor os.stat leaks out-of-root file existence, size, and mtime bypassing pathsec ENFORCE
items.description: NLTK (Natural Language Toolkit) is a suite of open source Python modules, data sets, and tutorials supporting research and development in Natural Language Processing. From 3.10.0 until 3.10.4, StreamBackedCorpusView performs os.stat on a caller-supplied plain string path during construction before pathsec containment is enforced. The PathPointer branch used by in-tree corpus readers is validated, so exploitation requires application code to pass an attacker-influenced string directly to the public constructor. That string can identify an out-of-root path and disclose its existence, size, and modification time even though opening the file would be rejected. This issue is fixed in version 3.10.4.

items.title: Joomla Extension - vi-solutions - Missing core.create check in form creation in Visforms extension 1.0.0-5.6.3, 6.0.0-6…
items.description: Joomla Extension - vi-solutions - Missing core.create check in form creation in Visforms extension 1.0.0-5.6.3, 6.0.0-6.2.0 - The createForm task of the form creator did not check the core.create permission, allowing backend users without create permission to create forms.

items.title: Natural Language Toolkit (NLTK): Uncontrolled recursion (crash DoS) in DependencyGraph.tree()/triples()
items.description: NLTK (Natural Language Toolkit) is a suite of open source Python modules, data sets, and tutorials supporting research and development in Natural Language Processing. Prior to 3.10.4, DependencyGraph.tree and DependencyGraph.triples walk parsed dependency edges through unbounded Python recursion and do not use a working cycle or depth guard. A crafted CoNLL or Malt-TAB dependency file containing a sufficiently long chain can raise RecursionError when the documented traversal APIs are called, aborting the current worker. This issue is fixed in version 3.10.4.

items.title: Natural Language Toolkit (NLTK): Uncontrolled recursion (crash DoS) in Synset.tree()/acyclic_tree() via WordNet relation traversal
items.description: NLTK (Natural Language Toolkit) is a suite of open source Python modules, data sets, and tutorials supporting research and development in Natural Language Processing. Prior to 3.10.4, WordNet Synset.tree and acyclic_tree traverse relation graphs through recursive utility helpers without a depth bound. Exploitation requires the host application to load an attacker-influenced custom or foreign WordNet-format lexical resource; no relation in NLTK's bundled WordNet 3.0 corpus reaches the crash threshold. An excessively deep relation graph in such a resource can exceed the Python recursion limit and terminate the traversal or request worker. This issue is fixed in version 3.10.4.

items.title: NLTK: Compile-time regex DoS in NLTK search/tokenizer sinks: quadratic regex-engine compile bypasses the match-only timeout
items.description: NLTK (Natural Language Toolkit) is a suite of open source Python modules, data sets, and tutorials supporting research and development in Natural Language Processing. From 3.10.0 until 3.10.4, TokenSearcher.findall and Text.findall accept caller-controlled regular expressions with an unbounded number of capturing groups throughout the affected range. Starting in 3.10.3, nltk.redos.compile and RegexpTokenizer expose the same compile-time vector. The third-party regex engine compiles group-dense patterns with roughly quadratic cost before the match-time timeout begins, allowing a small unauthenticated request to exhaust CPU and deny service. This issue is fixed in version 3.10.4.

items.title: NLTK: Uncontrolled recursion in DependencyGraph traversal causes denial of service via deep dependency chains
items.description: NLTK (Natural Language Toolkit) is a suite of open source Python modules, data sets, and tutorials supporting research and development in Natural Language Processing. In 3.10.3 and earlier, DependencyGraph._tree and triples recurse once per dependency edge without a depth bound, and get_cycle_path also lacks a visited-set termination guard. A deeply chained or cyclic attacker-controlled CoNLL or Malt-TAB dependency structure can raise RecursionError and abort a parse worker. This issue is fixed in version 3.10.4.

items.title: NLTK: Uncontrolled recursion in semantic-logic type parser causes denial of service via nested type strings
items.description: NLTK (Natural Language Toolkit) is a suite of open source Python modules, data sets, and tutorials supporting research and development in Natural Language Processing. Prior to 3.10.4, the semantic-logic read_type parser recursively processes both halves of nested complex type strings without applying LogicParser.MAX_PARSE_DEPTH. An attacker-controlled type string or signature with excessive nesting can raise RecursionError through Type.fromstring or type-checking entry points and abort the current worker. This issue is fixed in version 3.10.4.

items.title: NLTK: Uncontrolled recursion in Tree.fromlist causes denial of service via deeply nested list input
items.description: NLTK (Natural Language Toolkit) is a suite of open source Python modules, data sets, and tutorials supporting research and development in Natural Language Processing. Prior to 3.10.4, Tree.fromlist recursively converts nested Python list input into Tree objects without enforcing a maximum tree depth. An attacker-controlled list nested beyond the interpreter recursion limit can raise RecursionError and terminate the current parse operation or request worker. This issue is fixed in version 3.10.4.

items.title: NLTK incomplete fix: additional JVM/JAR sandbox bypass through unvalidated launcher tokens in java() command arguments
items.description: NLTK (Natural Language Toolkit) is a suite of open source Python modules, data sets, and tutorials supporting research and development in Natural Language Processing. From 3.10.3 until 3.10.4, the NLTK 3.10.3 JVM hardening validates Java launcher tokens in the options channel but appends the caller-controlled cmd sequence without requiring its first token to be a main class. Supplying -jar or an @argfile through nltk.internals.java or StanfordSegmenter.java_class can therefore execute attacker-selected Java bytecode without the unsafe-JAR opt-in. This issue is fixed in version 3.10.4.

items.title: NLTK: XMLCorpusView comment and CDATA parsing permits quadratic CPU denial of service
items.description: NLTK (Natural Language Toolkit) is a suite of open source Python modules, data sets, and tutorials supporting research and development in Natural Language Processing. From 3.6 to 3.10.3, XMLCorpusView._read_xml_fragment accumulates 1 KiB blocks and repeatedly applies whole-buffer XML validation while a comment or CDATA terminator remains ahead. A large comment in an attacker-controlled corpus file causes quadratic CPU consumption through documented XML corpus readers across the affected range. On 3.6 and 3.9.2, a large CDATA section incurs the quadratic scan before rejection, while on 3.10.3 both comment and CDATA documents are read successfully. This vulnerability is fixed in 3.10.4.

items.title: NLTK: Downloader cyclic collection indices cause an infinite closure walk
items.description: NLTK (Natural Language Toolkit) is a suite of open source Python modules, data sets, and tutorials supporting research and development in Natural Language Processing. From 3.6.7 until 3.10.4, nltk.downloader follows collection membership without tracking already visited collection nodes. A self-referencing or mutually referencing collection index can therefore make the package-closure walk loop indefinitely while its queue and memory usage grow, denying service when a victim processes the attacker-influenced index. This issue is fixed in version 3.10.4.

items.title: Improper certificate validation vulnerability in Estonian Information System Authority (RIA) libdigidocpp, Estonian Inf…
items.description:
Improper certificate validation vulnerability in Estonian Information System Authority (RIA) libdigidocpp, Estonian Information System Authority (RIA) DigiDoc4, and Estonian Information System Authority (RIA) DigiDoc on Android and iOS.

This issue affects libdigidocpp: from 3.13.0 before 4.5.2; DigiDoc4: from 4.0.0 before 4.11.2; DigiDoc: from 3.0.0 before 3.2.0.

items.title: NLTK: ARFF_Formatter Injects Weka ARFF Schema Directives via Attacker-Controlled Class Labels
items.description: NLTK (Natural Language Toolkit) is a suite of open source Python modules, data sets, and tutorials supporting research and development in Natural Language Processing. Prior to 3.10.4, nltk.classify.weka.ARFF_Formatter writes attacker-controlled class labels into the Weka ARFF @ATTRIBUTE '-label-' declaration without safely formatting the label tokens. Crafted labels can alter the generated ARFF schema or records, corrupting classifier input and causing integrity loss or processing failure. This issue is fixed in version 3.10.4.

items.title: NLTK: ZIP package extraction follows in-root hardlinks and overwrites files outside the NLTK data root
items.description: NLTK (Natural Language Toolkit) is a suite of open source Python modules, data sets, and tutorials supporting research and development in Natural Language Processing. From 3.9.4 to 3.10.3, NLTK ZIP package extraction can write through an existing in-root hardlink whose other link points outside the NLTK data root. A local attacker who can prepare the extraction target can cause a package member write to overwrite an out-of-root file, violating the pathsec containment boundary and affecting integrity and availability. This issues is fixed in version 3.10.4.

items.title: NLTK: AllowlistUnpickler does not deny numpy submodule-local file-I/O sinks
items.description: NLTK (Natural Language Toolkit) is a suite of open source Python modules, data sets, and tutorials supporting research and development in Natural Language Processing. From 3.10.0 until 3.10.4, allowlisted_pickle_load keys dangerous NumPy globals by export name, allowing submodule-local numpy.lib file input/output callables to evade the denylist under the broad module allowance used by TransitionParser. A crafted pickle can invoke recfromtxt to read a local file or open_memmap to create or truncate an attacker-selected file when a victim loads an untrusted model. This issue is fixed in version 3.10.4.

items.title: InfoScan fails to properly handle certain malformed or incomplete requests to its login and password-reset endpoints.
items.description: InfoScan fails to properly handle certain malformed or incomplete requests to its login and password-reset endpoints. These requests can trigger unhandled server exceptions that return detailed Node.js stack traces to the requester. The responses disclose internal filesystem paths, application directory names, source file locations, and line numbers.

items.title: The InfoScan Electron desktop client improperly handles TLS certificate errors by accepting certificates without valida…
items.description: The InfoScan Electron desktop client improperly handles TLS certificate errors by accepting certificates without validating their trustworthiness. The client also configures Electron with nodeIntegration enabled, contextIsolation disabled, and webSecurity disabled. These settings weaken the client’s security boundaries. An attacker who is able to intercept or manipulate network communications may be able to present an untrusted certificate without the application rejecting the connection.

items.title: The publicly distributed InfoScan Electron installer contains configuration files identifying hostnames associated with…
items.description: The publicly distributed InfoScan Electron installer contains configuration files identifying hostnames associated with customer installations and internal development, testing, and database infrastructure. An individual who obtains and inspects the installer can extract these hostnames without authenticating to the affected systems.

items.title: InfoScan contains an unauthenticated information disclosure vulnerability in its mobile-enumeration and version-reporti…
items.description: InfoScan contains an unauthenticated information disclosure vulnerability in its mobile-enumeration and version-reporting endpoints. A remote attacker can send HTTP requests without authentication to retrieve system configuration information, including usernames and display names, multifactor authentication configuration status, session settings, application version information, server details, hardware module firmware versions, and the BACnet/IP port used by the installation.

items.title: InfoScan does not enforce authentication on an endpoint used to retrieve sales-automation templates.
items.description: InfoScan does not enforce authentication on an endpoint used to retrieve sales-automation templates. A local attacker can submit an HTTP request to the affected endpoint without a valid session and retrieve the returned template data.

items.title: @fastify/static is the Fastify plugin for serving static files.
items.description: @fastify/static is the Fastify plugin for serving static files. In versions before 10.1.8, the allowedPath guard receives only the requested pathname, but the underlying send step selects the file to serve afterwards, so a request for a directory resolves to its default index file and an extensionless request resolves through the configured extensions to a matching file. The selected file is streamed without being re-checked against allowedPath, so a guard that denies a specific file is bypassed by requesting its directory or extensionless form. An unauthenticated client can read files inside the static root that the application meant to keep private whenever the denied file is reachable as a directory index or an extension match. The issue is fixed in @fastify/static 10.1.8, and users should upgrade to 10.1.8 or later. As a workaround, also deny the directory and extensionless forms in allowedPath, or disable the index and extensions options.

items.title: InfoScan uses hard-coded cryptographic keys and initialization-vector values in its database-encryption implementation.
items.description: InfoScan uses hard-coded cryptographic keys and initialization-vector values in its database-encryption implementation. The application uses these values to encrypt the MongoDB password before storing it in the Windows registry. Because the cryptographic material is embedded in the distributed application, an individual with access to the encrypted registry value and the application code may be able to recover the database password.

items.title: Bolt ListFormatHelper SQL injection
items.description: Bolt is a fully open source, adaptable platform for building and running modern websites. Prior to 6.1.4, SQL injection in ListFormatHelper allows authenticated users with upload permission to execute arbitrary SQL queries through /async/select-options and exfiltrate sensitive database contents when general/caching/list_format is enabled. This issue is fixed in version 6.1.4.

items.title: Bolt: Open redirect enables post-authentication redirection to arbitrary domains
items.description: Bolt is a fully open source, adaptable platform for building and running modern websites. Prior to 6.1.4, LoginFormAuthenticator accepts unsafe destinations for the login success redirect and login failure redirect. An attacker can direct a user to an attacker-controlled domain after authentication succeeds or fails, enabling phishing and potential token theft. This issue is fixed in version 6.1.4.

items.title: falcon-rust: Discrete-Gaussian sampler runs at 2^-33 precision, far below Falcon's requirement (reference KAT vectors no longer pass)
items.description: falcon-rust is a Rust implementation of the Falcon post-quantum signature scheme. Prior to 0.2.0, the discrete-Gaussian sampler in src/samplerz.rs evaluates approx_exp, ber_exp, and sampler_z acceptance probabilities with FixedPoint64 values having only 32 fractional bits. The scaling in approx_exp quantizes its input and limits relative precision to about 2^-33, below Falcon's required bound, causing reference known-answer vectors to diverge and invalidating the proof assumption that secret-dependent signature and key distributions are negligibly close to the ideal discrete Gaussian. This is a cryptographic-soundness defect and no practical key-recovery attack has been demonstrated. This issue is fixed in version 0.2.0.

items.title: Bolt: Information disclosure through unfiltered public relation API endpoint
items.description: Bolt is a fully open source, adaptable platform for building and running modern websites. Prior to 6.1.4, the public Relation API lacks an access-control filter. Unauthenticated users can query its REST endpoints and GraphQL endpoints to discover metadata about unpublished, draft, and viewless content. This issue is fixed in version 6.1.4.

items.title: Bolt: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) in URL-upload and embed endpoints
items.description: Bolt is a fully open source, adaptable platform for building and running modern websites. Prior to 6.1.4, the authenticated URL-upload endpoint and authenticated embed endpoint fetch user-supplied URLs server-side without protection against internal targets, allowing an attacker with the applicable backend permission to cause the Bolt server to request those targets. This issue is fixed in version 6.1.4.

items.title: Bolt: Prevent SSRF due to unchecked followed redirects
items.description: Bolt is a fully open source, adaptable platform for building and running modern websites. Prior to 6.1.5, the /bolt/async/upload-url and /bolt/async/embed endpoints validate only a submitted URL before fetching it server-side. The fetchers then follow redirects without revalidating each destination, allowing an authenticated user to bypass UrlSafetyChecker and cause the server to request internal or cloud-metadata addresses. This issue is fixed in version 6.1.5.

items.title: Daptin: Broken Access Control (IDOR) in the generic YJS collaboration endpoint
items.description: Daptin is a GraphQL/JSON-API headless CMS. From 0.11.4 until 0.12.30, the generic GET /yjs/:documentName WebSocket route in InitializeYjsResources requires a session but does not authorize the database resource selected by a typename.referenceId.columnName room name. The YJS initial-content provider then reads the selected file.* column without CanRead or CanUpdate checks, and bidirectional synchronization allows a low-privileged authenticated user to read or modify restricted row content. Unauthenticated requests are rejected, and standalone non-canonical room names remain shared-by-name rooms. This issue is fixed in version 0.12.30.

items.title: Daptin: Unauthenticated SQL Injection via the `sort` query parameter on every entity list endpoint
items.description: Daptin is a GraphQL/JSON-API headless CMS. Prior to 0.12.30, the generic GET /api/{entity} list endpoint accepts attacker-controlled sort values in PaginatedFindAllWithoutFilters in server/resource/resource_findallpaginated.go without validating the requested column against the table schema. The code uses those values for SELECT and ORDER BY identifier construction, so an embedded identifier quote can terminate the quoted identifier and make the remainder parse as SQL, allowing an unauthenticated attacker to extract unauthorized table data through blind or error-based behavior or repeatedly trigger query failures. This issue is fixed in version 0.12.30.

items.title: Sprout Track is a self-hosted baby tracking application.
items.description: Sprout Track is a self-hosted baby tracking application. Prior to 1.3.5, Sprout Track uses a publicly known hardcoded signing secret when JWT_SECRET is unset, and standard setup does not generate a unique secret. On a network-reachable affected deployment, an unauthenticated attacker can sign JWTs with arbitrary claims, including system-administrator claims, to access administrative functionality and read or modify family, child activity, account, and email data. Deployments with a strong unique JWT_SECRET are not affected. Managed and hosted instances were reported remediated. This issue is fixed in version 1.3.5.

items.title: Jupyter MCP Server: Browser DNS rebinding can hijack the Jupyter backend through management routes
items.description: Jupyter MCP Server is a Model Context Protocol server for Jupyter. Prior to 1.0.3, standalone streamable-http mode validates Host and Origin values for /mcp but does not apply the same browser-origin controls to the state-changing /api/connect and /api/stop management routes. A malicious website can use DNS rebinding so that its hostname resolves to a loopback, LAN, VPN, or published-container MCP listener, then send a browser-shaped request that /api/connect accepts to replace runtime_url and document_url values and start a kernel client against attacker-controlled infrastructure. The attacker can thereby cause Jupyter API and WebSocket traffic to reach that infrastructure and can use /api/stop to stop the current notebook kernel. The default broad bind can increase exposure, but the vulnerability is the missing management-route origin boundary, not a lack of Host validation on /mcp. This issue is fixed in version 1.0.3.

items.title: Jupyter MCP Server: Unauthenticated management routes can hijack the Jupyter backend in standalone HTTP mode
items.description: Jupyter MCP Server is a Model Context Protocol server for Jupyter. Prior to 1.0.3, standalone streamable-http mode can enforce MCP_TOKEN on /mcp while leaving the state-changing /api/connect and /api/stop management routes unauthenticated. An unauthenticated network caller can use /api/connect to replace runtime_url and document_url values and their tokens, reset ServerContext, and start a kernel client against attacker-controlled infrastructure, causing the server to send Jupyter API and WebSocket traffic to that backend. The caller can also use /api/stop to stop the current notebook kernel. This boundary failure does not require explicit insecure no-auth mode and occurs outside normal MCP JSON-RPC tool dispatch. This issue is fixed in version 1.0.3.

items.title: Aperi'Solve is an open-source steganalysis web platform.
items.description: Aperi'Solve is an open-source steganalysis web platform. Prior to 3.4.2, an unauthenticated user can submit a PNG to POST /upload, which reaches aperisolve/utils/png.py through analyze_image, PCRTAnalyzer, PNG.repair(), and check_idat(). A malformed IDAT chunk can make attacker-controlled length and newline data drive an unbounded combinations search in PNG._fix_dos2unix(), causing repeated CRC checks that occupy a worker and delay or block image analysis for other users. Per-IP upload limits and eventual job termination bound the denial of service, and the issue has no confidentiality or integrity impact. This issue is fixed in version 3.4.2.

items.title: django-docutils unsafe Docutils defaults allow local file disclosure, SSRF, and stored XSS
items.description: django-docutils provides reStructuredText support for Django. Prior to 0.30.0, public rendering paths including publish_doctree, publish_html_from_source, publish_html_from_doctree, publish_parts_from_doctree, the {% rst %} template tag, the rst template filter, DocutilsTemplates, and DocutilsView pass lower-trust reStructuredText to Docutils without disabling file_insertion_enabled, raw_enabled, ambient docutils.conf processing, or unsafe URI schemes and without consistently sanitizing doctrees. An attacker who can influence rendered reStructuredText can use include or csv-table directives to read local files or cause server-side URL requests, or use raw HTML and unsafe URI output to inject stored script-capable content. Applications that render only trusted static reStructuredText are not affected unless attackers can influence it. This issue is fixed in version 0.30.0.

items.title: Git LFS may attempt arbitrary remote commands via crafted SSH URLs
items.description: Git LFS is a Git extension for versioning large files. From 0.5.0 until 3.8.1, Git LFS does not format the SSH URL path component as a single argument when constructing remote object-transfer or authentication commands. Shell metacharacters in the SSH URL can therefore escape the intended path argument and cause arbitrary command execution when the remote Git LFS service passes received commands to a shell without adequate sanitization. Git LFS also incorrectly encodes default HTTPS URLs when an SSH URL is configured and the remote host either does not support Git LFS remote commands over SSH or supports HTTP authentication over SSH but git-lfs-authenticate does not return an explicit HTTP URL. This issue is fixed in version 3.8.1.

items.title: Git LFS may leak HTTP headers after redirections
items.description: Git LFS is a Git extension for versioning large files. From 0.5.0 until 3.8.1, Git LFS may forward a Cookie header after an HTTP redirect to a host other than the one for which the header was intended. That unintended host can therefore receive cookies containing credentials or other confidential values. Authorization headers are never forwarded to inappropriate hosts and are not the affected secret in this vulnerability. This issue is fixed in version 3.8.1.

items.title: Frappe is a full-stack web application framework.
items.description: Frappe is a full-stack web application framework. Prior to 15.108.0 and 16.18.3, the add_comment handler in frappe/templates/includes/comments/comments.py trusts the client-provided comment_by and comment_email fields. A caller can submit chosen identity metadata that is stored with a comment, causing the comment to appear to originate from another name or email address. This issue is fixed in versions 15.108.0 and 16.18.3.

items.title: The visitor tracking of JTL-Shop automatically registers unknown crawler user agents without filtering the value, and t…
items.description:
The visitor tracking of JTL-Shop automatically
registers unknown crawler user agents without filtering the value, and the stored
value is rendered without output encoding on several pages of the
administration backend (search engine statistics, crawler dashboard widget, crawler
edit form, sitemap export download list and campaign details). An
unauthenticated remote attacker can store script code with a single request. The code is
executed in the browser session of an administrator who opens one of these
pages, allowing actions to be performed with the administrator's privileges.

items.title: When the setting for saving requests to non-existent pages (404) is enabled, JTL-Shop stores the raw requested URL in i…
items.description:
When the setting for saving requests to non-existent
pages (404) is enabled, JTL-Shop stores the raw requested URL in its
redirect table, and the administration backend renders it without output
encoding in the form used to edit a redirect. An unauthenticated remote
attacker can store script code with a single request, which is executed in the
browser session of an administrator who opens the affected redirect,
allowing actions to be performed with the administrator's privileges. The
setting is disabled by default in new installations but may still be
enabled in older ones.

items.title: ClassiCube before 1.4.0 contains a heap-based out-of-bounds write vulnerability in Png_Decode in src/Bitmap.c that allo…
items.description: ClassiCube before 1.4.0 contains a heap-based out-of-bounds write vulnerability in Png_Decode in src/Bitmap.c that allows malicious servers to corrupt client memory by sending a PNG with a duplicate IHDR chunk. Attackers can supply crafted PNGs via texture pack URLs or player skins so the unreset bufferIdx underflows remaining space, letting IDAT data overflow the buffer to crash clients or execute code.

items.title: @scalar/typebox before 0.1.4 contains a code injection vulnerability in TypeCompiler that allows attackers to execute J…

items.title: A vulnerability in the Audio, Web, and Video Conferencing (AWV) component of Mitel MiCollab through 10.3 (10.3.0.18) co…
items.description: A vulnerability in the Audio, Web, and Video Conferencing (AWV) component of Mitel MiCollab through 10.3 (10.3.0.18) could allow an unauthenticated attacker, with knowledge of a specific system-generated random identifier or pre-staged content, to conduct an unauthorized access attack due to improper authentication mechanisms. A successful exploit could allow an attacker to obtain sensitive information. The vulnerability is limited to the affected functionality and does not provide unrestricted access to arbitrary files elsewhere on the system. This is MTLVULN-1863.

items.title: ClassiCube before 1.4.0 contains a heap-based out-of-bounds write vulnerability in Png_Reconstruct in src/Bitmap.c that…
items.description: ClassiCube before 1.4.0 contains a heap-based out-of-bounds write vulnerability in Png_Reconstruct in src/Bitmap.c that occurs when AVERAGE and PAETH filters process zero-width PNG images. A malicious multiplayer server can supply a crafted texture pack URL or player skin to write past the heap buffer, corrupting memory and crashing connecting clients.

items.title: A vulnerability in the Audio, Web, and Video Conferencing (AWV) component of Mitel MiCollab through 10.3 (10.3.0.18) co…
items.description: A vulnerability in the Audio, Web, and Video Conferencing (AWV) component of Mitel MiCollab through 10.3 (10.3.0.18) could allow an unauthenticated attacker to leverage pre-staged malicious content to conduct an XML injection attack due to insufficient parameter validation. A successful exploit could allow an attacker to execute arbitrary commands within the context of the system. This is MTLVULN-1862.

items.title: VideoLAN libaacs 0.7.0 through 0.12.0 contains a stack-based buffer overflow vulnerability in aacs_resolve_path() that…
items.description: VideoLAN libaacs 0.7.0 through 0.12.0 contains a stack-based buffer overflow vulnerability in aacs_resolve_path() that allows local attackers to corrupt stack memory via crafted symlinks in disc paths. Attackers can plant a symlink with a long target in an extracted archive, removable media or shared directory, so that strcat() overflows the 1024-byte link buffer when opened, crashing the player or potentially executing code.

items.title: When extra data is allowed (extra=Extra.allow), providing a __pydantic_initialised__ key when validating a Pydantic V1…
items.description: When extra data is allowed (extra=Extra.allow), providing a __pydantic_initialised__ key when validating a Pydantic V1 dataclass makes it considered as already validated, resulting in field values not being validated. The __init__() method of Pydantic V1 dataclasses stores all the provided keyword arguments in the instance __dict__ before validation, so a __pydantic_initialised__ keyword argument overrides the internal flag used to skip validation of already validated instances. As a result, data returned by validation doesn't match the declared type. Affected are applications validating untrusted data into Pydantic V1 dataclasses allowing extra data. The issue was fixed in Pydantic 1.10.27. Users relying on the pydantic.v1 namespace in Pydantic V2 should upgrade to 2.14.2 or later.

items.title: sqlmap before 1.10.11.89 contains a credential exposure vulnerability that allows attackers to capture user-supplied Co…
items.description: sqlmap before 1.10.11.89 contains a credential exposure vulnerability that allows attackers to capture user-supplied Cookie and Authorization headers by redirecting requests to another host. Attackers controlling the scanned target or abusing an open redirect can make RedirectHandler.http_error_302 forward session cookies or bearer tokens to an attacker-controlled host.

items.title: A flaw was found in quarkus-vertx-utils.
items.description: A flaw was found in quarkus-vertx-utils. When a client disconnects while receiving a streaming response, the server fails to detect the closed connection and continues processing the data indefinitely. An unauthenticated remote attacker can exploit this issue by repeatedly initiating streaming requests and disconnecting, exhausting worker threads and resulting in a Denial of Service (DoS).

items.title: A command injection vulnerability was found in OpenStack Cinder's SSH-based storage-driver support.
items.description: A command injection vulnerability was found in OpenStack Cinder's SSH-based storage-driver support. Incomplete validation of shell metacharacters allows an authenticated user who owns a volume on an affected backend to supply crafted connection information and inject additional commands into the storage array's management interface. Commands execute with the privileges of Cinder's configured backend account. This can disclose storage configuration information and, where that account has administrative permissions, could allow changes that affect the integrity or availability of other tenants' storage.

items.title: A flaw was found in GIMP.
items.description: A flaw was found in GIMP. Opening a crafted XCF with a truncated uncompressed tile can expose uninitialized main-process stack memory through the imported layer's pixel data, which may include process addresses that weaken ASLR.

items.title: NLTK: Untrusted search path in prover9/mace4 config allows local code execution via relative binary_location
items.description: NLTK (Natural Language Toolkit) is a suite of open source Python modules, data sets, and tutorials supporting research and development in Natural Language Processing. Prior to 3.10.4, Prover9Parent.config_prover9 and Mace accept a relative binary_location and pass it to find_binary as path_to_bin, disabling the bare-name absolute-path guard. A local attacker who can plant prover9 or mace4 in the resolved working directory can cause subprocess.Popen to execute that binary with the invoking user's privileges. This issue is fixed in version 3.10.4.

items.title: NLTK: Quadratic CPU exhaustion in NLTK XMLCorpusView.read_block via deeply nested XML corpus tags
items.description: NLTK (Natural Language Toolkit) is a suite of open source Python modules, data sets, and tutorials supporting research and development in Natural Language Processing. Prior to 3.10.4, XMLCorpusView.read_block rebuilds the full root-to-node context path with "/".join(context) for every start tag while searching for a matching element. Deeply nested attacker-influenced corpus XML therefore causes quadratic pure-Python work and can pin a processing worker, resulting in denial of service. This issue is fixed in version 3.10.4.

items.title: Git LFS may execute arbitrary commands via crafted Git configurations
items.description: Git LFS is a Git extension for versioning large files. From 0.6.0 until 3.8.1, Git LFS reads Git configuration options defined for a submodule without checking certain values for embedded line-ending control characters. A malicious repository can insert control characters such as line feed (LF) into those values to mimic options that cause Git LFS to execute an attacker-controlled command or binary while fetching or adding objects. This issue is fixed in version 3.8.1.

items.title: Git LFS may execute arbitrary commands via crafted Git LFS configurations
items.description: Git LFS is a Git extension for versioning large files. From 1.3.0 until 3.8.1, Git LFS does not correctly filter the limited set of options permitted in a repository's .lfsconfig file when option keys contain certain additional components. Crafted keys can mimic options that configure Git LFS to use a custom command to transfer objects, causing Git LFS to execute an attacker-selected command or binary while fetching objects. This issue is fixed in version 3.8.1.

items.title: HTSlib is a library for reading and writing bioinformatics file formats.
items.description: HTSlib is a library for reading and writing bioinformatics file formats. Prior to 1.21.2, 1.22.3, 1.23.2, and 1.24, the BCF reader can experience an integer overflow in a record-length check that verifies whether a record contains enough bytes for the expected number and size of stored items. A crafted BCF record can bypass this check, causing reads beyond the stored data and, in some cases, writes beyond the heap buffer when the reader sets the least significant bit of accessed bytes. Opening such a file can crash the process, corrupt data or heap structures, and may permit arbitrary code execution. This issue is fixed in versions 1.21.2, 1.22.3, 1.23.2, and 1.24.

items.title: HTSlib is a library for reading and writing bioinformatics file formats.
items.description: HTSlib is a library for reading and writing bioinformatics file formats. Prior to 1.21.2, 1.22.3, 1.23.2, and 1.24, the experimental CRAM v4 functions cram_xpack_decode_char and cram_xrle_decode_char do not validate that attacker-controlled decode sizes remain within their expanded input arrays. Crafted CRAM data can therefore make either decoder read beyond the supplied input buffer, potentially disclosing process-state information or crashing the process through invalid memory access. This issue is fixed in versions 1.21.2, 1.22.3, 1.23.2, and 1.24.

items.title: HTSlib is a library for reading and writing bioinformatics file formats.
items.description: HTSlib is a library for reading and writing bioinformatics file formats. Prior to 1.21.2, 1.22.3, 1.23.2, and 1.24, the CRAM BETA decoder functions cram_beta_decode_long, cram_beta_decode_int, and cram_beta_decode_char, and the experimental CRAM v4 XPACK functions cram_xpack_decode_long and cram_xpack_decode_int, have bounds-checking flaws caused by integer overflow after a multiplication. The resulting incorrect bounds check can allow decoding to read beyond the supplied input buffer, potentially leaking process-state information or crashing the process. This issue is fixed in versions 1.21.2, 1.22.3, 1.23.2, and 1.24.

items.title: HTSlib is a library for reading and writing bioinformatics file formats.
items.description: HTSlib is a library for reading and writing bioinformatics file formats. Prior to 1.21.2, 1.22.3, 1.23.2, and 1.24, the experimental CRAM v4 XPACK and XRLE decoders cache expanded block pointers at indexes beyond the 512-element slice->block_by_id array. An array index partially controlled by data in the input file first causes an out-of-bounds read to determine whether a block is cached; a null value then causes allocation of a block and an out-of-bounds pointer write to the same element. The invalid read may crash the process, while the write may corrupt heap state and could permit arbitrary code execution. This issue is fixed in versions 1.21.2, 1.22.3, 1.23.2, and 1.24.

items.title: HTSlib is a library for reading and writing bioinformatics file formats.
items.description: HTSlib is a library for reading and writing bioinformatics file formats. Prior to 1.21.2, 1.22.3, 1.23.2, and 1.24, the CRAM decoder validates the 254-character query-name limit only after decoding the name into a 1024-byte stack array. An attacker-controlled CRAM record can provide an overlong query name and overflow the local stack buffer before the later validation runs; all CRAM format versions are affected. Opening such a file can crash the process, corrupt stack data, and may permit arbitrary code execution. This issue is fixed in versions 1.21.2, 1.22.3, 1.23.2, and 1.24.

items.title: HTSlib is a library for reading and writing bioinformatics file formats.
items.description: HTSlib is a library for reading and writing bioinformatics file formats. Prior to 1.21.2, 1.22.3, 1.23.2, and 1.24, cram_index_load does not verify that the number of reference sequences in a CRAM .crai index does not exceed the CRAM header reference count. A malformed index can drive unbounded index-array allocation, and when the number of references in the index is within two of INT_MAX, the growth calculation can wrap, read beyond a heap buffer, and use the resulting value as a pointer for an unchecked memory write. Any region query can trigger the flaw, causing denial of service or memory corruption. This issue is fixed in versions 1.21.2, 1.22.3, 1.23.2, and 1.24.

items.title: HTSlib is a library for reading and writing bioinformatics file formats.
items.description: HTSlib is a library for reading and writing bioinformatics file formats. Prior to 1.21.2, 1.22.3, 1.23.2, and 1.24, fai_retrieve does not verify that the line width recorded in a FASTA .fai index is greater than or equal to the number of bases per line. When the line width is exactly one less than the base count, retrieval allocates an undersized heap buffer and writes one byte beyond its end; larger discrepancies instead cause an allocation failure that is handled. This issue can corrupt heap memory and crash the process. This issue is fixed in versions 1.21.2, 1.22.3, 1.23.2, and 1.24.

items.title: A flaw was found in Moodle.
items.description: A flaw was found in Moodle. Due to a missing authorization check when editing Lesson activity pages, authenticated users with teacher privileges can view and move lesson pages from courses they are not permitted to access into their own lessons. This issue can lead to unauthorized access and modification of restricted course content.

items.description: A flaw was found in Moodle. Insufficient authorization checks in the quiz editing functionality allow an authenticated user with teacher privileges to view slot details and modify sections of quizzes they do not have permission to manage. An attacker could exploit this flaw to alter quiz configurations or disclose quiz structure information without proper authorization.

items.description: A flaw was found in Moodle's single view grade report web service. This vulnerability leads to unauthorized information disclosure.

An attacker could exploit this vulnerability to improperly alter exam access, deadlines, or testing conditions across unauthorized courses.

items.title: A flaw was found in Moodle.

Due to insufficient authorization checks in the quiz random question filter web service, an authenticated user with teacher privileges can modify random question settings in quizzes they do not have permission to manage. This flaw allows unauthorized users to alter assessment configurations across courses they do not oversee.

items.title: A flaw was found in Moodle.
items.description: A flaw was found in Moodle. This can result in unauthorized access, modification, or deletion of course materials.

items.title: A flaw was found in Moodle.
items.description: A flaw was found in Moodle. This vulnerability can lead to unauthorized data disclosure and tampering with badge configurations.

items.title: A flaw was found in Moodle.
items.description: A flaw was found in Moodle. Missing authorization checks in the forum discussion web services allow authenticated users to view discussion information in courses they do not have permission to access. In addition, users with teacher privileges may lock forum discussions in courses where they lack proper authorization. This issue can lead to unauthorized information disclosure and unauthorized discussion state modification.

items.title: A flaw was found in Moodle.
items.description: A flaw was found in Moodle. Insufficient sanitization of objective identifiers in the SCORM (Sharable Content Object Reference Model) objectives report allows an authenticated user with content upload permissions to inject malicious scripts. When another user views the report, the injected script executes in their browser session, potentially allowing the attacker to access sensitive information or perform unauthorized actions on their behalf.

items.title: A flaw was found in Moodle.
items.description: A flaw was found in Moodle. Due to insufficient permission checks and input validation in the quiz question bank callback, an authenticated user can access and view questions from question banks they do not have permission to access. Furthermore, this issue allows users to trigger arbitrary class instantiation (creating unintended application objects), potentially leading to further unauthorized actions.

items.title: A flaw was found in Moodle.
items.description: A flaw was found in Moodle. An improper authorization check when displaying individual glossary entries allows an authenticated user to view approved glossary items from courses they do not have permission to access. This vulnerability leads to unauthorized information disclosure of restricted educational materials.

items.title: A flaw was found in Moodle.
items.description: A flaw was found in Moodle. Due to a missing authorization check when viewing and restoring wiki page versions, an authenticated user can access content from courses they are not permitted to view. This issue allows an attacker to inspect restricted course material and copy it into their own wiki pages, leading to unauthorized information disclosure.

items.title: A flaw was found in Moodle's external database enrolment plugin.
items.description: A flaw was found in Moodle's external database enrolment plugin. Insufficient sanitization of data passed to queries against the external database allows an authenticated user with course editing permissions to perform a Structured Query Language (SQL) injection attack. When this non-default plugin is enabled, an attacker can exploit this issue to view, modify, or delete sensitive records within the connected external database.

items.description: A flaw was found in Moodle's Blackboard question import format. Insufficient validation of file paths during the question import process allows an authenticated user with permissions to import questions into a question bank to read arbitrary files accessible to the web server process. An attacker could leverage this vulnerability to view sensitive files, resulting in unauthorized information disclosure.

items.title: United Chargers Grizzl-E Smart 40A OCPP UpdateFirmware Out-Of-Bounds Write Remote Code Execution Vulnerability.
items.description:
United Chargers Grizzl-E Smart 40A OCPP UpdateFirmware Out-Of-Bounds Write Remote Code Execution Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows network-adjacent attackers to execute arbitrary code on affected installations of United Chargers Grizzl-E Smart 40A EV chargers. Authentication is not required to exploit this vulnerability.

The specific flaw exists within the handling of OCPP UpdateFirmware requests. The issue results from the lack of proper validation of user-supplied data, which can result in a write past the end of an allocated buffer. An attacker can leverage this in conjunction with other vulnerabilities to execute code in the context of the device. Was ZDI-CAN-29487.

The specific flaw exists within the handling of OCPP backend configuration requests. The issue results from the lack of authentication prior to allowing access to functionality. An attacker can leverage this in conjunction with other vulnerabilities to execute arbitrary code in the context of the device. Was ZDI-CAN-29063.

items.title: NATS Server MQTT subscribe permission bypass exposes internal QoS 2 metadata
items.description:
### Background

NATS.io is a high performance open source pub-sub distributed communication technology, built for the cloud, on-premise, IoT and edge computing.

The NATS Server MQTT support uses internal `$MQTT.*` subjects to implement MQTT protocol features such as QoS handling.

### Problem Description

An authenticated MQTT client could subscribe to an internal MQTT delivery subject that was not intended to be available to clients.

This bypassed configured subscribe permissions for that internal subject family and exposed MQTT QoS2 protocol metadata for sessions in the account. Message payloads were not exposed through this path.

This issue was related to an incomplete restriction on internal MQTT subjects. It affected MQTT users whose ordinary subscribe permissions would not otherwise allow access to those internal subjects.

### Affected Versions

Versions v2.14.2, v2.12.7 and below are vulnerable. The issue is fixed in v2.14.3 and v2.12.8.

### Workarounds

No known workaround for deployments that require MQTT. Upgrade to a fixed release. Deployments not using MQTT are not affected.

### References

 * GHSA advisory: <https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/security/advisories/GHSA-4g68-3pwx-5vfj>
 * Credit: Koda Reef

items.title: NATS Server: MQTT SUBSCRIBE Protocol Injection via Leaf Node/Route Forwarding allows arbitrary NATS command injection
items.description:
### Background

NATS.io is a high performance open source pub-sub distributed communication technology, built for the cloud, on-premise, IoT and edge computing.

The NATS Server supports MQTT clients and can bridge MQTT activity into NATS subjects across routes and leafnode connections.

### Problem Description

An MQTT client could include protocol control characters in subscription filters that were later forwarded as NATS protocol data to route or leafnode connections.

This could corrupt the forwarded protocol stream and allow injection of unintended NATS protocol operations, potentially across cluster nodes or accounts where route or gateway connections are present.

Anonymous MQTT deployments are higher risk because no credentials are required to reach the affected parser. Authenticated deployments are still affected for clients allowed to create MQTT subscriptions.

### Affected Versions

Versions v2.14.0, v2.12.8 and below are vulnerable. The issue is fixed in v2.14.1 and v2.12.9.

### Workarounds

Disable anonymous MQTT access where it is not required. Deployments that need MQTT have no known complete workaround other than upgrading.

### References

 * GHSA advisory: <https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/security/advisories/GHSA-qrcv-3558-gj4f>
 * Credit: @thesecguy45

items.title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: smb: smbdirect: don't wait for RDMA_CM_EVENT_DISCON…
items.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

smb: smbdirect: don't wait for RDMA_CM_EVENT_DISCONNECTED in smbdirect_socket_destroy_sync()

smbdirect_socket_destroy_sync() waited for RDMA_CM_EVENT_DISCONNECTED
after smbdirect_socket_cleanup_work() called rdma_disconnect(). That
can take very long, e.g. if the peer just disappeared, until the
rdma cm gives up, or forever if the event already happened, but the
status was overwritten afterwards.

This is not needed: smbdirect_socket_destroy() drains the qp under
rdma_lock_handler(), destroys it and calls rdma_destroy_id(), which
only waits for a currently running event handler and makes sure no
further events are delivered. The rest of the disconnect protocol
(DREQ/DREP and timewait for IB, abrupt close for iWarp) is handled
by the rdma core asynchronously. drivers/nvme/host/rdma.c also just
calls rdma_disconnect() and ib_drain_qp() before rdma_destroy_id().

So smbdirect_socket_destroy() now also accepts
SMBDIRECT_SOCKET_DISCONNECTING and changes the status to
SMBDIRECT_SOCKET_DISCONNECTED itself under rdma_lock_handler().

We could still get RDMA_CM_EVENT_DISCONNECTED in the small
windows between rdma_unlock_handler() and rdma_destroy_id(),
but in that case smbdirect_connection_rdma_event_handler()
is basically a no-op.

items.title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ksmbd: wait for negotiation before receiving anothe…
items.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ksmbd: wait for negotiation before receiving another PDU

The receive thread queues a request and can read the next PDU before
the negotiation worker finishes. While need_neg is set, the next PDU
can cause ksmbd_init_smb_server() to replace conn->ops. A pipelined
SMB2 request can therefore make the worker handle an earlier, shorter
SMB1 request with SMB2 operations and read beyond its buffer.

An SMB1 multi-protocol negotiate may be followed by an SMB2 NEGOTIATE
that changes conn->ops again. Wait for work queued while the connection
is new or needs negotiation to complete before reading another PDU.
This keeps the operations stable for both stages of negotiation without
changing when need_neg is cleared.

items.title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ksmbd: serialize directory emptiness checks with re…
items.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ksmbd: serialize directory emptiness checks with readdir

SMB2 QUERY_DIRECTORY holds fp->readdir_lock while it calls iterate_dir()
on fp->filp. An SMB2 SET_INFO request with FILE_DISPOSITION_INFORMATION
can resolve the same FileId and call ksmbd_vfs_empty_dir() on the same
filp without that lock.

iterate_dir()'s inode read lock permits concurrent readers and does not
serialize per-file iterator state. ext4 stores its dx readdir cursor and
fname RB tree in file->private_data. Concurrent reset or refill can
therefore free a fname node while the other worker still traverses it or
retains its RB-tree link, resulting in use-after-free accesses.

An authenticated SMB client with list and delete rights on a directory in
a writable KSMBD share backed by ext4 can trigger this when the directory
takes the dx readdir path. The client overlaps an SMB2 QUERY_DIRECTORY
request with an SMB2 SET_INFO request carrying FILE_DISPOSITION_INFORMATION
on one live FileId.

In one x86_64 SMP KASAN multi-shot guest using ksmbd-for-next at
171df27077fb, the unmodified kernel reported a cross-worker use-after-free
before a panic. The first report's access and free stacks show the two
request paths directly (trimmed):

  BUG: KASAN: slab-use-after-free in ext4_htree_store_dirent+0x488/0x550
  Read of size 8 by task kworker/2:0/29
  Workqueue: ksmbd-io handle_ksmbd_work
  Call Trace:
   ext4_htree_store_dirent+0x488/0x550
   htree_dirblock_to_tree+0x535/0x990
   ext4_htree_fill_tree+0x319/0xba0
   ext4_readdir+0x175a/0x2f40
   iterate_dir+0x1b6/0x630
   smb2_query_dir+0x1003/0x1cc0

  Freed by task 279:
   free_rb_tree_fname+0x67/0xc0
   ext4_readdir+0x13a9/0x2f40
   iterate_dir+0x1b6/0x630
   ksmbd_vfs_empty_dir+0xa2/0x100
   smb2_set_info+0x2ffa/0x45d0

Take fp->readdir_lock across the entire emptiness check. This places both
iterators over that handle's filp in the same lock domain while
preserving the disposition status handling. The exact code change
completed a warning-free x86_64 KASAN bzImage build. Tracing three request
pairs showed that the two iterate_dir() calls no longer overlapped and the
expected statuses were preserved. A further 1,600 reproducer iterations
completed with expected statuses and no KASAN report, Oops, or panic.

The reproducer and complete guest configuration are available privately
to maintainers on request.

items.title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ceph: fail readdir when the MDS reply carries no di…
items.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ceph: fail readdir when the MDS reply carries no dirfrag

A ceph mount oopses in ceph_readdir() when the MDS answers a READDIR
request with a reply whose extra blob is empty.  parse_reply_info()
skips reply blobs whose length is zero, so parse_reply_info_readdir()
never runs, r_reply_info.dir_dir stays NULL, and the reply still
parses as successful.  ceph_mdsc_do_request() returns 0 and
ceph_readdir() then reads rinfo->dir_dir->frag with no NULL check:

	/* extra */
	ceph_decode_32_safe(&p, end, len, bad);
	if (len > 0) {
		...
		err = parse_reply_info_extra(&p, p + len, req, features, s);
		...
	}

The oops on v7.3.0-rc4-00537-ga3ff15db6820, one getdents64(2) on the
mount root after an ms_mode=legacy mount, trimmed:

BUG: KASAN: null-ptr-deref in range [0x0000000000000000-0x0000000000000007]
Oops: general protection fault, probably for non-canonical address 0xdffffc0000000000: 0000 [#1] SMP KASAN NOPTI
CPU: 1 UID: 0 PID: 266 Comm: ls Tainted: G                 N  7.3.0-rc4-00537-ga3ff15db6820 #1 PREEMPT(lazy)
RIP: 0010:ceph_readdir+0xbff/0x3ea0
Call Trace:
 <TASK>
 ? __pfx_ceph_readdir+0x10/0x10
 wrap_directory_iterator+0xa2/0xe0
 iterate_dir+0x1da/0x5d0
 __x64_sys_getdents64+0x13b/0x2a0
 do_syscall_64+0xdd/0x4a0
 entry_SYSCALL_64_after_hwframe+0x77/0x7f
 </TASK>

The unconditional frag read came in with 81c6aea5275ea ("ceph: handle
frag mismatch between readdir request and reply"), so the bug is old.

Treat a reply with no dirfrag as a protocol violation: warn once,
drop the request and return -EIO, the same way ceph_readdir() already
handles the two malformed-reply cases later in the function.

Tested on v7.3.0-rc4-00537-ga3ff15db6820 (KASAN).  Unpatched, the
getdents64(2) above takes the machine down (oops=panic) on the first
READDIR reply.  With the patch it warns once and getdents64(2)
returns -EIO, no oops, no hang.  A conformant reply for an empty
directory — dirfrag present, zero entries, FRAG_END|FRAG_COMPLETE —
still lists "." and ".." and returns EOF on both kernels, so normal
readdir behavior is unchanged.  The oops is still present in
v7.3-rc5 (72d3fcf802c45).

items.title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: blk-crypto: fix NULL deref and UAF in __blk_crypto_…
items.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

blk-crypto: fix NULL deref and UAF in __blk_crypto_evict_key()

Sashiko reported a possible NULL pointer dereference, triggered by the
following flow:

  dm-inlinecrypt ctor            # first use of the fallback
   ├─ blk_crypto_init_key()      # succeeds, ctx->key.size != 0
   ├─ blk_crypto_start_using_key()
   │   ├─ hw-wrapped key: -EOPNOTSUPP
   │   │    # profile never allocated (NULL)
   │   └─ raw key: fallback_start_using_mode()
   │      └─ blk_crypto_fallback_init() fails
   │         └─ kfree(profile)   # not NULLed
   ├─ goto bad
   └─ inlinecrypt_dtr()          # evicts whenever key.size is set
      └─ blk_crypto_evict_key()
         └─ blk_crypto_config_supported_natively() = false
            └─ blk_crypto_fallback_evict_key()
               └─ __blk_crypto_evict_key(blk_crypto_fallback_profile)
                  └─ profile->num_slots # BOOM!!!

This issue can be reproduced using the following commands:

  dd if=/dev/zero of=/tmp/backing bs=1M count=64
  LOOP=$(losetup -f --show /tmp/backing)
  SZ=$(blockdev --getsz $LOOP)
  KEY=$(head -c 64 /dev/urandom | od -An -tx1 | tr -d ' \n')
  dmsetup create ic --table "0 $SZ inlinecrypt aes-xts-plain64 \
    $KEY 0 $LOOP 0 1 keytype:hw-wrapped"

And the following oops is triggered:

  ==================================================================
  blk-crypto: loop0: no support for wrapped keys
  Oops: general protection fault, probably for non-canonical address
        0xdffffc000000000b: 0000 [#1] SMP KASAN PTI
  KASAN: null-ptr-deref in range [0x0000000000000058-0x000000000000005f]
  CPU: 5 UID: 0 PID: 901 Comm: dmsetup 7.3.0-rc3 #1 PREEMPT(lazy)
  RIP: 0010:__blk_crypto_evict_key+0x2e/0x3b0
  Call Trace:
   blk_crypto_evict_key+0x24c/0x320
   inlinecrypt_dtr+0xf6/0x160
   inlinecrypt_ctr+0x2d3/0xbd0
   dm_table_add_target+0x661/0xf40
   table_load+0x1c4/0x490
   ctl_ioctl+0x32f/0x5f0
   dm_ctl_ioctl+0xe/0x20
  ==================================================================

dm-inlinecrypt is the only caller that can evict a key that was never
started, as fscrypt frees such a key without evicting it.

Fix this by returning early from blk_crypto_fallback_evict_key() when
tfms_inited[] is not set for the key's mode.  tfms_inited[] is only set
after blk_crypto_fallback_init() has successfully initialized the
profile, so the crash above is no longer reachable.

The bug has been latent since commit c984ff1423ae ("blk-crypto:
dynamically allocate fallback profile") was merged in v6.5, and only
became actually triggerable when commit e7f57d2c47e2 ("dm-inlinecrypt:
add target for inline block device encryption") was merged in v7.2.

items.title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ARM: 9524/1: mm: align hugetlb mappings to the huge…
items.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ARM: 9524/1: mm: align hugetlb mappings to the huge page size

mmap(MAP_HUGETLB) on 32-bit Arm can return an address which is not
aligned to the huge page size. In a QEMU virt guest, unmapping the VMA
then hits the alignment check in __unmap_hugepage_range():

  kernel BUG at mm/hugetlb.c:5213!
  Internal error: Oops - BUG: 0 [#1] SMP ARM
  PC is at __unmap_hugepage_range+0x540/0x584
  LR is at __zap_vma_range+0x13a0/0x1410

Commit 7bd3f1e1a9ae ("mm: make hugetlb mappings go through
mm_get_unmapped_area_vmflags") made hugetlb mappings use the
architecture's arch_get_unmapped_area(). The generic implementations
handle hugetlb alignment, but the Arm implementations only account for
the optional SHMLBA cache-colouring constraint. A 4 KiB-page kernel can
therefore align the mapping to 4 KiB or 16 KiB instead of the required
2 MiB.

Set the alignment mask from the file's hstate for hugetlb mappings in
both Arm implementations. Huge-page alignment also satisfies the
SHMLBA constraint.

items.title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: wifi: mt76: mt7925: fix reset panic caused by the W…
items.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

wifi: mt76: mt7925: fix reset panic caused by the WM2 rx irq mask

mt7925_irq_map sets wm2_complete_mask, but mt7925_dma_layout has no
tx done ring, so the MT_RXQ_MCU_WA queue and its NAPI are never set up.
On a chip reset, mt7925e_mac_reset() calls napi_disable() on that NAPI
and crashes:

  BUG: kernel NULL pointer dereference, address: 0000000000000a40
  Workqueue: mt76 mt7925_mac_reset_work [mt7925_common]
  RIP: 0010:mutex_lock+0x1c/0x50
  Call Trace:
   napi_disable+0x1d/0x50
   mt7925e_mac_reset+0x327/0x420 [mt7925e]
   mt7925_mac_reset_work+0x9a/0x1a0 [mt7925_common]

Remove the WM2 mask from mt7925_irq_map and from
MT7925_INT_RX_DONE_ALL.

items.title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: fork: don't create io threads once PF_POSTCOREDUMP…
items.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

fork: don't create io threads once PF_POSTCOREDUMP is set

zap_process() skips every thread that already has PF_POSTCOREDUMP set.
Such a thread is past synchronize_group_exit(), so a coredump can't
catch it anymore. It isn't counted in core_state->threads_remaining and
it isn't sent SIGKILL.

do_exit() sets PF_POSTCOREDUMP in synchronize_group_exit() and calls
io_uring_files_cancel() right after that. The cancellation runs task
work and a create_worker_cb() that io-wq queued before the exit creates
a new io-wq worker from there. If another thread started a coredump in
the meantime that worker joins a thread-group which is already being
dumped. zap_process() never saw it so it was never counted. But when it
exits it sees signal->core_state in synchronize_group_exit() and
decrements threads_remaining like any other thread.

So the count reaches zero one thread early and the dumper leaves
coredump_wait_inactive() while a thread it counted is still running.

The task has no fatal signal pending because zap_process() deliberately
didn't send it one, and it never went through get_signal() so it doesn't
have PF_SIGNALED either.

Refuse to create an io thread when the creator has PF_POSTCOREDUMP.
That costs nothing. io_uring_files_cancel() raises IO_WQ_BIT_EXIT
before it runs any task work, so a worker created from there only ever
gets to exit again, and io_should_retry_thread() doesn't retry -EINTR.

Clearing PF_POSTCOREDUMP for the new thread in copy_process() was the
other option. It makes the worker a thread like any other, but it only
helps while the dump hasn't started. A worker born after zap_process()
has run is invisible to it whatever its flags say and still decrements
threads_remaining on the way out. Refusing to create it covers both, and
then no task is ever born with the flag, so there is nothing to clear.

Moving io_uring_files_cancel() ahead of synchronize_group_exit() closes
the same window. It runs the cancellation, and whatever that can block
on, before the thread announces itself to the dumper. A thread that
blocks there never reaches coredump_task_exit() at all, so the dumper
ends up waiting for a thread that never parks. Refusing the creation
leaves the cancellation where it is. But it's very ugly to run io_uring
work even before we did all the generic exit work.

items.title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ksmbd: reject FSCTL_SET_ZERO_DATA on a directory ha…
items.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ksmbd: reject FSCTL_SET_ZERO_DATA on a directory handle

An authenticated client with a writable tree connection can open a
directory with FILE_WRITE_DATA and send FSCTL_SET_ZERO_DATA on that
handle. The handler only checks fp->daccess & FILE_WRITE_DATA_LE, but on
a directory FILE_WRITE_DATA is the legitimate add-file right, so the
check passes. ksmbd_vfs_zero_data() then calls kernel_write() on the
directory file, which has no FMODE_WRITE, and __kernel_write_iter()
hits WARN_ON_ONCE(!(file->f_mode & FMODE_WRITE)), panicking a
panic_on_warn kernel.

Before commit 25e414db7033 ("ksmbd: report holes in allocated range
queries") the dense-file path used vfs_fallocate(), which rejects
directories with -EISDIR. The kernel_write() loop that replaced it has
no such check. Reject a directory handle in ksmbd_vfs_zero_data() before
writing, as ksmbd_vfs_write() already does for SMB2_WRITE.

  WARNING: fs/read_write.c:608 at __kernel_write_iter+0x74b/0x8c0
  Workqueue: ksmbd-io handle_ksmbd_work
  Call Trace:
   kernel_write+0x1ef/0x4d0
   ksmbd_vfs_zero_data+0x413/0x590
   smb2_ioctl+0x21fa/0x66a0
   handle_ksmbd_work+0x61b/0x1ff0

items.title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: smb: smbdirect: release failed pending sockets of a…
items.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

smb: smbdirect: release failed pending sockets of a listener

A child of a listener only left the listen.pending or listen.ready
list via smbdirect_socket_accept() or when the listener was
destroyed. So every connection that failed before it was accepted
(negotiate timeout, peer disconnect, invalid negotiate request, ...)
stayed on the list and counted against the backlog until the listener
was destroyed. After about backlog (10 for ksmbd) such connections
smbdirect_listen_connect_request() rejected every new connection with
-EBUSY, so an unauthenticated peer was able to permanently stop
ksmbd from accepting SMB-Direct connections.

Now a failed child moves itself to a new listen.orphaned list at the
end of smbdirect_socket_cleanup_work(), after the disconnect was
started, and queues listen.purge_orphaned_work, which releases it
with smbdirect_socket_release(), without holding the listener's
rdma_lock_handler() lock, in the same way smbdirect_socket_destroy()
does for the remaining children. Orphaned sockets still count against
the backlog until they are released.

sc->accept.listener is now only changed under listener->listen.lock
and whoever clears it is responsible for releasing the socket:
smbdirect_socket_accept(), purge_orphaned_work or the destroy of the
listener.

In order to make that work:

- a struct smbdirect_socket that is a listener is now freed via
  kfree_rcu(), so that a child can dereference sc->accept.listener
  under rcu_read_lock(), even if the listener is released concurrently.

- smbdirect_listen_connect_request() adds nsc to the listen.pending
  list and sets nsc->accept.listener before it calls
  smbdirect_accept_connect_request(), and always returns 0 so the
  rdma_cm core keeps the connection id and nsc owns it. On a non-zero
  return it schedules nsc's teardown with
  smbdirect_socket_schedule_cleanup(), which orphans it off the
  listener so that purge_orphaned_work releases it; nsc destroys its
  own connection id with rdma_destroy_id() in that teardown. The
  teardown has to be deferred because the rdma_cm core holds nsc's
  id_priv->handler_mutex across the handler, so nsc->rdma.cm_id must
  not be destroyed synchronously from here. That same handler_mutex
  (and the listener's) also guarantees nsc can't go away under us,
  so setting the listener before the call is safe and lets a failure
  orphan nsc.

- smbdirect_accept_negotiate_recv_work() no longer moves a socket to
  the ready list if it already failed or no longer belongs to the
  listener. Every accepting socket has a listener, so if
  sc->accept.listener is already cleared, it no longer sends a
  negotiate response, as the socket is about to be released.

- smbdirect_socket_destroy() of the listener disables
  purge_orphaned_work and also releases the orphaned sockets.

items.title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: smb: client: fix early procfs exposure race Current…
items.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

smb: client: fix early procfs exposure race

Currently, init_cifs() calls cifs_proc_init() near the beginning of
the function, before INIT_LIST_HEAD, leading to a momentarily
uninitialized, but exposed, procfs. If a userspace process reads this
empty procfs, iterating over a zeroed list_head leads to a NULL
pointer dereference and a kernel oops/panic.

For example, if a delay is added between cifs_proc_init() and
INIT_LIST_HEAD, and a userspace process is polling
/proc/fs/cifs/DebugData, the following oops occurs:

BUG: kernel NULL pointer dereference, address: 0000000000000608
Oops: Oops: 0000 [#1] SMP PTI
CPU: 0 UID: 0 PID: 3477 Comm: cat Not tainted
7.3.0-02212-g4df4d2a577db-dirty #6 PREEMPT(lazy)
RIP: 0010:cifs_debug_data_proc_show+0x103/0xd80 [cifs]
Call Trace:
<TASK>
 ? seq_read_iter+0x86/0x400
 ? seq_read_iter+0x86/0x400
 seq_read_iter+0x183/0x400
 proc_reg_read_iter+0x62/0x90
 copy_splice_read+0x215/0x310
 splice_file_to_pipe+0xec/0x1c0
 do_splice+0x4b8/0x780
 __se_sys_splice+0x18f/0x250
 do_syscall_64+0x109/0x330
 entry_SYSCALL_64_after_hwframe+0x77/0x7f
</TASK>

Fix this by moving cifs_proc_init() down in init_cifs(), ensuring it runs
only after all internal lists, locks, counters, and workqueues are fully
ready, but before registering the filesystem. Update the error cleanup
ladder and exit_cifs() to maintain proper LIFO order.

items.title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: smb: client: do not pass a NULL buf to is_oplock_br…
items.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

smb: client: do not pass a NULL buf to is_oplock_break()

receive_encrypted_read() sets *num_mids = 1 and never writes the
caller's bufs[]. Offload returns -1 with *num_mids = 0, so the
demultiplex thread skips the frame. The inline decrypt path
returns 0 even when smb2_find_mid() fails.

cifs_demultiplex_thread() then treats mids[i] == NULL as an
oplock break and calls is_oplock_break(bufs[i], server) with
bufs[i] still NULL. smb2_is_valid_oplock_break() reads
hdr.Command at offset 12 and oopses.

A large encrypted READ whose MessageId does not match is enough
to panic cifsd.

    Oops: general protection fault, probably for non-canonical address
    0xdffffc0000000001: 0000 [#1] SMP KASAN PTI
    KASAN: null-ptr-deref in range
    [0x0000000000000008-0x000000000000000f]
    CPU: 0 PID: 100 Comm: cifsd
    RIP: smb2_is_valid_oplock_break+0xc8/0x2270 [cifs]
    cifs_demultiplex_thread
    Kernel panic - not syncing: Fatal exception

Return -1 when inline decrypt finds no mid, and skip
is_oplock_break() plus the unknown-frame dump when bufs[i]
is NULL. receive_encrypted_standard() already assigns
bufs[*num_mids].

items.title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ocfs2: pin owning modules for open debugfs files Th…
items.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ocfs2: pin owning modules for open debugfs files

The OCFS2 debugfs file operation tables do not set owner. The
full debugfs proxy obtains real_fops with fops_get() at open and
keeps it until final release. Without an owner, this does not acquire
a reference to the module containing the table and its callbacks.
Removing the debugfs entries does not drain retained open files.

An open connected_nodes file can therefore outlive ocfs2_nodemanager
and make full_proxy_release() read real_fops->release from freed
module memory. Heming also reproduced the issue with fs_state and
asked for the other OCFS2 debugfs operation tables to be checked.

Set owner to THIS_MODULE in all eleven explicit debugfs operation
tables: five in ocfs2_nodemanager, four in ocfs2_dlm, and two in
ocfs2. The existing debugfs get/put pair then holds the appropriate
module until final release. Leave the open, read and release callbacks
unchanged. The blockcheck table already sets owner through
DEFINE_DEBUGFS_ATTRIBUTE(), so it needs no change.

The original controlled test used an unloadable OCFS2 module and
case-local probe filters without changing the candidate open, unload
or release logic. Closing a retained connected_nodes file after
normal unload produced:

  BUG: unable to handle page fault for address: fffffbfff804cfef
  Oops: Oops: 0000 [#1] SMP KASAN NOPTI
  RIP: 0010:full_proxy_release+0xbf/0x190
  Call Trace:
   <TASK>
   __fput+0x39a/0xa60
   fput_close_sync+0xff/0x200
   __x64_sys_close+0x8c/0xf0
   do_syscall_64+0x114/0x620
   entry_SYSCALL_64_after_hwframe+0x77/0x7f
   </TASK>
  Modules linked in: [last unloaded: ocfs2_nodemanager]

items.title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ocfs2: drain quorum work before removing the cluste…
items.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ocfs2: drain quorum work before removing the cluster

The configured cluster must remain available until an in-flight quorum
decision has finished using its fencing method.  o2quo_make_decision()
drops qs_lock before calling o2quo_fence_self(), which marks heartbeat
regions for unclean stop and then reads
o2nm_single_cluster->cl_fence_method.  Cluster removal clears the
singleton without waiting for this independent system-workqueue item.

When a failed-quorum decision overlaps removal of the heartbeat regions,
nodes and cluster through configfs, the worker can be preempted after
marking the regions and resume after the singleton has been cleared:

  Quorum worker                     Configfs removal
  select fence; drop qs_lock
  o2hb_stop_all_regions()
                                    remove regions; join heartbeat threads
                                    remove nodes; stop o2net
                                    clear singleton; release cluster
  read cl_fence_method

The resumed read dereferences NULL instead of applying the configured
fencing method. The heartbeat thread's dependency protects the local
node only until the thread exits, and draining o2net does not wait for
qs_work.

Add o2quo_flush_work() to drain pending or running quorum decisions
before clearing the singleton in o2nm_cluster_group_drop_item(). By
this point the heartbeat regions and nodes have been removed, so their
work publishers are stopped. The worker can finish while the cluster
and its configured fencing method remain available. It does not acquire
the configfs mutex held by the removal path.

Keep o2quo_exit() as the counterpart of o2quo_init() for module teardown
and initialization failure, and have it call the same drain helper.
Cluster removal uses only the explicitly named drain operation.

KASAN report as below:

    Oops: general protection fault, probably for non-canonical address 0xdffffc000000011b: 0000 [#1] SMP KASAN NOPTI
    KASAN: null-ptr-deref in range [0x00000000000008d8-0x00000000000008df]
    CPU: 0 UID: 0 PID: 72 Comm: kworker/0:2 Not tainted 7.3.0-rc4-next-20260921-pmb-ocfs2-functional-v1+ #1 PREEMPT(lazy)
    Hardware name: QEMU Ubuntu 24.04 PC v2 (i440FX + PIIX, arch_caps fix, 1996), BIOS 1.16.3-debian-1.16.3-2 04/01/2014
    Workqueue: events o2quo_make_decision
    RIP: 0010:o2quo_fence_self+0x65/0x200

Register dump omitted.

    Call Trace:
     <TASK>
     o2quo_make_decision+0x345/0x3a0
     ? __pfx_o2quo_make_decision+0x10/0x10
     ? process_one_work+0x834/0x1b40
     ? srso_alias_return_thunk+0x5/0xfbef5
     ? lock_release+0xc8/0x290
     ? srso_alias_return_thunk+0x5/0xfbef5
     process_one_work+0x9a8/0x1b40
     ? __pfx_process_one_work+0x10/0x10
     ? lock_acquire+0x190/0x300
     ? lock_is_held_type+0x8f/0x100
     ? srso_alias_return_thunk+0x5/0xfbef5
     worker_thread+0x65c/0xe40
     ? srso_alias_return_thunk+0x5/0xfbef5
     ? __kthread_parkme+0x177/0x220
     ? srso_alias_return_thunk+0x5/0xfbef5
     ? __pfx_worker_thread+0x10/0x10
     kthread+0x351/0x460
     ? srso_alias_return_thunk+0x5/0xfbef5
     ? __pfx_kthread+0x10/0x10
     ret_from_fork+0x659/0x940
     ? __pfx_ret_from_fork+0x10/0x10
     ? srso_alias_return_thunk+0x5/0xfbef5
     ? __switch_to+0x74f/0xf70
     ? __pfx_kthread+0x10/0x10
