items.title: bt_att_find_req_by_user_data() in subsys/bluetooth/host/att.c walks every ATT channel attached to a connection and dere…
items.description:
bt_att_find_req_by_user_data() in subsys/bluetooth/host/att.c walks every ATT channel attached to a connection and dereferences chan->req->user_data without checking chan->req. An ATT channel with no client request in flight holds chan->req == NULL — that is its normal idle state, set by att_handle_rsp() when a response resolves the transaction and tested by att_req_send_process() to pick a free channel — so the lookup reads through a NULL pointer as soon as it visits an idle channel. Every other chan->req user in the file already guards the pointer.

The lookup is reached from the public bt_gatt_cancel() API and, more importantly, from the host itself: bt_gatt_unsubscribe() calls bt_gatt_cancel() while a subscribe CCC write is still outstanding (BT_GATT_SUBSCRIBE_FLAG_WRITE_PENDING), and call_notify_cb_and_maybe_unsubscribe() in subsys/bluetooth/host/gatt.c invokes bt_gatt_unsubscribe() from the RX path whenever an application notify callback returns BT_GATT_ITER_STOP. A malicious or malfunctioning peer can hold the trigger window open by withholding the ATT Write Response to the CCC write and then sending a notification for the subscribed handle. With CONFIG_BT_EATT the traversal is very likely to meet an idle sibling channel, since ATT channels are prepended to the list and a channel opened after the pending request was sent is visited first.

The dereference is a read of a small constant offset from address zero, so the impact is availability only: no memory corruption, no attacker-chosen address and no information disclosure. On platforms and configurations where a near-NULL read traps — TrustZone non-secure images, MMU targets, native_sim, or builds with CONFIG_NULL_POINTER_EXCEPTION_DETECTION_MPU/_DWT — the fault occurs in the Bluetooth RX context and results in a fatal error and device reset. On a plain Cortex-M build with the vector table mapped at address 0 and null-pointer detection disabled (the default) the read succeeds and the defect is inert.

The fix adds an explicit chan->req != NULL test to the channel traversal and additionally rejects a NULL user_data argument, which would otherwise have matched, and cancelled, an unrelated request.

items.title: The Zephyr WebSocket client validates the server's handshake response in on_header_value() in subsys/net/lib/websocket/…
items.description:
The Zephyr WebSocket client validates the server's handshake response in on_header_value() in subsys/net/lib/websocket/websocket.c. The comparison was performed as strncmp(at, str, length), where length is the length of the value the server sent rather than the length of the expected value, so the check only asked whether the received value was a prefix of the expected base64(SHA-1(key || GUID)). A server that returned a handful of correct characters passed, and a response carrying an empty Sec-WebSocket-Accept: header caused strncmp() to be called with a count of zero, which returns 0 and set ctx->sec_accept_ok with no comparison performed at all. The header-value callback also cleared ctx->sec_accept_present after the first chunk, so a value split across receive-buffer boundaries was only ever examined in part.

ctx->sec_accept_ok is the sole WebSocket-specific gate in websocket_connect(); the client does not check the HTTP status code or the Upgrade:/Connection: headers. Any HTTP response containing an empty or prefix-matching Sec-WebSocket-Accept header therefore completed the handshake, after which the socket is finalized as a WebSocket and all further peer bytes are parsed as frames. The affected path is driven directly by remote input through subsys/net/lib/http/http_parser.c, and is reached by every user of websocket_connect(), including MQTT over WebSocket (subsys/net/lib/mqtt/mqtt_transport_websocket.c) and subsys/net/lib/ocpp/ocpp.c.

The Sec-WebSocket-Accept exchange is not a secret-based authentication -- an endpoint or on-path attacker that sees the request can compute the expected value -- so the impact is bounded to parties that never observed the handshake request: a caching or transparent intermediary replaying a canned response, an off-path attacker injecting a spoofed response, or a non-WebSocket endpoint the client was induced to talk to. For those, the per-connection binding that RFC 6455 requires the client to enforce provided no protection at all, letting a single crafted response convince the device it holds a live WebSocket session and causing it to send application data to, and accept frames from, an unverified peer. There is no memory-safety consequence.

The fix compares each delivered chunk against the expected value at the position reached so far, refuses a chunk that would overrun it, and accepts only once every byte of the expected value -- and no more -- has been matched; on_header_field() now also clears the flag for any other header so a partial value cannot be continued across an intervening header.

items.title: The Bluetooth Classic SDP server in subsys/bluetooth/host/classic/sdp.c allocated every response PDU through bt_sdp_cre…
items.description:
The Bluetooth Classic SDP server in subsys/bluetooth/host/classic/sdp.c allocated every response PDU through bt_sdp_create_pdu(), which expands to bt_l2cap_create_pdu() and therefore uses a K_FOREVER timeout. The allocation is made from sdp_pool, a fixed pool holding only CONFIG_BT_MAX_CONN buffers (one in the default configuration) that is shared with the SDP client role. When the pool is empty the call blocks without a bound.

The allocation is reached from bt_sdp_recv() on the Bluetooth host's RX context: the bt_workq "BT RX WQ" workqueue in the default configuration since v3.1.0, and the dedicated "BT RX" thread before that. This context processes all normal-priority HCI events and all received ACL data. The SDP L2CAP server is registered on PSM 0x0001 with no security requirement (BT_SECURITY_L0), so an unpaired, unauthenticated BR/EDR peer within radio range of a connectable device can drive it. Every malformed or unrecognised SDP PDU reaches send_err_rsp(), and the sdp_svc_search_req(), sdp_svc_att_req() and sdp_svc_search_att_req() handlers allocate as well, so a short burst of pipelined requests drains the pool and parks the RX context in the blocking allocation.

A pool buffer is released only once its response has been sent, and a peer that withholds baseband acknowledgements keeps the controller's buffers for the link full, so the response is never sent. While the RX context is blocked, the entire Bluetooth host, for all connections and both LE and BR/EDR, stops processing normal-priority HCI events and received data. In most affected releases the stall is permanent. Queued PDUs are freed only by connection or channel teardown, which waits for the normal-priority Disconnection Complete handler, and that handler runs on the blocked RX context, so the host does not recover without a reset. In v3.7.0 through v4.1.x the TX processor discards the queued response once the link supervision timeout drops the connection, so each stall ends at that timeout, but the peer can reconnect and repeat it for as long as it stays in range. The impact is limited to availability; no memory corruption or information disclosure is involved.

The fix adds sdp_svc_create_pdu() using K_NO_WAIT, pre-allocates the response buffer once in bt_sdp_recv(), stashes the request in sdp->recv_pending when no buffer is available, and retries it from a work handler once a buffer is freed by the pool destroy callback.

items.title: The Virtual L2 receive handler virtual_recv() in subsys/net/l2/virtual/virtual.c ends with a fall-through path meant fo…
items.description:
The Virtual L2 receive handler virtual_recv() in subsys/net/l2/virtual/virtual.c ends with a fall-through path meant for a virtual interface that has nothing attached below it: it takes net_if_get_device(iface)->api, treats it as a struct virtual_interface_api, and calls api->recv(iface, pkt). That handler is however also invoked with a non-virtual interface: ethernet_recv() in subsys/net/l2/ethernet/ethernet.c deliberately passes the Ethernet interface so that a tagged frame can be dispatched over the VLAN interfaces attached to it. For an Ethernet interface dev->api is a struct ethernet_api, whose layout only shares the leading struct net_if_api, so the slot read as recv is actually get_config() (default) or get_capabilities() (when CONFIG_NET_STATISTICS_ETHERNET is enabled).

The fall-through is reached whenever no attached virtual interface claims the frame - most simply when the VLAN interface owning the frame's tag exists but is administratively down, since net_eth_get_vlan_iface() resolves the tag without checking link state while virtual_recv() skips interfaces that are not up. Any host able to place an 802.1Q-tagged Ethernet frame on the same link can then trigger the mistyped indirect call; no authentication, IP reachability or user interaction is required, because the frame is consumed at L2 before any address check.

The resulting call passes a struct net_if  where the driver expects a struct device  and a struct net_pkt  where it expects a struct net_if , with the callee's remaining parameters left as whatever the call site happens to leave in the argument registers. Driver implementations dereference these values: get_capabilities() typically reads dev->config/dev->data (a wild read through a non-pointer field of struct net_if), and get_config() implementations write through the uninitialized struct ethernet_config * argument. The practical impact is undefined behaviour in the network RX path - crashes and uncontrolled memory corruption - plus mis-handling of the packet when a capability bitmask is returned as a net_verdict. The attacker controls neither the corrupted address nor the value written, so this is a denial-of-service and memory-corruption issue rather than a controllable write primitive.

The same defective fall-through is reachable through any_recv() in subsys/net/l2/dummy/any/any.c, which passes a dummy interface whose struct dummy_api is shorter than the offset read, producing an out-of-bounds read of the driver's API object followed by an indirect call. The fix drops any packet whose interface is not a Virtual L2 interface, closing both entry points.

items.title: The Bluetooth Classic SDP client built its outgoing request PDUs with bt_sdp_create_pdu(), which allocates from the sdp…
items.description:
The Bluetooth Classic SDP client built its outgoing request PDUs with bt_sdp_create_pdu(), which allocates from the sdp_pool net-buf pool with a K_FOREVER timeout and no failure handling, in sdp_client_ss_search(), sdp_client_sa_search() and sdp_client_ssa_search() in subsys/bluetooth/host/classic/sdp.c. All of these run on the Bluetooth workqueue bt_workq (via sdp_client_work_handler(), the L2CAP sdp_client_connected() callback, or the continuation-state follow-up from a received response), which is the same single thread that dispatches incoming HCI ACL and event traffic, drives L2CAP, and performs connection and channel teardown. sdp_pool holds only CONFIG_BT_MAX_CONN buffers (one by default) and is shared with the SDP server role.

An unauthenticated peer within BR/EDR range can drive both halves of the trigger. The SDP L2CAP server is registered at BT_SECURITY_L0, so any inbound SDP request makes the device allocate the pool's buffer for a response, which is held until the controller has transmitted it. The same peer can then cause a client request to be issued while the pool is empty: in-tree profiles start SDP discovery from inbound connection callbacks (for example hfp_hf_accept() calls bt_sdp_discover() through hfp_hf_create(), and hfp_ag.c mirrors this), and a peer acting as an SDP server can force repeated client requests by answering with partial responses carrying continuation state.

With the pool empty, the allocation blocks uninterruptibly and freezes the entire Bluetooth host. The stall becomes permanent when the release of the outstanding buffer itself depends on the blocked workqueue: if the link carrying the queued PDU is dropped or stalls, hci_disconn_complete() and the L2CAP channel cleanup that purges the channel TX queue are themselves bt_workq work items, so the buffer is never returned. The result is an unrecoverable denial of service of all Bluetooth functionality until reboot; there is no memory-safety, confidentiality or integrity impact.

The fix allocates client PDUs with K_NO_WAIT via a new sdp_client_create_pdu(), propagates -ENOBUFS, parks the session on a new SDP_CLIENT_FLAG_WAIT_FOR_TX_BUF flag, and adds an sdp_pool destructor that re-submits the SDP client worker when a buffer becomes available. Note that the SDP server role still allocated from the same pool with K_FOREVER at this commit; that path was addressed separately.

items.title: The ITE IT8xxx2 SHI host-command backend in subsys/mgmt/ec_host_cmd/backends/ec_host_cmd_backend_shi_ite.c arms the SPI…
items.description:
The ITE IT8xxx2 SHI host-command backend in subsys/mgmt/ec_host_cmd/backends/ec_host_cmd_backend_shi_ite.c arms the SPI peripheral before its receive context exists. shi_ite_init_registers() sets the state machine to SHI_STATE_READY_TO_RECV and calls irq_enable() while the device initializes at POST_KERNEL priority CONFIG_KERNEL_INIT_PRIORITY_DEFAULT (40), but data->rx_ctx and data->tx are only assigned later by shi_ite_backend_init(), which ec_host_cmd_init() invokes at CONFIG_EC_HOST_CMD_INIT_PRIORITY (default 80).

If the attached host processor starts a SPI transaction inside that window, the Rx-valid-length interrupt fires, shi_ite_int_handler() passes its state check and calls shi_ite_parse_header(), which stores the host-derived request length through the still-NULL data->rx_ctx. On the IT8xxx2 low addresses are not backed by RAM, and with CONFIG_NULL_POINTER_EXCEPTION_DETECTION_PMP the first bytes of the address space are explicitly made inaccessible, so the store raises a fatal access fault in interrupt context. The window widens further when CONFIG_EC_HOST_CMD_INITIALIZE_AT_BOOT is disabled and the application calls ec_host_cmd_init() itself.

The result is a kernel panic on the embedded controller: with Zephyr's default fatal handler the CPU halts, so the controller stops servicing host commands until a hardware reset. Because the trigger is traffic from the attached host processor -- an untrusted peer from the controller firmware's point of view -- software on that host can provoke the fault by forcing a controller reset and issuing transactions during the reboot, turning a recoverable reset into a persistent outage. Impact is limited to availability: the faulting address is fixed and not attacker-chosen, so no memory-corruption primitive follows.

The fix leaves the interface at SHI_STATE_DISABLED with the interrupt masked during device init, moves irq_enable() into shi_ite_backend_init() after the buffers are published, and makes shi_ite_int_handler() reject a NULL data->rx_ctx while write-clearing IT83XX_SPI_ISR and IT83XX_SPI_RX_VLISR so that an unexpected early interrupt cannot storm.

items.title: The websocket client's HTTP header callback on_header_value() in subsys/net/lib/websocket/websocket.c receives the Sec-…
items.description:
The websocket client's HTTP header callback on_header_value() in subsys/net/lib/websocket/websocket.c receives the Sec-WebSocket-Accept header value as a pointer/length pair from the HTTP parser. The referenced bytes live inside the application-supplied receive buffer and are not NUL terminated. When the received value did not match the expected accept key, the pointer was passed directly to a %s conversion in a NET_DBG() call, so the logging code measured the string with strlen() and read on past the end of the header value looking for a terminator.

The value is supplied by the peer during the WebSocket handshake, before any application-level authentication, so a malicious or man-in-the-middle server reached over a ws:// (or otherwise attacker-terminated) connection can trigger the mismatch branch at will simply by answering with a wrong accept key. By sizing the response so the header value ends at the tail of the buffer passed to websocket_connect() as wreq->tmp_buf, the peer can make the scan run off the end of that buffer and into adjacent memory. The defective log statement is compiled in only when websocket debug logging is enabled (CONFIG_NET_WEBSOCKET_LOG_LEVEL_DBG=y, or CONFIG_LOG_DEFAULT_LEVEL=4); it is absent from a default build, which bounds exposure to diagnostic configurations.

The consequence is an out-of-bounds read whose contents are emitted to the log stream: memory adjacent to the receive buffer is disclosed wherever the device's logs are collected or displayed. On targets where the memory following the buffer is not mapped, the scan can instead fault and terminate the connection or thread. No out-of-bounds write occurs, so there is no integrity impact.

The fix copies at most sizeof(got) - 1 bytes of the parser-provided slice into a bounded stack buffer, NUL terminates the copy, and logs that instead, so the formatter never reads beyond the bytes the parser actually offered.

items.title: The Synopsys DesignWare I3C controller driver (drivers/i3c/i3c_dw.c) tracks free Device Address Table (DAT) slots with…
items.description:
The Synopsys DesignWare I3C controller driver (drivers/i3c/i3c_dw.c) tracks free Device Address Table (DAT) slots with get_free_pos(), which signals an exhausted table by returning -1. The helper declared its return type as uint8_t, so the sentinel was truncated to 255, and both consumers (dw_i3c_attach_device() and dw_i3c_i2c_attach_device()) also stored it in a uint8_t before testing if (pos < 0) — a comparison that is never true for an unsigned value. The exhaustion guard was therefore inert in every build.

With the guard defeated, an attach attempted on a full DAT proceeds with pos == 255: it writes data->dw_i3c_i2c_priv_data[255].id, more than 200 bytes past the end of the 32-element dw_i3c_i2c_priv_data array and past the end of struct dw_i3c_data; it stores the resulting out-of-bounds address in desc->controller_priv, from which later detach, reattach and IBI operations read the slot index back; and it performs a 32-bit MMIO store 1020 bytes beyond the hardware DAT base, outside the table the controller reports. The attach still returns success, so the upper layer believes the device is bound.

The DAT is smaller than the software array (its depth is read from DEVICE_ADDR_TABLE_POINTER, commonly 8 or 16 entries), so exhaustion is reachable. In a dual-role build (CONFIG_I3C_DUAL_ROLE with CONFIG_I3C_USE_IBI) acting as a secondary controller, the attach count is supplied by the bus's active controller: i3c_sec_handoffed() attaches one device per entry of the received DEFTGTS list, so a hostile or malfunctioning controller on the local I3C bus that declares more targets than the local DAT depth triggers the condition once per surplus entry. Exhaustion can also be reached from a devicetree that declares more devices than the table holds, or by repeated i3c attach shell commands.

Impact is bounded: the out-of-bounds store is a single byte of fixed value at a fixed displacement, with no attacker-chosen data or offset, so the realistic outcomes are corruption of neighbouring static driver state, writes into reserved controller registers, and inconsistent driver bookkeeping (a crash or a wedged I3C bus) rather than a controllable memory-write primitive. The attack vector is the local chip-to-chip I3C bus; there is no network-reachable path.

items.title: code-review-mcp-server: Command injection via unsanitized folderPath/baseBranch parameters
items.description: code-review-mcp-server automates code review and can post comments directly on GitHub pull requests. Prior to 1.5.3, the getLocalGitDiff, codeReview, createPR, and getPRTemplate MCP tools accept caller-controlled folderPath and baseBranch string parameters that are interpolated into command strings executed by child_process.execSync through /bin/sh. Shell metacharacters, command substitution, or quote-breaking input can therefore execute arbitrary commands with the privileges of the host process running the MCP server. This issue is fixed in version 1.5.3.

items.title: The Coder VS Code extension opens Coder workspaces in VS Code with a single click.
items.description: The Coder VS Code extension opens Coder workspaces in VS Code with a single click. From 0.1.20 until 1.14.6, a malicious repository can provide .vscode/settings.json values for security-sensitive Coder settings because the extension permits workspace and folder scope to override those settings. Values such as coder.headerCommand and coder.tlsCertRefreshCommand are later executed as shell commands, while other affected settings can redirect the Coder CLI binary or download source, inject CLI or SSH flags, replace TLS material, disable TLS verification, or change identity and credential-storage behavior. A victim with the extension installed must open the malicious workspace or repository; when the extension activates, attacker-controlled commands can run with the victim user's privileges. The issue also affects untrusted workspaces because the extension declares untrusted-workspace support without preventing consumption of the workspace-controlled settings. This issue is fixed in version 1.14.6.

items.title: django-tenants 3.4.8 before 4.0.1 contains an SQL injection vulnerability in its PostgreSQL backend that allows attacke…
items.description: django-tenants 3.4.8 before 4.0.1 contains an SQL injection vulnerability in its PostgreSQL backend that allows attackers to inject SQL through unescaped tenant schema names. Attackers who can choose or influence a schema name can supply quote characters that are interpolated into SET search_path and CREATE, DROP or ALTER SCHEMA statements, letting them read other tenants' data or run SQL as the application's database user.

items.title: In Open Object Rexx (ooRexx) before 5.2.0, RXAPI has a heap buffer over-read in a QueueManager DataQueue::addmethod.
items.description: In Open Object Rexx (ooRexx) before 5.2.0, RXAPI has a heap buffer over-read in a QueueManager DataQueue::addmethod. In particular, the code blindly trusts the message.parameter1 value provided by the client as the size used to fill the data from the queueData heap buffer. An attacker sends a large parameter1 value in an ADD_TO_SESSION_QUEUE or ADD_TO_NAMED_QUEUE message and then retrieves data with a PULL_FROM_SESSION_QUEUE message. (A very large value causes a process crash.)

items.title: BookStack before 26.09.2 contains an uncontrolled resource consumption vulnerability in the ZIP content importer that a…
items.description: BookStack before 26.09.2 contains an uncontrolled resource consumption vulnerability in the ZIP content importer that allows authenticated users with the Import Content permission to exhaust server storage. Attackers can upload a small ZIP whose data.json references one bundled file many times, causing ZipImportRunner::importAttachment() to write a full copy per reference.

items.title: Chyrp Lite (xenocrat/chyrp-lite) contains a missing brute-force protection vulnerability in the main_login() function t…
items.description: Chyrp Lite (xenocrat/chyrp-lite) contains a missing brute-force protection vulnerability in the main_login() function that allows remote attackers to repeatedly submit login attempts against the admin account without any attempt counter, lockout, delay, or CAPTCHA enforcement. Attackers can send unlimited password guesses via POST requests to the login action until a correct credential is found, gaining full administrative control including post publishing, user management, and file uploads.

items.title: B3log Solo through 4.4.0 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to obta…
items.description: B3log Solo through 4.4.0 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to obtain article view passwords by querying the public GET /articles API. The ArticleProcessor.getArticlesByPage handler leaves the articleViewPwd property in JSON responses, letting attackers read passwords for encrypted articles and access their protected content.

items.title: B3log Solo through 4.4.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in B3Receiver.receiveArticle that allows visito…
items.description: B3log Solo through 4.4.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in B3Receiver.receiveArticle that allows visitor accounts to modify any article via the POST /apis/symphony/article endpoint. Attackers can supply their username as userB3Key, since OAuth-created visitors receive it as their B3 key, and overwrite any article's title, content and tags.

items.title: B3log Solo through 4.4.0 contains an SQL injection vulnerability in the console article update API that allows authenti…
items.description: B3log Solo through 4.4.0 contains an SQL injection vulnerability in the console article update API that allows authenticated authors to inject SQL through unvalidated JSON property names. Attackers can send a PUT request to /console/article/ with crafted property names used as UPDATE column names, then read query results back through the updated article.

items.title: crw-server before 0.45.1 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to…
items.description: crw-server before 0.45.1 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to reach internal services by supplying an unvalidated baseUrl to the /v1/scrape endpoint. Attackers can set llmApiKey and request the summary format, making the server POST to loopback or private addresses and use returned warnings as a reachability oracle.

items.title: crw-server before 0.45.1 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to…
items.description: crw-server before 0.45.1 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to reach internal hosts via caller-controlled proxy and proxy_list fields in /v1/scrape. Attackers can supply proxy entries pointing to loopback, private-network or link-local hosts, bypassing page URL checks to open HTTP-proxy or SOCKS connections internally.

items.title: B3log Solo through 4.4.0 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows attackers to inject script by…
items.description: B3log Solo through 4.4.0 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows attackers to inject script by setting a malicious article title rendered without escaping. Attackers can set titles, including via the B3 sync endpoint, so admin/article-pwd.ftl, skin templates, and js/page.js article lists execute script in visitors' and administrators' browsers.

items.title: Ghost by muneeb141 on the main branch from commit c731cdf through commit 672dfec contains an authentication bypass vuln…
items.description: Ghost by muneeb141 on the main branch from commit c731cdf through commit 672dfec contains an authentication bypass vulnerability in the whitelisted ghost.api.ghost.convert_to_real_user method that allows unauthenticated attackers to skip OTP verification by setting the client-supplied bypass_otp parameter. Attackers can obtain a ghost session from the guest-accessible create_ghost_session endpoint, then call convert_to_real_user with an arbitrary real_email and bypass_otp=1 to receive OAuth tokens for existing accounts and take them over.

items.title: TridotsTech go1cms master branch through commit 7f68d05 and version-3 branch before commit ead8da3 contains a missing a…
items.description: TridotsTech go1cms master branch through commit 7f68d05 and version-3 branch before commit ead8da3 contains a missing authentication vulnerability in the guest-whitelisted update_doc method that allows unauthenticated attackers to modify any document. Attackers can supply a doctype, name and arbitrary fields that are saved with ignore_permissions=True, altering User records to escalate privileges, take over accounts or tamper with business data.

items.title: Cloud Commander (cloudcmd) before 19.21.4 contains an authentication bypass and path traversal vulnerability that allow…
items.description: Cloud Commander (cloudcmd) before 19.21.4 contains an authentication bypass and path traversal vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to rename files by sending PUT /rename requests handled before authentication middleware. Attackers can supply absolute or ../ paths in the from and to arrays to move any file the Node.js process can access outside the configured root, causing data loss or denial of service.

items.title: free5GC WebConsole through 1.4.6 contains an authorization flaw in the ChangePasswordInfo handler that allows authentic…
items.description: free5GC WebConsole through 1.4.6 contains an authorization flaw in the ChangePasswordInfo handler that allows authenticated tenant users to change other members' passwords. Attackers can send POST /api/change-password with another tenant member's email and a new password, without the current password, to take over that account.

items.title: CBoard before commit 7bd8180 contains a missing authorization vulnerability that allows any authenticated user to reach…
items.description: CBoard before commit 7bd8180 contains a missing authorization vulnerability that allows any authenticated user to reach admin functions because AdminController and DashboardController methods bypass AOP role checks. Attackers with no role grants can call deleteUser, deleteRole, getUserList, getAllWidgetList and getAllDatasetList to read query configurations and delete accounts including the administrator.

items.title: Frappe Framework before 15.123.0 and 16.x before 16.50.0 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability in the fr…
items.description: Frappe Framework before 15.123.0 and 16.x before 16.50.0 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability in the frappe.email.email_body.get_email_html method, which lacks role checks. Authenticated users, including portal Website Users, can inject stylesheet link tags into unescaped email templates, causing Premailer to fetch internal or external hosts and return the content.

items.title: SplitPro through 2.1.6 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the addOrEditExpense and addOrEditCurrencyConv…
items.description: SplitPro through 2.1.6 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the addOrEditExpense and addOrEditCurrencyConversion tRPC mutations that allows authenticated users to assign expenses to arbitrary users. Attackers can enumerate sequential user IDs and supply them in participants or paidBy fields to fabricate debts on victims' balances, even in unseen groups.

items.title: 7-Zip File Manager before 26.03 fails to detect archive entry names padded with Unicode space characters, allowing atta…
items.description: 7-Zip File Manager before 26.03 fails to detect archive entry names padded with Unicode space characters, allowing attackers to bypass the deceptive file name warning in CPanel::IsVirus_Message. Attackers can craft archive entries like a PDF name followed by ideographic spaces and .hta to hide the real extension, executing script content via ShellExecuteExW when opened.

items.title: Alinto SOGo before 5.12.13 contains an SQL injection vulnerability in SQLSource contact lookup that allows authenticate…
items.description: Alinto SOGo before 5.12.13 contains an SQL injection vulnerability in SQLSource contact lookup that allows authenticated users to inject SQL by placing a backslash before a quote in the object name. Attackers can send requests under a SQL-backed address book path on MySQL or MariaDB to perform UNION or boolean-based reads of the user-source table, including password hashes.

items.title: GPAC before 26.07.0 contains a use-after-free vulnerability in the XMT scene loader that allows attackers to read freed…
items.description: GPAC before 26.07.0 contains a use-after-free vulnerability in the XMT scene loader that allows attackers to read freed heap memory via discarded nodes left on the parser node stack. Attackers can supply a crafted XMT scene file processed by MP4Box, causing xmt_text_content() to call gf_node_get_tag() on a freed node and crash the process.

items.title: GPAC before 26.07.0 contains a use-after-free vulnerability in gf_sg_command_del() that allows attackers to trigger rea…
items.description: GPAC before 26.07.0 contains a use-after-free vulnerability in gf_sg_command_del() that allows attackers to trigger reads of freed memory through aliased XMT-A SFCommandBuffer command ownership. Attackers can supply a crafted XMT scene file processed by MP4Box, causing commands freed during node destruction to be reaccessed during access unit cleanup, crashing the process.

items.title: msgpack-c through 7.0.2 contains a heap buffer overflow vulnerability in msgpack_vrefbuffer_migrate() in src/vrefbuffer…
items.description: msgpack-c through 7.0.2 contains a heap buffer overflow vulnerability in msgpack_vrefbuffer_migrate() in src/vrefbuffer.c that checks capacity against the source array's end pointer. When migrating between vrefbuffers of unequal size, the realloc is skipped and memcpy() writes iovec entries past the destination array, corrupting adjacent heap memory or crashing the application.

items.title: Umbraco CMS 17.0.0 before 17.7.1 and 18.0.0 before 18.2.1 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability in Management…
items.description: Umbraco CMS 17.0.0 before 17.7.1 and 18.0.0 before 18.2.1 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability in Management API document version endpoints that skip per-document ContentPermissionByResource checks. Authenticated back-office users restricted to a start node can list and read document versions outside their tree by GUID, exposing unpublished values and altering prevent-cleanup flags.

items.title: GPAC before 26.07.0 contains a double free vulnerability in gf_sg_sfcommand_del() that allows attackers to crash the pr…
items.description: GPAC before 26.07.0 contains a double free vulnerability in gf_sg_sfcommand_del() that allows attackers to crash the process via crafted XMT scenes. Attackers can supply a crafted XMT/MP4 file where a Conditional node's SFCommandBuffer references a command freed twice during scene teardown, causing MP4Box to crash.

items.title: GPAC before 26.07.0 contains a NULL pointer dereference vulnerability in gf_node_get_tag() that allows attackers to cra…
items.description: GPAC before 26.07.0 contains a NULL pointer dereference vulnerability in gf_node_get_tag() that allows attackers to crash the process via crafted XMT connect elements. Attackers can supply an XMT scene file whose connect element has a parent with no node, crashing MP4Box during processing and causing denial of service.

items.title: WPChat plugin for WordPress before 1.4.6 contains a broken access control vulnerability that allows unauthenticated rem…
items.description: WPChat plugin for WordPress before 1.4.6 contains a broken access control vulnerability that allows unauthenticated remote attackers to invoke the admin claim-offer action by reusing the publicly exposed wpchat_frontend nonce without any capability check. Attackers can call SmartSearchManagerService::claimOffer() via POST /wp-json/wpchat/v1/smart-search/claim-offer to register an attacker-controlled email against the site's domain using the site's stored api_token, corrupting the WPChat account and newsletter identity bound to the installation.

items.title: A vulnerability in Phison SSD controller firmwares (Phison E18; EIFM80.0, Phison E18; EIFK51.2) allows a local attacker…
items.description: A vulnerability in Phison SSD controller firmwares (Phison E18; EIFM80.0, Phison E18; EIFK51.2) allows a local attacker with administrative privileges to bypass the "Security Access" handshake by leveraging leaked RSA parameters found in vendor utility binaries. By successfully completing the authentication, an attacker can access vendor-specific commands that permit arbitrary memory read and write operations. Because the firmware's code regions lack protection, these primitives can be used to overwrite existing handlers and achieve volatile code execution on the SSD controller.

items.title: Docmost is open-source collaborative wiki and documentation software.
items.description: Docmost is open-source collaborative wiki and documentation software. Prior to 0.96.0, two concurrent role-demotion requests from a space admin or workspace owner can each pass the last-admin or last-owner count check before either update is committed because the validation and role update are not serialized in one transaction. The requests can therefore demote the final two space admins or workspace owners and leave the affected space without an admin or the workspace without an owner, preventing normal administrative recovery. This issue is fixed in version 0.96.0.

items.title: Wiki.js is an open source wiki app built on Node.js.
items.description: Wiki.js is an open source wiki app built on Node.js. Prior to 2.5.315, an authenticated account with only manage:users can use users.update to change the password of any local account, including the Root administrator and other accounts with manage:system, by omitting the optional groups argument, which is automatically allowed and bypasses destination-group authorization without checking the target's current privileges. The attacker can use users.disableTFA to clear the same target's tfaIsActive state and TFA secret without a target-privilege check, then authenticate with the replacement password. Supplying groups: [] to users.update can remove every group relationship from a selected administrator and leave the installation without a legitimate account holding manage:system. Additional administrators with IDs greater than 2 can also be deactivated or deleted. This issue is fixed in version 2.5.315.

items.title: Wiki.js is an open source wiki app built on Node.js.
items.description: Wiki.js is an open source wiki app built on Node.js. Prior to 2.5.315, an authenticated user with write:pages can store JavaScript expressions in the v-slot:tabs or v-slot:content attributes of page HTML because server/modules/rendering/html-security/renderer.js adds those executable Vue directives to DOMPurify's allowlist. The sanitized output is inserted as rendered page HTML and later compiled by the Vue 2 runtime compiler, so the expressions execute in the Wiki.js origin when another user views the page even when the author lacks write:scripts and administrative permissions. The script runs with the viewer's browser session and can read same-origin data, modify displayed content, present phishing content, or perform actions available to that viewer, including privileged GraphQL operations when a privileged user opens the page. This issue is fixed in version 2.5.315.

items.title: The Libreswan IKEv2 state machine did not verify that an IKE_INTERMEDIATE exchange was required to satisfy the addke= P…
items.description: The Libreswan IKEv2 state machine did not verify that an IKE_INTERMEDIATE exchange was required to satisfy the addke= PostQuantum algorithm component of the exchange. A connecting client could (maliciously or by implementation error) skip the IKE_INTERMEDIATE exchange and start an IKE_AUTH exchange prematurely. The result is as if the addke= option had not been specified, and such connections are only protected by the classic key exchange algorithm (such as P-256 or Curve25519), allowing "store now, decrypt later" attacks once a quantum computer becomes available. Only connections with the addke= keyword in the ike= and/or esp= configuration option are affected. PostQuantum Hybrid Key Exchange support was added in version 5.4.

items.title: The Libreswan pluto daemon dereferences a NULL pointer when a CERT payload is received with an empty PKCS#7 payload, ca…
items.description: The Libreswan pluto daemon dereferences a NULL pointer when a CERT payload is received with an empty PKCS#7 payload, causing the daemon to crash and restart. The NSS function SEC_PKCS7GetCertificateList() was used to check whether the content was empty, but this check did not trigger if the non-empty content of the PKCS#7 wrapped payload was an empty list. Continued triggering of this vulnerability can lead to a denial of service. Remote code execution is not possible. Authentication is not required to trigger this vulnerability.

items.description: GPAC before 26.02.0 contains a use of uninitialized memory vulnerability in stbl_AddCTS() that allows attackers to corrupt sample table data via crafted MP4 files. Attackers can supply an MP4 with out-of-order composition time offsets for MP4Box import, triggering invalid memory access in gf_list_get() and crashing the process.

items.description: OpenCTI is an open source platform for managing cyber threat intelligence knowledge and observables. Prior to 7.260706.0, the logsWorkerConfig GraphQL query is authorized with the broad CONNECTORAPI capability and returns Elasticsearch connection details including elasticsearch_username, elasticsearch_password, elasticsearch_api_key, the URL, index, proxy, and TLS-verification setting. A holder of any connector API bearer token can retrieve this credential material. If the returned credentials are valid and Elasticsearch is reachable, the caller can directly read, modify, or delete OpenCTI indices and audit history outside application-layer role, marking, organization, and audit controls, with the practical impact bounded by the credentials' privileges and network reachability. This issue is fixed in version 7.260706.0.

items.title: OpenCTI is an open source platform for managing cyber threat intelligence knowledge and observables.
items.description: OpenCTI is an open source platform for managing cyber threat intelligence knowledge and observables. Prior to 7.260701.0, the caseIncidentAdd, caseRfiAdd, and caseRftAdd GraphQL mutations require only authentication and do not require a capability check. An authenticated user with reader-level permissions can therefore create incident, request-for-information, and request-for-takedown case objects regardless of the user's assigned role, causing unauthorized changes to platform data. This issue is fixed in version 7.260701.0.

items.title: iSponsorBlockTV: SSRF via Malicious SSDP Response Spoofing in Local Device Discovery
items.description: iSponsorBlockTV is a SponsorBlock client for YouTube TV clients. Prior to 2.11.0, src/iSponsorBlockTV/dial_client.py trusts the SSDP LOCATION URL supplied by a local-network responder without validating its destination. During automatic discovery, this can cause an attacker-directed GET request and a constrained POST request to a path ending in /YouTube; the POST uses application-defined headers and an application-defined payload rather than attacker-selected request contents. The requests can reach internal services, but the detailed request behavior states that response data and errors are not returned to the attacker, making the demonstrated behavior blind SSRF with bounded integrity impact. This issue is fixed in version 2.11.0.

items.title: Mikochi is a minimalist file manager with streaming capabilities.
items.description: Mikochi is a minimalist file manager with streaming capabilities. Prior to 1.10.1, authenticated users of bare-metal instances configured with a non-default trailing-slash DATA_DIR can use the Move endpoint to supply traversal-containing source or destination paths. The affected path validation can resolve those paths outside the configured data directory, allowing files to be written beyond Mikochi's intended storage boundary. Docker deployments that confine the data directory to a mounted volume and configurations whose DATA_DIR lacks a trailing slash are not affected by the described attack. This issue is fixed in version 1.10.1.

items.title: OpenCTI is an open source platform for managing cyber threat intelligence knowledge and observables.
items.description: OpenCTI is an open source platform for managing cyber threat intelligence knowledge and observables. Prior to 7.260624.0, an Organization Administrator with VIRTUAL_ORGANIZATION_ADMIN and KNOWLEDGE_KNUPDATE can use organizationFieldPatch to replace the administered organization's grantable_groups without a SETTINGS_SETACCESSES authorization check. The administrator can add the built-in Administrators group to that grant scope and then bypass the grantable_groups guard added by the incomplete CVE-2026-44730 remediation to add their own account to Administrators. Membership grants the BYPASS capability after session cache refresh, escalating the tenant-scoped account to global administrator with access across organizations, users, settings, markings, connectors, and ingestion. This issue is fixed in version 7.260624.0.

Prior to 10.0.28, 11.0.10, and 12.0.1, authenticated users can craft a URL that invokes massive actions without all required object- and action-specific authorization checks. The bypass permits operations outside the user's granted rights, including unauthorized plugin activation, deactivation, and uninstallation for plugins already present on the filesystem and other state-changing maintenance actions. This issue is fixed in versions 10.0.28, 11.0.10, and 12.0.1.

This allows the technician to disable or take control of the higher-privileged user's two-factor authentication protection. This issue is fixed in versions 11.0.10 and 12.0.1.

To remediate this issue, users should upgrade to version 0.0.19 or later and rotate any InfluxDB API tokens configured for the server.

items.title: Phison E12 and E18 PCIe SSD controllers contain a Secure Boot bypass vulnerability that allows a privileged local attac…
items.description: Phison E12 and E18 PCIe SSD controllers contain a Secure Boot bypass vulnerability that allows a privileged local attacker to inject persistent boot-patch tuples into the unsigned, CRC-protected flash ID page read by the BootROM. By overwriting a fuse-derived RAM variable via a crafted patch entry using Phison Vendor Specific Commands, an attacker can force CRC-only firmware verification instead of signature checking, enabling an unsigned firmware image to load and creating a persistent controller-level implant that survives firmware reinstallation and operates below the host operating system.

items.title: OpenCTI is an open source platform for managing cyber threat intelligence knowledge and observables.
items.description: OpenCTI is an open source platform for managing cyber threat intelligence knowledge and observables. Prior to 7.260513.0, Draft Workspace identifiers are accepted without verifying that the authenticated user can access the referenced draft. Any authenticated user can enumerate draftWorkspaces, use a disclosed DRAFT_ID with draftWorkspaceEntities to read unpublished reports, descriptions, observables, and other staged intelligence, or place the identifier in the opencti-draft-id header and run mutations that inject entities and relationships into another user's private workspace. The flaw permits cross-user disclosure and tampering but does not cause a denial of service. This issue is fixed in version 7.260513.0.

items.title: CubeSandbox is an instant, concurrent, secure, and lightweight sandbox for AI agents.
items.description: CubeSandbox is an instant, concurrent, secure, and lightweight sandbox for AI agents. Prior to 0.5.1, any authenticated tenant permitted to call POST /sandboxes can supply metadata["host-mount"] with an arbitrary existing host path because the control plane performs no authorization check or allowed-prefix validation for the path. injectHostDirMounts forwards the path to prepareHostDirVolume, where Cubelet uses mount --rbind through the function to perform a recursive bind mount as root and exposes the host subtree to the tenant's MicroVM through virtio-fs, read-write by default. This allows host-root file access and modification, host code execution, access to the container runtime, and compromise of co-resident tenants without a kernel or virtual-machine-monitor flaw. This issue is fixed in version 0.5.1.

items.title: Model Context Protocol Python SDK: OAuth client could send credentials to an authorization server chosen by the MCP server
items.description: The Model Context Protocol Python SDK is the official Python SDK for Model Context Protocol servers and clients. From 1.9.1 until 1.30.0 and 2.2.0, OAuth client support in mcp.client.auth can send credentials to an authorization server chosen by an untrusted MCP server. ClientCredentialsOAuthProvider and PrivateKeyJWTOAuthProvider cannot identify the authorization server that owns their credentials. Affected HTTP clients using those providers, OAuthClientProvider, or the deprecated 1.x RFC7523OAuthClientProvider can disclose a client_secret, authorization code, PKCE code_verifier, or signed client assertion. MCP servers, stdio clients, and clients that attach their own tokens or headers are not affected. Interactive OAuthClientProvider use requires a person to start sign-in, while the unattended providers do not. For ClientCredentialsOAuthProvider and PrivateKeyJWTOAuthProvider, callers must configure issuer= after upgrading because omission still follows the MCP server's advertised authorization server, and the deprecated RFC7523OAuthClientProvider must be replaced because it has no issuer option. A stored client registration without an issuer remains unbound after upgrading, so stored OAuth client information must be cleared once to register again or a manually pre-registered record must be updated with its issuer. This issue is fixed in versions 1.30.0 and 2.2.0.

items.title: OpenCTI is an open source platform for managing cyber threat intelligence knowledge and observables.
items.description: OpenCTI is an open source platform for managing cyber threat intelligence knowledge and observables. Prior to 7.260722.0, the GraphQL endpoint accepts query operations over HTTP GET because CSRF prevention is disabled (csrfPrevention: false), placing the complete GraphQL query and its arguments in the request URL. Server and reverse-proxy logs, browser history, and shared caches can retain sensitive filters, marking-restricted identifiers, and investigation search arguments, allowing a person with access to those records to recover legitimate users' query contents. GraphQL mutations are not accepted over GET, and the issue does not permit code execution. This issue is fixed in version 7.260722.0.

items.title: Git is a fast, scalable, distributed revision control system with an unusually rich command set that provides both high…
items.description: Git is a fast, scalable, distributed revision control system with an unusually rich command set that provides both high-level operations and full access to internals. Prior to 2.50.2, 2.51.3, 2.52.1, 2.53.1, 2.54.1, 2.55.1, and 2.56.1, an attacker-controlled repository hosted by the attacker rather than on a normal forge site can exploit git clone --recurse-submodules by causing Git to overwrite a submodule gitfile with a symbolic link. The symbolic link can point to a directory containing attacker-controlled Git configuration or hooks, allowing those hooks or configuration to execute code on the cloning user's system. The issue requires the recursive-submodule option, and users should avoid cloning repositories from untrusted sources. This issue is fixed in versions 2.50.2, 2.51.3, 2.52.1, 2.53.1, 2.54.1, 2.55.1, and 2.56.1.

items.title: OpenCTI is an open source platform for managing cyber threat intelligence knowledge and observables.
items.description: OpenCTI is an open source platform for managing cyber threat intelligence knowledge and observables. Prior to 7.260428.0, the token GraphQL mutation used for primary login has no endpoint-specific rate limit, while the global Express limiter defaults to permitting 10,000 requests in a one-second window. An unauthenticated remote attacker can make password guesses at network speed against a chosen user account and, if a credential is recovered, access the account's threat-intelligence data and permitted operations. This issue is fixed in version 7.260428.0.

items.title: OpenCTI is an open source platform for managing cyber threat intelligence knowledge and observables.
items.description: OpenCTI is an open source platform for managing cyber threat intelligence knowledge and observables. In 7.260722.0 and earlier, a user with the SETTINGS_SETCUSTOMIZATION capability can configure a webhook notifier with an arbitrary destination URL and invoke notifierTest to make the OpenCTI server send the request immediately. The request can target internal services or cloud metadata endpoints that are reachable from the server, enabling server-side request forgery without waiting for a notifier event. No fixed release is verified by the available evidence; later releases remain unclassified.

A person who can access the profile response can recover the secret, enroll a duplicate authenticator, and generate valid one-time codes, undermining the account's second-factor protection. items.title: OpenCTI is an open source platform for managing cyber threat intelligence knowledge and observables.
items.description: OpenCTI is an open source platform for managing cyber threat intelligence knowledge and observables. Prior to 7.260416.0, public TAXII 2.1 collections configured with taxii_public set to true are served under the high-privilege SYSTEM_USER context rather than a restricted public-sharing user context. Unauthenticated requests can therefore bypass object markings, organization segregation, and authorized_members restrictions and retrieve restricted threat-intelligence objects that match the collection filters; a broad or absent filter can expose most of the database. Version 7.260416.0 remediates this issue for new configurations, but public-sharing configurations created before that version are not covered and are tracked separately in GHSA-25r9-q6rp-j7jw.

items.title: containerd image-triggered daemon crash via malformed digest in subject-annotated descriptor
items.description: containerd is an open-source container runtime. From 2.2.0 until 2.2.10, 2.3.7, and 2.4.2, image manifest processing through the transfer service can encounter a child descriptor containing the io.containerd.manifest.subject annotation and a malformed digest. Pulling or importing such an image, including through a default CRI PullImage request, can trigger an unrecovered panic and crash the containerd daemon. In Kubernetes, kubelet retries can repeatedly trigger the crash and disrupt container operations on the worker node. This issue is fixed in versions 2.2.10, 2.3.7, and 2.4.2.

items.title: Faust.js is a headless WordPress toolkit.
items.description: Faust.js is a headless WordPress toolkit. Prior to 1.8.12, the FaustWP generateAuthorizationCode GraphQL mutation called wp_authenticate_username_password and wp_authenticate_email_password directly instead of using wp_authenticate. This bypassed callbacks registered on WordPress's outer authenticate filter, including policies for multifactor authentication, single sign-on, IP allowlists, or disabled accounts. On a site using FaustWP local login and one of those policies, an attacker with a valid username or email and password could obtain an authorization code and exchange it through /api/faust/auth/token for access and refresh tokens even when the normal WordPress login path would deny access. This issue is fixed in version 1.8.12.

items.title: EGroupware: User-Controlled Identity Provider Selection in SAML Authentication
items.description: EGroupware is a web-based groupware server written in PHP. Prior to 23.1.20260601 and 26.6.20260616, login() in api/src/Auth/Saml.php accepts the unauthenticated idp request parameter when it merely begins with the HTTPS scheme and passes it to SimpleSAMLphp's requireAuth() without checking the configured trusted identity providers. A malicious actor can redirect the sign-in flow to an attacker-controlled identity provider, enabling credential phishing and, when the SimpleSAMLphp deployment does not strictly validate identity-provider metadata, forged SAML assertions as arbitrary users, including administrators. This issue is fixed in versions 23.1.20260601 and 26.6.20260616.

items.title: qbee-agent: Local Privilege Escalation and Arbitrary File Tampering via Symlink Following in createFile helper
items.description: qbee-agent is the device agent component of the qbee.io IoT device management platform. Prior to 2026.27, the privileged createFile helper followed attacker-controlled symbolic links during file creation. A local unprivileged user whose account is managed by the SSH Keys bundle could replace ~/.ssh with a link to /root/.ssh, causing the agent to write an authorized key for root. On systems using RAUC download mode with ineffective kernel symlink protection, the predictable /tmp/.bundle.raucb.part path could be linked to a system file and then overwritten or truncated during an update. A file-distribution destination beneath an attacker-controlled directory could similarly redirect the partial-download path so the agent changed ownership of a sensitive file. These vectors could result in root privilege escalation, arbitrary file modification, or denial of service. This issue is fixed in version 2026.27.

items.title: Phoenix: Format String Injection in applyChatTemplate
items.description: Phoenix is an AI observability and evaluation platform. From 13.0.0 until 15.7.0, the applyChatTemplate GraphQL query passed attacker-controlled F-string templates to FStringTemplateFormatter._format, while DotDict.__getattr__ did not prevent traversal through Python private attributes. A crafted field could traverse object internals such as __class__, __init__, and __globals__ to read process environment variables and internal module state. The endpoint is unauthenticated on default installations, and any account can reach it when authentication is enabled. Exposure of PHOENIX_SECRET can allow administrative session-token forgery and decryption of credentials protected by keys derived from that secret. This issue is fixed in version 15.7.0.

items.title: EGroupware is a web-based groupware server written in PHP.
items.description: EGroupware is a web-based groupware server written in PHP. Prior to 23.1.20260601 and 26.5.20260507, the processURL2InlineImages logic in api/src/Mail.php treats non-HTTP image sources in an HTML mail body as local paths and passes a decoded attacker-controlled file:// URI to file_get_contents. Any authenticated user with mail access can cause files readable by the web server process to be embedded as inline MIME attachments in outgoing email, exposing local configuration, credentials, private keys, or other server files. This issue is fixed in versions 23.1.20260601 and 26.5.20260507.

items.title: Guard Core: Quadratic ReDoS in built-in detection pattern freezes the event loop with a single request
items.description: Guard Core is an API security core engine for the FastAPI-Guard, FlaskAPI Guard, and DjAPI Guard adapters. From 3.5.0 until 3.13.0, built-in penetration-detection patterns in guard_core/handlers/suspatterns_handler.py execute through a direct pattern.search(content) call instead of the timeout-protected create_safe_matcher() path used for custom patterns. The built-in template-injection detector contains an unbounded expression with quadratic behavior when scanning repeated opening braces. Because penetration detection and enhanced mode are enabled by a stock SecurityConfig, an unauthenticated request can block the shared asyncio event loop, affecting all application endpoints. The triggering input does not produce a detection match, so the request can complete without incrementing ban counters or being recorded as suspicious. This issue is fixed in version 3.13.0.

items.title: Guard Core: Unvalidated X-Forwarded-For-derived string used as a Redis key component and interpolated into a KEYS glob pattern
items.description: Guard Core is an API security core engine for the FastAPI-Guard, FlaskAPI Guard, and DjAPI Guard adapters. From 1.0.0 until 3.13.0, _extract_from_forwarded_header() in guard_core/utils.py returns the selected X-Forwarded-For entry without validating that it is an IP address. In deployments configured with trusted_proxies where the selected entry is attacker-controlled, the arbitrary client_ip string reaches BehaviorTracker in guard_core/handlers/behavior_handler.py and is interpolated into Redis key names and blocking KEYS glob patterns. Glob metacharacters can cause one request to count other clients' behavior events, embedded separators can disturb key parsing, and rotating identities can create unbounded keys while repeatedly scanning the shared Redis keyspace. A non-IP identity can also reach a ban action and cause an uncaught validation error. This issue is fixed in version 3.13.0.

items.title: Guard Core: Whitespace-collapse preprocessing permanently disables the CRLF-anchored http-splitting and command-injection detectors in the default detection mode
items.description: Guard Core is an API security core engine for the FastAPI-Guard, FlaskAPI Guard, and DjAPI Guard adapters. From 1.0.0 until 3.13.0, ContentPreprocessor.preprocess() in guard_core/detection_engine/preprocessor.py collapses all whitespace before built-in pattern matching in the default enhanced mode. This removes carriage returns and newlines required by the http_split and newline-anchored cmd_injection detectors in guard_core/handlers/suspatterns_handler.py, making those detectors unable to match. Framework-decoded CRLF can therefore pass through Guard Core unflagged while the downstream application still receives the raw newline-bearing value. Direct security impact requires a downstream stack or application that persists or re-emits the value into a CRLF-tolerant response or command context. This issue is fixed in version 3.13.0.

items.description: VB-Audio VB-CABLE before 3.5.2.0 contains out-of-bounds read and write vulnerabilities in the vbaudio_cable64_win10.sys kernel streaming driver's KSPROPSETID_Audio MUTE, VOLUMELEVEL, and PEAKMETER2 property handlers that allow a local standard user to supply an all-channels sentinel value improperly used as a loop terminator or array index instead of being bounds-checked. Attackers can exploit the accessible low-integrity KS filter device object to write attacker-controlled values sequentially into kernel memory, corrupting kernel globals and object pointers, or read past an array boundary to leak kernel memory, resulting in local privilege escalation or denial of service via a kernel bug check.

items.title: CodeWhale: exec_shell parallel-readonly classifier auto-approves fd/rg/git grep exec flags enabling silent RCE
items.description: CodeWhale is a DeepSeek and MiMo coding agent for the terminal. Prior to 0.9.0, the ExecShellTool::approval_requirement_for path used is_parallel_readonly_command to downgrade commands to automatic approval based on a flag-stripped command allowlist. The allowlist treated fd, rg, and git grep as read-only even when fd -x or fd --exec, rg --pre, or git grep --open-files-in-pager selected an external program. registered_tool_approval_required returned without displaying a prompt for that automatic classification, and the later command-safety check also treated the base utilities as safe. Attacker-controlled content that influenced an agent tool call could therefore cause arbitrary program execution on the developer host without the approval promised by the default interactive profile, resulting in unauthorized access, modification, or disruption. This issue is fixed in version 0.9.0.

items.title: CodeWhale: Automation auto_approve defaults to true, bypassing the task-path hardening fix for silent recurring agent execution
items.description: CodeWhale is a DeepSeek and MiMo coding agent for the terminal. Prior to 0.9.0, DEFAULT_AUTOMATION_AUTO_APPROVE caused AutomationRecord::task_auto_approve to resolve an omitted setting to true, and the automation_create schema advertised the same insecure default. enqueue_run_task converted that omission into an explicit true value, bypassing the safer task-path fallback and selecting ApprovalMode::Bypass for each scheduled run. After a user approved creation of an apparently benign recurring automation, subsequent executions could silently authorize mutating tools without a human present, and an automation created with shell access could repeatedly execute commands. This issue is fixed in version 0.9.0.

items.title: In EDB Postgres Extended Server and EDB Postgres Advanced Server versions 15 through 18 with Transparent Data Encryptio…
items.description: In EDB Postgres Extended Server and EDB Postgres Advanced Server versions 15 through 18 with Transparent Data Encryption (TDE) enabled, the key used to encrypt temporary files was incompletely initialized. The code applied sizeof() to a pointer to the key buffer rather than to the buffer itself, so only 8 of the intended 32 bytes were filled from a secure random source and the remaining 24 bytes kept whatever was already in memory. This reduces the guaranteed randomness of the temporary-file key from 256 bits to 64 bits. Exploiting this requires local read access to the server's temporary-file directory, and those files normally exist only while the server is running; they persist only after a crash and are removed at the next server start. Permanent data files and WAL are not affected. The issue is fixed in EDB Postgres Extended Server 15.20, 16.16, 17.12 and 18.7 and EDB Postgres Advanced Server 15.20.0, 16.16.0, 17.12.0 and 18.7.0; the server must be restarted after upgrading.

items.title: eml_parser: Algorithmic-complexity DoS (O(n^4) regex backtracking) in Received-header parsing
items.description: eml_parser serves as a python module for parsing eml files and returning various information found in the e-mail as well as computed information. In 3.0.3 and earlier, eml_parser.routing.parserouting() in eml_parser/routing.py builds a regular expression with multiple greedy capture groups and appends the npdate date literal extracted from a normalized copy of an attacker-controlled Received header, then searches that expression against the original unnormalized line. A formatting difference can make the trailing literal impossible to match, causing exhaustive backtracking across the greedy groups at each start position. The unsliced Received-header path is invoked by decode_email, decode_email_bytes, and parse_email, so one small unauthenticated message can pin a parser worker and create sustained queue backlog. This issue is fixed in version 3.0.4.

items.title: Axigen Mail Server 10.3.3.67 through 10.3.3.x, 10.4.42 through 10.4.x, 10.5.29 through 10.5.x, 10.6.x before 10.6.41, a…
items.description: Axigen Mail Server 10.3.3.67 through 10.3.3.x, 10.4.42 through 10.4.x, 10.5.29 through 10.5.x, 10.6.x before 10.6.41, and 10.7.x before 10.7.3 contains an unauthenticated denial of service vulnerability caused by uncontrolled recursion when validating query parameter and cookie values with a recursive regular expression engine before authentication in the WebAdmin and WebMail services. Attackers can send a single HTTP request with a query parameter or cookie value of a few thousand characters to exhaust the worker thread stack and crash the server process, taking down SMTP, IMAP, POP3, and web services repeatedly.
