items.title: A security vulnerability has been detected in Moonshot AI Kimi Code up to 2.5.2.
items.description: A security vulnerability has been detected in Moonshot AI Kimi Code up to 2.5.2. This affects the function isOriginAllowed of the file apps/kimi-code/dist-web/assets/index-HU0LCM-X.js of the component Web UI. Such manipulation of the argument kimi_origin leads to open redirect. The attack can be executed remotely. The exploit has been disclosed publicly and may be used. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way.

items.title: A vulnerability was detected in Moonshot AI Kimi Code up to 2.0.2.
items.description: A vulnerability was detected in Moonshot AI Kimi Code up to 2.0.2. This vulnerability affects unknown code of the file .kimi-code/local.toml of the component WorkspaceDirsService. Performing a manipulation of the argument additional_dir results in reliance on untrusted inputs in a security decision. The attack requires a local approach. The exploit is now public and may be used. Upgrading to version 2.1.0 is able to resolve this issue. Upgrading the affected component is recommended.

items.title: A flaw was found in the Konflux UI proxy.
items.description: A flaw was found in the Konflux UI proxy. Hostname values defined in the KonfluxUI custom resource are inserted directly into proxy configuration files without adequate validation or sanitization. An authenticated user with permissions to modify the custom resource can inject malicious configuration directives to bypass authentication and authorization controls, potentially exposing internal backend services. In addition, providing malformed input can cause the configuration generator to fail, resulting in a denial of service (DoS) by preventing the proxy from starting.

items.title: fulgur converts untrusted HTML/CSS into PDF, commonly on a server that processes input supplied by many tenants.
items.description: fulgur converts untrusted HTML/CSS into PDF, commonly on a server that processes input supplied by many tenants. From version 0.15.0 to before version 0.27.0, resolving the CSS counters(name, sep) function in generated content was bounded neither in the size of a single expansion nor in the aggregate work across an element tree. An attacker able to submit HTML/CSS to a fulgur-based conversion service can trigger CPU and memory exhaustion with a trivially small payload, denying service to the host and any co-tenants. This issue has been patched in version 0.27.0.

items.title: fulgur converts untrusted HTML/CSS into PDF, commonly on a server that processes input supplied by many tenants.
items.description: fulgur converts untrusted HTML/CSS into PDF, commonly on a server that processes input supplied by many tenants. From version 0.4.4 to before version 0.29.0, the CSS string-set named-string values resolved from a document were accumulated per element with no memory budget, letting a small crafted document amplify into large retained memory (and the CPU to copy it) — results in a denial of service. This issue has been patched in version 0.29.0.

items.title: fulgur converts untrusted HTML/CSS into PDF, commonly on a server that processes input supplied by many tenants.
items.description: fulgur converts untrusted HTML/CSS into PDF, commonly on a server that processes input supplied by many tenants. From version 0.6.0 to before version 0.33.0, quadratic style-list reprocessing during containing-block resolution for absolutely-positioned pseudo-elements cause denial of service. This issue has been patched in version 0.33.0.

items.title: An internal security review identified a development regression from ThinkSystem v4 XClarity Controller 3 (XCC3) versio…
items.description: An internal security review identified a development regression from ThinkSystem v4 XClarity Controller 3 (XCC3) versions (2.51) IHX432Y to (2.56) IHX436K which re-introduces the default OpenBMC root password upon performing an XCC Reset to Default operation.  An attacker can gain access to enabled administrative interfaces of XCC using the default OpenBMC credential re-introduced after Reset to Default. Additionally, this provides access to the underlying XCC Operating System which is not normally accessible. Only these versions are affected and are no longer available for download. Process enhancements have also been made to prevent and identify potential future regression.

items.title: Paaster is a pastebin application.
items.description: Paaster is a pastebin application. Prior to version 3.3.0, Paaster's "view once" (burn-after-reading) paste mode can be bypassed with concurrent requests. The check that's supposed to enforce single-use is a plain read followed by a separate write, with no atomicity, so multiple simultaneous requests can all see the paste as "not yet read" and all successfully retrieve it. This issue has been patched in version 3.3.0.

items.title: Paaster is a pastebin application.
items.description: Paaster is a pastebin application. Prior to version 3.3.0, Paaster's account login has no rate limiting, lockout, or CAPTCHA of any kind, and a companion endpoint openly discloses whether a username exists along with that account's password-hashing salts. Together these let an attacker enumerate real accounts and then brute-force their passwords with unlimited, unthrottled attempts. This issue has been patched in version 3.3.0.

items.title: Heym builds and runs agentic systems and business-process automations on self-hosted infrastructure.
items.description: Heym builds and runs agentic systems and business-process automations on self-hosted infrastructure. Prior to version 0.0.71, Heym's workflow engine accepts an arbitrary Python code string in the playwrightCode field of a Playwright node. This string is written to a temporary .py file and executed directly by the backend process via subprocess.Popen([sys.executable, script_path]) with no sandboxing, AST validation, or role gate. Any authenticated user — including a freshly registered account — can achieve full remote code execution (RCE) on the backend host, running as the service process user (observed as root in the default Docker deployment). This issue has been patched in version 0.0.71.

items.title: Heym builds and runs agentic systems and business-process automations on self-hosted infrastructure.
items.description: Heym builds and runs agentic systems and business-process automations on self-hosted infrastructure. Prior to version 0.0.75, the same POST /api/mcp/fetch-tools endpoint (any authenticated user, lowest role) also accepts the stdio transport, which spawns the attacker-supplied command with attacker-supplied args and an environment merged over os.environ. The process executes on the shared backend host before MCP protocol validation fails — so side effects fire regardless of whether the command speaks MCP. This is a distinct weakness class and exploit primitive from the SSRF (Advisory 2) on the same endpoint, and needs a different fix (role gating / opt-in trust boundary rather than egress controls). This issue has been patched in version 0.0.75.

items.title: taOS is a self-hosted AI agent OS.
items.description: taOS is a self-hosted AI agent OS. Prior to version 1.0.0-beta.23, the POST /api/skill-exec/{skill_id}/call endpoint in taOS executes built-in skills — including the code_exec skill which runs arbitrary Python via subprocess.run(["python3", "-c", code]) — without performing any admin role check, skill ownership check, or agent assignment verification. Any authenticated non-admin user can supply attacker-controlled Python code in the request body and have it executed as the taOS backend process user on the host, achieving full remote code execution with no privilege escalation required beyond a valid (non-admin) session. This issue has been patched in version 1.0.0-beta.23.

items.title: taOS is a self-hosted AI agent OS.
items.description: taOS is a self-hosted AI agent OS. Prior to version 1.0.0-beta.25, tinyagentos (taOS) registers all system settings routes under a single APIRouter() instance created with no admin authorization dependency. Any authenticated user—including non-admin invited users whose is_admin flag is explicitly False—can read the full system configuration, overwrite it, modify platform settings, trigger a git pull + dependency reinstall + service restart, and switch the tracked update branch. Successful exploitation of the write endpoints causes immediate configuration corruption or a denial of service for all users on the instance from a low-privileged account. This issue has been patched in version 1.0.0-beta.25.

items.title: Heym builds and runs agentic systems and business-process automations on self-hosted infrastructure.
items.description: Heym builds and runs agentic systems and business-process automations on self-hosted infrastructure. Prior to version 0.0.73, the HTTP workflow node in Heym makes outbound HTTP requests to user-supplied URLs without validation of the target host or IP address. If a workflow author has already configured an HTTP node that targets internal addresses such as cloud metadata endpoints or private network hosts, and exposed the workflow with anonymous execution, an unauthenticated attacker can trigger the preconfigured SSRF sink. The same project has comprehensive SSRF protection in its MCP integration, which is absent from the HTTP node. This issue has been patched in version 0.0.73.

items.title: Portabase is a database backup and restore tool for PostgreSQL, MySQL, MsSQL, MariaDB, Firebird SQL, SQLite, MongoDB, R…
items.description: Portabase is a database backup and restore tool for PostgreSQL, MySQL, MsSQL, MariaDB, Firebird SQL, SQLite, MongoDB, Redis, Files and Docker Volume. Prior to version 1.21.2, a path traversal in the TUS upload webhook handler (app/api/tus/hooks/route.ts) allowed an unauthenticated attacker to overwrite arbitrary files under the private data directory, including /data/private/keys/master_key.bin (the AES-256-GCM master key). This issue has been patched in version 1.21.2.

items.title: Heym builds and runs agentic systems and business-process automations on self-hosted infrastructure.
items.description: Heym builds and runs agentic systems and business-process automations on self-hosted infrastructure. Prior to version 0.0.70, heym hardens one untrusted-code path but not its sibling. The Python tool executor (python_tool_executor.py) treats user code as untrusted and mandates a Docker sandbox (no network, read-only fs, non-root, no docker socket), failing closed. The skill executor (skill_python_executor.py) runs skill Python via a local backend subprocess with no Docker isolation — only a 512 MB RLIMIT and a 7-key env denylist — so a skill executes inside the backend execution context, with filesystem access, network egress, and non-denylisted environment variables that should not be exposed to untrusted/shared skills. In the shipped Docker config (backend runs as root + /var/run/docker.sock mounted), this escalates to host root. This issue has been patched in version 0.0.70.

items.title: Heym builds and runs agentic systems and business-process automations on self-hosted infrastructure.
items.description: Heym builds and runs agentic systems and business-process automations on self-hosted infrastructure. Prior to version 0.0.70, team-member management (add / remove / update) is gated only on team membership, not on the team creator/admin role — and TeamMember has no role column. Any non-creator member can seat an attacker account into the team; because credential team-shares are scoped only by TeamMember.user_id, the newly-added attacker can then decrypt every credential shared into that team (provider API keys, OAuth tokens. This issue has been patched in version 0.0.70.

items.title: Livewire PowerGrid creates data tables based on Laravel Livewire library.
items.description: Livewire PowerGrid creates data tables based on Laravel Livewire library. From version 6.0.0 to before version 6.10.4, the public Livewire property sortDirection is interpolated verbatim into a raw SQL ORDER BY clause and is not restricted to asc/desc, allowing arbitrary SQL injection through POST /livewire/update. This issue has been patched in version 6.10.4.

items.title: Heym builds and runs agentic systems and business-process automations on self-hosted infrastructure.
items.description: Heym builds and runs agentic systems and business-process automations on self-hosted infrastructure. Prior to version 0.0.70, POST /api/mcp/fetch-tools is reachable by any authenticated user (lowest role; no admin/workflow association) and fetches an attacker-supplied URL through the sse and streamable_http transports with no scheme / private-IP / allowlist / redirect guard. The transport error is reflected in the HTTP 422 response, giving a semi-blind SSRF oracle, and the attacker also controls the outbound request headers. This issue has been patched in version 0.0.70.

items.title: Heym builds and runs agentic systems and business-process automations on self-hosted infrastructure.
items.description: Heym builds and runs agentic systems and business-process automations on self-hosted infrastructure. Prior to version 0.0.70, get_workflow_template / get_node_template fetches a template by ID with no visibility / author / shared_with predicate, so any authenticated user can read (and use) any other tenant's private (visibility=specific_users) template — including its full node/edge graph and the email addresses it was shared with. The list endpoint enforces visibility correctly; the single-item get/use paths do not. This issue has been patched in version 0.0.70.

items.title: ideon is a self-hosted visual workspace.
items.description: ideon is a self-hosted visual workspace. Prior to version 0.9.5, ideon's link-preview endpoint requires no authentication at all and forwards any URL a caller supplies straight into a server-side fetch. The app does have a general-purpose SSRF guard (safeFetch/validateSafeUrl in src/app/lib/ssrf.ts), but this route sits behind no login check whatsoever, making it a fully open, anonymous URL-fetch relay - and the guard's IP blocklist itself has a gap that lets it reach the server's own loopback interface via the 0.0.0.0 "any address" bypass, a well-documented SSRF-filter evasion technique on Linux. This issue has been patched in version 0.9.5.

items.title: ideon is a self-hosted visual workspace.
items.description: ideon is a self-hosted visual workspace. Prior to version 0.9.4, several project mutation endpoints under /api/projects/[id]/* resolve the caller's project role but never enforce it, so a user who was granted only the read-only viewer role on a project can perform write operations on that project. The most severe is POST /api/projects/[id]/graph, which deletes every block and link in the project and re-inserts client-supplied ones. A viewer can silently rewrite or wipe the entire canvas of a project they were invited to read. The application clearly intends viewer to be read-only: the collaborators endpoint, the automation endpoints, and the realtime Yjs sync path all reject write attempts from viewers. These specific HTTP handlers simply omit the guard their siblings enforce. This issue has been patched in version 0.9.4.

items.title: nginx-http-flv-module is a media streaming server based on nginx-rtmp-module.
items.description: nginx-http-flv-module is a media streaming server based on nginx-rtmp-module. Prior to version 1.2.14, if a server received an HTTP/1.0 request without a header Host, which was permitted by HTTP core of Nginx, then r->headers_in.host was NULL, nginx-http-flv-module used r->headers_in.host->value to make a pseudo tcUrl, so NULL-pointer dereference happened. This issue has been patched in version 1.2.14.

items.title: Helio is an MCP proxy that sits between AI agents and the tools they use.
items.description: Helio is an MCP proxy that sits between AI agents and the tools they use. Prior to version 0.8.0, the dashboard sideband (default 127.0.0.1:3100) validated CORS request origins by matching the hostname against a private-network string prefix (10., 172.16.–172.31., 192.168.) rather than validating an IP address. A public DNS name such as 192.168.attacker.com, 10.evil.io, or 172.16.pwn.example also satisfies that prefix, so the proxy echoed the attacker origin in Access-Control-Allow-Origin. This issue has been patched in version 0.8.0.

items.title: Laradocs maintains version-controlled documentation inside a Laravel codebase.

This issue has been patched in version 1.0.0.

items.title: ideon is a self-hosted visual workspace.
items.description: ideon is a self-hosted visual workspace. Prior to version 0.9.4, validateUrlForSSRF() / safeFetch() in lib/oauth/ssrf-protection.ts (and the parallel validateMcpUrl() in lib/security/validators.ts) perform SSRF host-blocking by string/regex matching on new URL(url).hostname. Their IPv6 branch only recognises the textual forms ::1, fe80:/fc00:/fd00: prefixes, and the dotted-decimal IPv4-mapped form ::ffff:127.x. It does not recognise the WHATWG-canonical IPv4-mapped-IPv6 host that Node emits for a mapped address, which is hex-compressed and bracket-wrapped: [::ffff:7f00:1] for 127.0.0.1, [::ffff:a9fe:a9fe] for 169.254.169.254. An authenticated user who registers a STREAMABLE_HTTP / SSE MCP server with URL http://[::ffff:7f00:1]:PORT/ (loopback) or http://[::ffff:a9fe:a9fe]/ (cloud metadata) passes both guards, and the server-side OAuth-discovery action then fetches that host, yielding server-side request forgery to loopback and to the cloud metadata service. This issue has been patched in version 0.9.4.

items.title: ideon is a self-hosted visual workspace.
items.description: ideon is a self-hosted visual workspace. Prior to version 0.9.6, the SSRF protection in safeFetch is bypassed by IPv6 transition addresses that embed private IPv4 addresses. The isPrivateIP function in src/app/lib/ssrf.ts checks only a narrow set of IPv6 ranges (loopback ::1, ULA fc/fd, link-local fe80) but does not recognize IPv4-mapped (::ffff:), NAT64 well-known (64:ff9b::/96, RFC 6052), NAT64 local-use (64:ff9b:1::/48, RFC 8215), 6to4 (2002::/16, RFC 3056), or Teredo (2001::/32, RFC 4380) encodings. An authenticated user can supply these addresses in link URLs to reach cloud metadata endpoints (169.254.169.254), localhost services, and RFC 1918 internal networks through the link preview metadata fetcher. This issue has been patched in version 0.9.6.

items.title: A flaw was found in Cockpit.
items.description: A flaw was found in Cockpit. A local authenticated user with control over a target account's home directory can exploit a privileged symlink dereference vulnerability in the `ssh-add-public-key.sh` helper. When this helper runs with elevated privileges, it can be tricked into following attacker-controlled symlinks within the `.ssh` or `authorized_keys` paths. This allows the attacker to arbitrarily change file ownership and modes, potentially leading to local privilege escalation and impacting the integrity, confidentiality, and availability of the system.

items.title: A flaw was found in Cockpit.
items.description: A flaw was found in Cockpit. This vulnerability allows a remote attacker, without prior authentication, to send specially crafted fragmented WebSocket messages. These messages accumulate without a total-size limit, leading to unbounded memory exhaustion and a denial of service in the `cockpit-ws` service.

items.description: sync-rpc runs asynchronous commands synchronously by putting them in a separate proces. items.description: Probo is a self-hostable governance, risk, and compliance (GRC) platform built for engineering and security teams. items.title: Fider is a feedback portal for feature requests and suggestions.
items.description: Fider is a feedback portal for feature requests and suggestions. Prior to version 0.34.0, a Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) vulnerability exists in Fider due to insufficient validation of webhook URLs. The application allows user-controlled URLs to be fetched by the server without restricting access to internal or external network resources. This enables attackers with administrative privileges to make arbitrary HTTP requests from the server, potentially accessing internal services or cloud metadata endpoints. This issue has been patched in version 0.34.0.

items.title: Probo is a self-hostable governance, risk, and compliance (GRC) platform built for engineering and security teams.
items.description: Probo is a self-hostable governance, risk, and compliance (GRC) platform built for engineering and security teams. Prior to version 0.224.0, the public Trust Center GraphQL API exposes Query.node(id:) with @authentication(required: OPTIONAL) — an unauthenticated internet visitor to any published trust center can call it. Six of its type branches — Organization, Framework, Audit, ThirdParty (subprocessor), TrustCenter, and TrustCenterReference — resolve the object with a tenant scope derived from the client-supplied GID itself (coredata.NewScopeFromObjectID(id)) and load it with a bare Get(scope, id) that performs no comparison to the current trust center's OrganizationID and no showOnTrustCenter/visibility check. (The Document and File branches, by contrast, correctly pass trustCenter.OrganizationID and check visibility). This issue has been patched in version 0.224.0.

items.title: Probo is a self-hostable governance, risk, and compliance (GRC) platform built for engineering and security teams.
items.description: Probo is a self-hostable governance, risk, and compliance (GRC) platform built for engineering and security teams. Prior to version 0.224.0, the public Trust Center GraphQL API exposes acceptElectronicSignature and recordSigningEvent, both gated only by @authentication(required: PRESENT) @sessionOnly — any self-provisioned trust center identity can call them. The underlying esign.Service.AcceptSignature and esign.Service.recordEvent build the tenant scope from the client-supplied signatureId GID (coredata.NewScopeFromObjectID(req.SignatureID)) and load the signature by that GID. At no point do they verify that the signature belongs to the caller or that the caller's email matches the signature's SignerEmail. As a result, any authenticated trust-center visitor who possesses another visitor's signature GID can: (1) complete that visitor's NDA signature — overwriting signer name/IP/UA with attacker data and setting status to Accepted, which triggers the sealing worker to generate a completion certificate; (2) inject arbitrary audit-trail events into any signature's log. Both attacks defeat the non-repudiation and integrity guarantees of the e-signature system. This issue has been patched in version 0.224.0.

items.title: Fider is a feedback portal for feature requests and suggestions.
items.description: Fider is a feedback portal for feature requests and suggestions. Prior to version 0.36.0, in multi-tenant mode (HOST_MODE=multi), an attacker can use an email verification key issued by Tenant A to authenticate as the same email address on Tenant B. This completely bypasses tenant isolation and allows unauthorized account takeover across tenants. Single-host deployments (HOST_MODE=single, the default) are NOT affected. This issue has been patched in version 0.36.0.

items.title: iopress is a native HTTP server for Node.js with platform-specific async I/O.
items.description: iopress is a native HTTP server for Node.js with platform-specific async I/O. Prior to version 1.0.5, the chunked-transfer-encoding HTTP request parser in @iopress/core reads past the end of the input buffer when a request declares a chunk size larger than the body actually received. This results in a heap-buffer-over-read. This issue has been patched in version 1.0.5.

items.title: Probo is a self-hostable governance, risk, and compliance (GRC) platform built for engineering and security teams.
items.description: Probo is a self-hostable governance, risk, and compliance (GRC) platform built for engineering and security teams. Prior to version 0.223.1, Probo's console GraphQL API is a multi-tenant GRC platform where all data is scoped to an organization. A Finding can reference a Risk via finding.riskId. That reference is stored without validating that the risk belongs to the caller's organization, and the Finding.risk field resolver authorizes the finding (caller's org) instead of the risk, then loads the risk with a tenant scope derived from the risk's own global ID. As a result, an authenticated member of organization A can attach an arbitrary organization B risk GID to a finding they own and then read organization B's Risk (name, description, treatment, category, severity, owner) — with no membership in B. The stored cross-tenant reference also blocks B from deleting its own risk (ON DELETE RESTRICT), a cross-tenant integrity/DoS. This issue has been patched in version 0.223.1.

items.title: Probo is a self-hostable governance, risk, and compliance (GRC) platform built for engineering and security teams.
items.description: Probo is a self-hostable governance, risk, and compliance (GRC) platform built for engineering and security teams. Prior to version 0.222.0, the GraphQL endpoint does not enforce restrictions on alias count, query depth, or query complexity. An attacker can send a single request containing thousands of aliased resolver calls, causing excessive server-side resource consumption and service degradation. This issue has been patched in version 0.222.0.

items.title: geojson-vt is a JavaScript library for slicing GeoJSON data into vector tiles on the fly, primarily designed to enable…
items.description: geojson-vt is a JavaScript library for slicing GeoJSON data into vector tiles on the fly, primarily designed to enable rendering and interacting with large geospatial datasets on the browser side (without a server). Prior to version 6.1.1, @maplibre/geojson-vt contains an uncontrolled recursion vulnerability in its GeoJSON conversion logic. When a GeoJSONVT instance is constructed with a deeply nested GeometryCollection object, the mutually recursive functions featureToInternal and convertGeometryCollection in src/convert.ts exhaust the Node.js call stack, causing an unhandled RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded that terminates the process. Because the library is widely used in server-side tile services that accept GeoJSON over the network, a remote unauthenticated attacker can trigger a denial-of-service by sending a single crafted payload. No authentication is required, and no non-default library options are needed. This issue has been patched in version 6.1.1.

items.title: A deferred-callback use-after-destroy in Node.js TLS server handshake handling allows a remote, unauthenticated attacke…
items.description: A deferred-callback use-after-destroy in Node.js TLS server handshake handling allows a remote, unauthenticated attacker to terminate the server process. When a TLS server uses any of the SNICallback, OCSPRequest, newSession, or resumeSession hooks, or server.addContext(), the corresponding OpenSSL callbacks are deferred, and the deferred code does not handle the underlying socket being destroyed between scheduling and execution. By sending a client hello that reaches the vulnerable path (for example, no SNI together with an OCSP request) followed by padding and a socket FIN, an attacker makes OpenSSL deliver the client hello and the end-of-file in the same tick, so the socket is destroyed before the deferred callback runs and the process raises an uncaught exception instead of emitting an 'error' event. This vulnerability affects Node.js 26.x and 24.x.

items.title: OpsTree REMS through 1.0.0 contains an improper authorization vulnerability that allows authenticated users to set an i…
items.description: OpsTree REMS through 1.0.0 contains an improper authorization vulnerability that allows authenticated users to set an incident's reporter to another user by supplying a client-controlled reporter field. Attackers can send crafted POST /api/v1/incidents or PATCH /api/v1/incidents/{id}/status requests to falsify incident attribution and corrupt the accountability audit trail.

items.title: A client certificate authentication bypass in Node.js TLS lets a client change the servername during TLS 1.2 renegotiat…
items.description: A client certificate authentication bypass in Node.js TLS lets a client change the servername during TLS 1.2 renegotiation to reach endpoints it was not authorized for. On a server that applies different client-certificate policies per hostname, for example stricter admin-only client-cert auth on one host and ordinary client-cert auth on another, a client that authenticates for a permitted host can renegotiate the TLS 1.2 connection under a different servername and carry its existing authentication to the protected host, bypassing the stricter policy. This vulnerability affects Node.js 26.x, 24.x, and 22.x.

items.title: A use-after-free in Node.js HTTP/2 lets an unauthenticated client corrupt server memory, over both TLS and cleartext, w…
items.description: A use-after-free in Node.js HTTP/2 lets an unauthenticated client corrupt server memory, over both TLS and cleartext, when the server serves files with respondWithFile() or respondWithFD(). A client can make the server free an Http2Stream while a write request that points to it is still queued on the socket; when that write completes, the code dereferences and makes a virtual call through the freed object. The only precondition is that the application serves a file with stream.respondWithFile() or stream.respondWithFD(), with default settings otherwise. This vulnerability affects Node.js 26.x (since 26.9.0) and 24.x (since 24.22.0).

items.title: A certificate validation bypass in Node.js https.Agent lets a cached TLS session authenticated under one CA policy be r…
items.description: A certificate validation bypass in Node.js https.Agent lets a cached TLS session authenticated under one CA policy be reused by a later request with a stricter policy. https.Agent.prototype.getName() assigns the same Agent and session-cache key to a request that omits ca and one that explicitly supplies ca: [], because an omitted value appends nothing to the key while an empty array stringifies to an empty string. The two policies differ: omitting ca uses the default trust store, while supplying ca replaces it. Since they share a key, a TLS session authenticated under the broader default policy is handed to a new connection made under the later ca: [] policy, and TLS 1.3 session resumption carries the earlier authentication forward, so the second request reports authorized === true and transmits confidential data to a server its own CA policy would reject on a fresh connection. This vulnerability affects Node.js 26.x, 24.x, and 22.x.

items.title: Node.js discloses proxy credentials in ERR_PROXY_INVALID_CONFIG error messages.
items.description: Node.js discloses proxy credentials in ERR_PROXY_INVALID_CONFIG error messages. CVE-2026-48615 established that a proxy credential must not appear in a Node.js error message and redacted the username and password from ProxyConfig.href, but that fix missed four error paths in the same subsystem, one of them inside the same constructor, which interpolate the raw proxy URL, credentials included, into an ERR_PROXY_INVALID_CONFIG message. The proxy URL comes from the environment, but the defect is the sink: a secret that Node.js redacts everywhere else is emitted verbatim into a much wider audience than the process environment, such as stderr, container logs, log aggregation, and crash reporting services. This vulnerability affects Node.js 26.x, 24.x, and 22.x.

items.title: A NULL pointer dereference in Node.js HTTP/2 lets an unauthenticated client crash the server, over both TLS and clearte…
items.description: A NULL pointer dereference in Node.js HTTP/2 lets an unauthenticated client crash the server, over both TLS and cleartext, by cancelling file downloads. When the server serves a file with stream.respondWithFile() or stream.respondWithFD() and the client cancels the request, a StreamPipe used for the transfer is torn down in an order that leaves a NULL pointer which is then dereferenced, aborting the process. No crafted frames are needed, and a handful of cancelled requests against a default file-serving handler is enough. This vulnerability affects Node.js 26.x, 24.x, and 22.x.

items.title: An unauthenticated HTTP/2 client can permanently leak Node.js server memory and file descriptors.
items.description: An unauthenticated HTTP/2 client can permanently leak Node.js server memory and file descriptors. If a peer triggers a protocol error, for example an oversized frame header, while the session is already shutting down, nghttp2 tears the session down internally but Node.js never notices, leaving a dangling session: the socket stays in CLOSE_WAIT and all of Node.js's HTTP/2 state for that connection is held in memory indefinitely, with no further cost to the attacker. The attacker can start the shutdown remotely by sending GOAWAY(NO_ERROR), so it is reliable against default HTTP/2 servers. It is an incomplete-fix case of CVE-2026-48937: that fix detected nghttp2 internal terminations by watching for GOAWAY sent while not shutting down, but missed terminations that arrive while the session is already shutting down. This vulnerability affects Node.js 26.x, 24.x, and 22.x.

items.title: A use-after-free in Node.js HTTP/2 stream teardown can leak response memory, including the contents of other connection…
items.description: A use-after-free in Node.js HTTP/2 stream teardown can leak response memory, including the contents of other connections' response buffers, to a peer. When a stream is torn down while a write is still backpressured, for example by a peer RST_STREAM or by the server's own per-stream timeout destroying the stream, the stream's response buffer is freed but a reference to it is still used, so freed or unrelated heap memory is written to the socket instead of the intended response. On Node.js 26.x and 24.x the teardown can be driven purely by a remote peer once the window-size change from 26.9.0 and 24.22.0 is present, and on all supported lines the same defect is reachable through an application-initiated teardown such as a per-stream idle timeout. This vulnerability affects Node.js 26.x, 24.x, and 22.x.

items.title: An unauthenticated HTTP/2 client can exhaust Node.js server memory because inbound DATA queued on an undrained stream i…
items.description: An unauthenticated HTTP/2 client can exhaust Node.js server memory because inbound DATA queued on an undrained stream is charged to no session budget. Each inbound DATA frame creates one JavaScript Buffer view in the receiving stream's readable queue, but nothing charges that queue to current_session_memory_: the socket read buffer is accounted only during parsing and released immediately, so whatever stays queued is accounted to nothing. A peer that fills a stream's receive window with one-byte DATA frames pays about 10 wire bytes per frame while the server retains about 114 bytes per frame, so a single stream on one connection can retain hundreds of megabytes from tens of megabytes sent. maxSessionMemory neither bounds the growth nor refuses new streams, because Http2Session::CanAddStream gates admission on the same counter that never sees the queue. This vulnerability affects Node.js 26.x and 24.x.

items.title: A per-host mutual-TLS authorization bypass in Node.js lets a client authorized for the default hostname reach a protect…
items.description: A per-host mutual-TLS authorization bypass in Node.js lets a client authorized for the default hostname reach a protected hostname it is not authorized for. When a TLS server assigns a hostname a different client-certificate CA with `server.addContext(host, { ca: protectedCA })` but no server certificate in that SNI context, the per-host client CA is never installed and the handshake falls back to the default client CA. In `src/crypto/crypto_tls.cc`, `CertCbDone` installs the SNI context's CA only when `setSniContext` succeeds, but `setSniContext` returns `false` for a context with no server certificate, so a CA-only SNI context silently keeps the default CA. A client holding a certificate trusted by the default CA, but not the protected CA, can therefore complete mTLS to the protected hostname and read its response even with `requestCert` and `rejectUnauthorized` enabled, while a client certified by the protected CA is rejected. This vulnerability affects Node.js 26.x, 24.x, and 22.x.

items.title: A reachable assertion in Node.js HTTP/2 session teardown lets any unauthenticated client abort the server, over both TL…
items.description: A reachable assertion in Node.js HTTP/2 session teardown lets any unauthenticated client abort the server, over both TLS and cleartext. A client can arrange for an Http2Stream that still holds nghttp2-allocated header buffers to outlive its session: the stream is removed from the session's stream set but never detached, so when ~Http2Session() runs the memory accounting is nonzero and the CHECK_EQ(current_nghttp2_memory_, 0) assertion fails, terminating the process. The trigger needs only a default http2 server whose handler responds before the request body has ended, which is typical. It is a variant of CVE-2024-27983 that the earlier fix did not cover, because that fix only detached streams still tracked in the session. This vulnerability affects Node.js 26.x (since 26.9.0) and 24.x (since 24.22.0).

items.title: A re-entrancy flaw in Node.js HTTPS lets an unauthenticated client read memory belonging to other connections, includin…
items.description: A re-entrancy flaw in Node.js HTTPS lets an unauthenticated client read memory belonging to other connections, including TLS private keys and other users' requests. TLSWrap::DoWrite() calls ClearOut() directly when asked to write zero bytes; if that write is issued from JavaScript running inside the HTTP parser's on_body callback, ClearOut() decrypts the next TLS record while the parser is still mid-body, re-entering llhttp_execute() and causing a use-after-free and an out-of-bounds heap read. The server then copies that freed or unrelated heap memory into the response for the request body. Triggering it requires a handler that calls res.flushHeaders() before the request body ends and later calls res.end() with a non-empty chunk, and reading the leaked memory requires any ordinary route that echoes or stores a request body. Cleartext node:http is not affected. This vulnerability affects Node.js 26.x, 24.x, and 22.x.

items.title: An uncatchable exception in the Node.js zlib streaming API lets a peer crash a process by disconnecting while data is b…
items.description: An uncatchable exception in the Node.js zlib streaming API lets a peer crash a process by disconnecting while data is being compressed. zlib.params() queues a flush and completes its work in that write's callback; if the stream is destroyed first, as pipeline() does when the peer goes away, Writable still invokes the callback with an error, but the callback ignores its arguments and asserts that the native handle still exists. The handle is gone, so an ERR_INTERNAL_ASSERTION is thrown from inside stream internals and bypasses the stream's error event, the params() callback, and the pipeline() callback, terminating the process. An application is affected only if it calls deflate.params() while streaming to a peer, which is uncommon. This vulnerability affects Node.js 26.x, 24.x, and 22.x.

items.title: A Permission Model bypass in Node.js recursive file watching discloses the names of files and directories the process i…
items.description: A Permission Model bypass in Node.js recursive file watching discloses the names of files and directories the process is not permitted to read. On macOS and Windows, fs.watch() and fs.promises.watch() in recursive mode are backed by the native libuv watcher: FSEventWrap::Start checks kFileSystemRead only once, on the watched root, and FSEventWrap::OnEvent then forwards every filename libuv reports (relative paths at any depth) to the JavaScript callback without checking that each path is covered by the read grant. Code running under --permission with an exact read grant on a directory can therefore learn names such as sub/secret.txt even though readdir on that subdirectory is denied. The flaw exposes names and timing metadata, not file contents, and requires macOS or Windows plus files created under the watched directory by another actor. This vulnerability affects Node.js 26.x, 24.x, and 22.x.

items.title: A flaw was found in pappl-retrofit.
items.description: A flaw was found in pappl-retrofit. The application fails to properly sanitize user-supplied filenames when handling the upload and deletion of PostScript Printer Description (PPD) files. A remote, unauthenticated attacker can exploit this directory traversal flaw by submitting filenames containing path traversal sequences. This allows the attacker to upload or delete arbitrary files on the system, which can result in data corruption, denial of service, or arbitrary command execution.

items.title: A one-byte heap buffer overflow in Node.js HTTP/2 Alt-Svc handling lets a remote, unauthenticated attacker corrupt proc…
items.description: A one-byte heap buffer overflow in Node.js HTTP/2 Alt-Svc handling lets a remote, unauthenticated attacker corrupt process memory. When an application passes an attacker-controlled value such as a request's :authority header to Http2Session.altsvc(), the AltSvc implementation in src/node_http2.cc allocates a buffer sized to the origin length and then writes it with a null terminator, placing one byte past the end of the allocation. A single request carrying a long but syntactically valid :authority triggers the out-of-bounds write, which aborts the process and serves as a remote heap-corruption primitive. This vulnerability affects Node.js 26.x and 24.x.

items.description: A flaw was found in the xfs_admin utility in xfsprogs. The tool does not properly validate user-supplied parameters, allowing operating system command injection. A local attacker can exploit this issue by providing crafted input arguments, which may result in arbitrary command execution and local privilege escalation depending on how xfs_admin is executed.

items.title: A cross-site request forgery vulnerability in tracker-invocation.php in Revive Adserver 6.0.8 and earlier allows an att…
items.description: A cross-site request forgery vulnerability in tracker-invocation.php in Revive Adserver 6.0.8 and earlier allows an attacker to modify a tracker's name, description or advertiser assignment using an authenticated victim's permissions. A leftover state-changing handler accepts request parameters without verifying a CSRF token, although it is not used by the normal invocation-tag interface. Exploitation requires victim interaction and a request path that carries the victim's session credentials. The issue is fixed in Revive Adserver 6.0.9 by removing the unused tracker-modification handler.

items.title: An authorization bypass in channel-edit.php in Revive Adserver 6.0.8 and earlier allows an authenticated manager to cre…
items.description: An authorization bypass in channel-edit.php in Revive Adserver 6.0.8 and earlier allows an authenticated manager to create a delivery rule set belonging to another agency by changing the submitted agencyid parameter. The server trusts the submitted agency identifier when inserting the new rule set, allowing unauthorized creation of objects in another agency's account. The issue is fixed in Revive Adserver 6.0.9 by obtaining the agency identifier from the authenticated account rather than submitted form data and removing the agency identifier from the form's hidden fields.

items.title: An authorization bypass in campaign-zone linking in Revive Adserver 6.0.8 and earlier allows an authenticated manager,…
items.description: An authorization bypass in campaign-zone linking in Revive Adserver 6.0.8 and earlier allows an authenticated manager, or a trafficker with zone-linking permissions, to associate another agency's campaign with their own zone. Campaign ownership checks are missing from the bulk-linking and single-link operations in zone-include.php and the XML-RPC campaign-linking method. Although agency filtering prevents foreign banners from being linked, the unauthorized association can expose the foreign campaign's name, type and identifier in the linked-campaign listing. The issue is fixed in Revive Adserver 6.0.9 by validating campaign ownership in the affected operations.

items.title: An authorization bypass in website-index.php in Revive Adserver 6.0.8 and earlier allows an authenticated manager restr…
items.description: An authorization bypass in website-index.php in Revive Adserver 6.0.8 and earlier allows an authenticated manager restricted to one agency to view another agency's website listing by changing the agencyid request parameter. Disclosed information includes website names, identifiers and timestamps. Detailed website pages continue to enforce ownership checks. The issue is fixed in Revive Adserver 6.0.9 by obtaining the agency identifier from the authenticated account rather than the request.

items.title: The OWASP core rule set (CRS) is a set of generic attack detection rules for use with compatible web application firewa…
items.description: The OWASP core rule set (CRS) is a set of generic attack detection rules for use with compatible web application firewalls. Prior to versions 3.3.10, 4.25.1, and 4.28.0, regular-expression denial of service (ReDoS) affects a shared regex-assembly include used to build 12 Unix RCE detection rules in CRS v4, and the same ambiguous pattern was present in the manually-assembled regexes in 4 rules in CRS v3.3. With a single, unauthenticated, crafted request, the generated pattern drives PCRE2 past its backtracking limit. When PCRE2 exceeds that limit, the @rx operator returns an error rather than a match result, which results in detection bypass and CPU denial of service. This issue has been patched in versions 3.3.10, 4.25.1, and 4.28.0.

items.title: aeon is a scikit-learn compatible Python library for learning from time series.
items.description: aeon is a scikit-learn compatible Python library for learning from time series. Prior to version 1.5.0, a GitHub Actions workflow used pull_request_target for pre-commit checks on pull requests from forks. In this configuration, fork-controlled code could be checked out and executed in a privileged context. The vulnerable workflow also generated/used elevated credentials and could automatically commit or push fixes back to pull request branches. This created a potential token exposure and repository write path if an attacker submitted a malicious fork pull request designed to execute during the privileged workflow run. This issue has been patched in version 1.5.0.

items.title: The OWASP core rule set (CRS) is a set of generic attack detection rules for use with compatible web application firewa…
items.description: The OWASP core rule set (CRS) is a set of generic attack detection rules for use with compatible web application firewalls. Prior to versions 3.3.10, 4.25.1, and 4.28.0, CRS rules in the 921 (protocol-attack), 930 (LFI), 931 (RFI), 932 (RCE), 933 (PHP), 934 (generic), 941 (XSS), 942 (SQLi), and 943 (session-fixation) families inspect XML request bodies via the XPath expression XML:/*. That expression matches only element text nodes — it does not match XML attribute values. As a result, an attacker who places an attack payload inside an XML attribute (e.g. or ) bypasses CRS detection entirely. This is verified empirically against a local CRS test instance and against the public CRS sandbox. The bypass affects approximately 159 rules across 9 rule files and applies at every paranoia level (PL1 through PL4), since the variable list is more or less shared across PLs. The 944 (Java) family is the only one that correctly includes XML://@* in addition to XML:/* and is therefore unaffected. This issue has been patched in versions 3.3.10, 4.25.1, and 4.28.0.

items.title: vulnerability-operator scans SBOMs and Images for vulnerabilities.
items.description: vulnerability-operator scans SBOMs and Images for vulnerabilities. Prior to version 0.28.16, an unauthenticated information-disclosure vulnerability exposes all vulnerability scan reports served by the operator. The /report/ HTTP endpoint mounts a raw http.FileServer over the reports directory (default /reports) with no authentication, authorization, or middleware. Any client that can reach the operator's HTTP port (default 8080) can list and download every JSON vulnerability report, disclosing CVE IDs, affected package names/versions, and container image identifiers for every workload scanned in the cluster. This issue has been patched in version 0.28.16.

items.title: Janus WebRTC Server 1.2.3 through 1.4.0 is vulnerable to Directory Traversal.
items.description: Janus WebRTC Server 1.2.3 through 1.4.0 is vulnerable to Directory Traversal. The application accepts a caller supplied media path when an ondemand stream is created. The path is validated only by checking whether it contains one of the audio extensions and is then passed to the file source which opens it. No canonicalization is performed and no directory allowlist is enforced, so an unauthenticated caller can make the server open an arbitrary local file and use it as a media source, with the content delivered to viewers as RTP audio.

items.title: A reflected cross-site scripting vulnerability in the invocation-tag generation interface of Revive Adserver 6.0.8 and…
items.description: A reflected cross-site scripting vulnerability in the invocation-tag generation interface of Revive Adserver 6.0.8 and earlier allows an unauthenticated attacker to execute JavaScript in an authenticated user's browser by persuading them to visit a crafted URL. When Direct Selection is enabled, an attacker-controlled banner identifier can be included in HTML form fields without appropriate encoding. Direct Selection is disabled by default. The issue is fixed in Revive Adserver 6.0.9 by HTML-encoding banner identifier values in the invocation-option form fields.

items.title: A reflected cross-site scripting vulnerability in the popup invocation options of Revive Adserver 6.0.8 and earlier all…
items.description: A reflected cross-site scripting vulnerability in the popup invocation options of Revive Adserver 6.0.8 and earlier allows an unauthenticated attacker to execute JavaScript in an authenticated user's browser by persuading them to visit a crafted URL. The top, left, timeout and delay request parameters are included in HTML attributes without appropriate encoding. Exploitation requires an existing popup zone, which can be created through the administrator API but is not offered by the normal zone-creation interface. The issue is fixed in Revive Adserver 6.0.9 by HTML-encoding the affected popup option values.

items.title: A reflected cross-site scripting vulnerability in the conversion-statistics pages of Revive Adserver 6.0.8 and earlier…
items.description: A reflected cross-site scripting vulnerability in the conversion-statistics pages of Revive Adserver 6.0.8 and earlier allows an unauthenticated attacker to execute JavaScript in an authenticated user's browser by persuading them to visit a crafted URL. An incorrect ownership check validates the advertiser identifier instead of the supplied website identifier, allowing malicious website input to reach HTML output without appropriate encoding. A related output issue affects the hour parameter. The issue is fixed in Revive Adserver 6.0.9 by validating the correct website identifier and normalising the hour parameter before formatting.

items.title: A reflected cross-site scripting vulnerability in the iframe invocation options of Revive Adserver 6.0.8 and earlier al…
items.description: A reflected cross-site scripting vulnerability in the iframe invocation options of Revive Adserver 6.0.8 and earlier allows an unauthenticated attacker to execute JavaScript in an authenticated user's browser by persuading them to visit a crafted URL. When generating invocation tags for an any-size zone, the frame_width and frame_height request parameters are included in HTML attributes without appropriate encoding. The issue is fixed in Revive Adserver 6.0.9 by HTML-encoding the affected values in the invocation-option form fields.

items.title: A reflected cross-site scripting vulnerability in updates-history.php in Revive Adserver 6.0.8 and earlier allows an un…
items.description: A reflected cross-site scripting vulnerability in updates-history.php in Revive Adserver 6.0.8 and earlier allows an unauthenticated attacker to execute JavaScript in a victim's browser by persuading them to visit a crafted URL. Attacker-controlled values are included in XML command attributes without appropriate encoding, allowing injection of executable XHTML into the response. The preliminary session check omits GET xajax requests, exposing an unauthenticated attack path, while authenticated administrator requests also reach the unsafe output. The issue is fixed in Revive Adserver 6.0.9 by applying the session check to both GET and POST requests and encoding XML command attribute values in both response serializers.

items.title: A stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in the report date-selection controls of Revive Adserver 6.0.8 and earlier…
items.description: A stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in the report date-selection controls of Revive Adserver 6.0.8 and earlier allows an unauthenticated attacker to execute JavaScript in a victim's browser by persuading them to follow a crafted report URL and complete normal reauthentication. An attacker-controlled period_preset value can be saved in the victim's session and inserted into JavaScript without appropriate encoding. The payload can execute on the initial report view and subsequent report views using the stored defaults. The issue is fixed in Revive Adserver 6.0.9 by applying JSON encoding appropriate for the JavaScript context to date-selection values.

items.title: A stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in maintenance-appendcode-check.php in Revive Adserver 6.0.8 and earlier al…
items.description: A stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in maintenance-appendcode-check.php in Revive Adserver 6.0.8 and earlier allows an authenticated manager to execute JavaScript in an administrator's browser. A manager can store a malicious tracker name and cause the tracker to appear in the append-code maintenance results. When an administrator opens the affected maintenance page, the tracker name is included in HTML without appropriate encoding. The issue is fixed in Revive Adserver 6.0.9 by HTML-encoding tracker names when displaying the maintenance results.

items.title: Spreadsheet formula injection in conversion-tracking report exports in Revive Adserver 6.0.8 and earlier allows an unau…
items.description: Spreadsheet formula injection in conversion-tracking report exports in Revive Adserver 6.0.8 and earlier allows an unauthenticated attacker to submit conversion values that are written as formulas instead of text in an XLS workbook. When a user opens the exported report in a spreadsheet application, attacker-supplied formulas can be evaluated. The confirmed impact is formula execution within the workbook; disclosure of information to the attacker has not been established. The issue is fixed in Revive Adserver 6.0.9 by sanitising conversion values before writing them to the affected XLS report sections.

items.title: In Progress® Telerik® Report Server prior to version 12.3.26.1110, an external control of a system configuration settin…
items.description: In Progress® Telerik® Report Server prior to version 12.3.26.1110, an external control of a system configuration setting vulnerability allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to influence the server address used by Report Server when generating links and notifications. With user interaction, this can lead to disclosure of sensitive information and account takeover.

items.title: Blind SQL injection in Revive Adserver 6.0.8 and earlier allows an authenticated manager restricted to one agency to ex…
items.description: Blind SQL injection in Revive Adserver 6.0.8 and earlier allows an authenticated manager restricted to one agency to extract arbitrary database values through the banner-zone.php and campaign-zone.php administration pages. Permission checks and database queries obtain identifiers through inconsistent request-input precedence, allowing an authorized numeric identifier to pass validation while a different, attacker-controlled value reaches an SQL query. Extracted data can include password hashes and active session identifiers. Reusing an unexpired administrator session can grant administrative access, allowing modification of configuration and disruption of ad delivery. The issue is fixed in Revive Adserver 6.0.9 by consistently selecting POST values before GET values in both global input registration and common input helpers, and excluding cookies from these helpers. Both commits e301dbbb7 and 0aa9d0124 are required for the complete correction.

items.title: In affected versions of Progress® Telerik® UI for ASP.NET MVC `2012.2.710` through `2026.3.811`, ClassFactory updates a…
items.description: In affected versions of Progress® Telerik® UI for ASP.NET MVC `2012.2.710` through `2026.3.811`, ClassFactory updates a shared class dictionary without exclusive write protection and emits non-collectible dynamic assemblies that remain loaded for the AppDomain's lifetime. The dictionary lookup and insertion are not atomic, and case variations in aggregate descriptors can produce distinct retained types even though member resolution is case-insensitive. An unauthenticated remote attacker can exploit this if the application exposes an aggregation endpoint that is reachable without authentication, by submitting concurrent or repeated crafted requests. These requests may corrupt dictionary state or increase CPU and memory use, potentially degrading availability. The issue is fixed in version `2026.3.1015`.

items.title: In Progress® Telerik® UI for ASP.NET Core versions `2015.1.318` through `2026.3.811`, repeated server-side aggregation…
items.description: In Progress® Telerik® UI for ASP.NET Core versions `2015.1.318` through `2026.3.811`, repeated server-side aggregation requests, with or without grouping, cause dynamic assemblies and load contexts to be retained, resulting in accumulating process memory consumption. An unauthenticated remote attacker can exploit this if the application exposes an aggregation endpoint that is reachable without authentication. Repeated requests can cause memory growth that may exhaust available resources and affect application availability. Disabling grouping in the client-side interface does not prevent direct requests containing these descriptors. The issue is fixed in version `2026.3.1015`.

items.title: An authorization bypass in Revive Adserver 6.0.0 through 6.0.8 allows an authenticated manager restricted to one agency…
items.description: An authorization bypass in Revive Adserver 6.0.0 through 6.0.8 allows an authenticated manager restricted to one agency to access or modify resources belonging to another agency. Global input registration gives GET parameters precedence over POST parameters, while submitted administration forms use POST values. By supplying authorized object identifiers in the query string and different identifiers in the POST body, an attacker can cause permission checks and subsequent operations to target different objects. This permits unauthorized cross-agency changes, campaign ownership reassignment and disclosure of campaign and banner data. The regression was introduced in commit 156dee7bc3283c128f35e5a31bb305054cc8de1b and is fixed in Revive Adserver 6.0.9 by restoring POST precedence in global input registration.

items.description: Rooxis RXR-12 Wi-Fi router contains an undocumented telnet backdoor daemon (/usr/bin/telnetd_startup) that, upon receipt of a precomputed AES-128-CBC magic packet using a firmware-wide static key and IV, enables telnet service with default credentials, providing remote root access. items.title: Rooxis RXR-12 Wi-Fi router contains an authenticated command injection vulnerability in the LuCI white_list RPC handler…
items.description: Rooxis RXR-12 Wi-Fi router contains an authenticated command injection vulnerability in the LuCI white_list RPC handler (/usr/lib/lua/luci/data/white_list_plt.lua), where unsanitized user-supplied MAC addresses are concatenated into os.execute() without validation, yielding root command execution via a malformed mac parameter. items.description: Rooxis RXR-12 Wi-Fi router contains an unauthenticated remote code execution vulnerability in /usr/bin/cloud_manage, where a server-controlled JSON diagnoseParameter field is passed unsanitized to popen(), enabling arbitrary command execution as root over cleartext HTTP when an attacker is positioned on-path and has access to the hard-coded cloud endpoint. Firmware 20260813_c2169ea5 fixes the vulnerability, and your router can be updated through the local web interface.

items.title: In Progress Kendo UI for jQuery, sanitizeSvgContent() parses custom icon markup into a live DOM before filtering it.
items.description: In Progress Kendo UI for jQuery, sanitizeSvgContent() parses custom icon markup into a live DOM before filtering it. An attacker who can influence custom icon content can cause JavaScript to execute during icon creation, before an unsafe element is removed. The issue was reported in version 2026.3.1015; the first affected release has not been established. The issue is fixed in version 2026.4.1110.

items.title: In Progress Kendo UI for jQuery versions 2026.3.1015 up to, but not including, 2026.4.1110, the Grid and TreeList colum…
items.description: In Progress Kendo UI for jQuery versions 2026.3.1015 up to, but not including, 2026.4.1110, the Grid and TreeList column-reorder drag clue reparses header text as HTML. An attacker who can influence a column field or title used by an affected application can cause JavaScript to execute when a user drags a column header while column reordering is enabled. items.title: In Progress Kendo UI for jQuery versions 2026.3.1015 up to, but not including, 2026.4.1110, PivotGrid and PivotConfigur…
items.description: In Progress Kendo UI for jQuery versions 2026.3.1015 up to, but not including, 2026.4.1110, PivotGrid and PivotConfigurator axis field names are passed to a chip template without appropriate encoding. An attacker who can influence an axis field name can cause JavaScript to execute when a user views the rendered chip. The field name can be interpreted as HTML in both attribute and element contexts. items.title: In Progress Kendo UI for jQuery versions 2026.3.1015 up to, but not including, 2026.4.1110, PropertyGrid does not encod…
items.description: In Progress Kendo UI for jQuery versions 2026.3.1015 up to, but not including, 2026.4.1110, PropertyGrid does not encode bound property values and items[].description in its default configuration. items.title: When parsing request variables such as query-string and form parameters, HHVM did not check that appending a nested arr…
items.description: When parsing request variables such as query-string and form parameters, HHVM did not check that appending a nested array succeeded before descending into it. A remote, unauthenticated attacker could send a GET or POST request which would crash the HHVM server process before any application code runs, leading to denial of service. This issue affected HHVM prior to 23c061f4e804a51badd5f85227e65185651253b5.

items.title: When a remote, unauthenticated HTTP/1.1 client pipelined the start of a second request and then stopped reading, proxyg…
items.description: When a remote, unauthenticated HTTP/1.1 client pipelined the start of a second request and then stopped reading, proxygen's coroutine-based HTTP session could free that pipelined stream while resetting the connection's streams on the resulting write timeout, then go on to use it. This can crash the server, leading to denial of service, and may allow memory corruption with further impact. This issue affects proxygen versions prior to v2026.11.09.00.

items.title: In Progress® Kendo® UI for jQuery versions from 2022.2.621 prior to 2026.4.1111 the DropDownButton and SplitButton allo…
items.description: In Progress® Kendo® UI for jQuery versions from 2022.2.621 prior to 2026.4.1111 the DropDownButton and SplitButton allow markup injection through the `id` and `target` attributes. items.title: In Progress® Kendo® UI for jQuery prior to 2026.4.1111 the TabStrip, PanelBar, and Menu widgets support mapping a dataS…
items.description: In Progress® Kendo® UI for jQuery prior to 2026.4.1111 the TabStrip, PanelBar, and Menu widgets support mapping a dataSource field to `spriteCssClass`. If an attacker can control the mapped data, they can break out of the attribute and inject markup, including event-handler attributes. The resulting JavaScript executes in the application's origin when a victim loads a page that renders the affected widget, allowing access to data and actions available in the victim's authenticated session.

items.title: In Progress Kendo UI for jQuery versions 2026.3.1014 up to, but not including, 2026.4.1110, ActionSheet does not encode…
items.description: In Progress Kendo UI for jQuery versions 2026.3.1014 up to, but not including, 2026.4.1110, ActionSheet does not encode title, subtitle, and header button label values before rendering them. An attacker who can influence these values can inject markup that executes as JavaScript when a user opens the ActionSheet. Successful exploitation may compromise the confidentiality and integrity of data available in the user's browser context. The report identifies version 2026.3.1014; the first affected release has not been established.

items.title: repmgr 4.0.0 through 5.5.0 is affected by an OS command injection vulnerability (CWE-78) in event notifications.
items.description: repmgr 4.0.0 through 5.5.0 is affected by an OS command injection vulnerability (CWE-78) in event notifications. When event_notification_command is configured, repmgr substitutes the %a (node name), %c (connection string) and %d (details) placeholders into the command and runs it through the shell. %a and %c are inserted without escaping, and %d escapes only double quotes, so shell command substitution still works inside the quoting the documentation recommends. The node name and connection string come from node records in the repmgr.nodes table. An attacker with the credentials of a non-superuser repmgr database user can write a crafted node record and run OS commands, as the operating system user that runs repmgr or repmgrd (usually postgres), on other cluster nodes that process an event using these placeholders. The %a placeholder of failover_validation_command has the same flaw. Deployments whose repmgr database user is a superuser gain no new capability, because a superuser can already run OS commands, and deployments that do not use these placeholders are not affected. The issue is fixed in repmgr 5.5.1. After upgrading, operators must remove any quotes they placed around these placeholders, because a placeholder left inside double quotes is still open to command injection.

items.title: A potential improper permissions vulnerability was reported in Lenovo XiangBangbang that could allow a local applicatio…
items.description: A potential improper permissions vulnerability was reported in Lenovo XiangBangbang that could allow a local application to perform unauthorized touch gestures.

items.title: proxygen's HTTP/3 codec buffered an incomplete non-DATA frame, such as a control-stream frame, a frame of an unknown or…
items.description: proxygen's HTTP/3 codec buffered an incomplete non-DATA frame, such as a control-stream frame, a frame of an unknown or reserved type, or a HEADERS frame, until its entire declared length had arrived, without limiting that length, and re-scanned all buffered data each time more bytes arrived. A remote, unauthenticated HTTP/3 peer could declare a very large frame and deliver it slowly, causing unbounded memory growth and CPU usage that grows quadratically with the number of fragments, leading to denial of service. This issue affects proxygen versions prior to v2026.11.09.00.

items.title: mvfst did not adequately merge or compact out-of-order STREAM frame data, and a small received fragment could keep a mu…
items.description: mvfst did not adequately merge or compact out-of-order STREAM frame data, and a small received fragment could keep a much larger receive buffer alive. QUIC flow control limits the number of buffered stream bytes, but not this per-fragment memory and bookkeeping. A remote, unauthenticated QUIC peer could send many small, non-contiguous stream fragments to make an endpoint consume memory far in excess of its advertised receive window and spend increasing CPU time reassembling stream data, leading to denial of service. This issue affects mvfst versions prior to v2026.11.09.0.

items.title: proxygen's QPACK decoder enforced its size limit on a string literal in an encoder-stream instruction only after the en…
items.description: proxygen's QPACK decoder enforced its size limit on a string literal in an encoder-stream instruction only after the entire literal had been received. A remote, unauthenticated HTTP/3 peer could send an insert instruction on the QPACK encoder stream that declares an arbitrarily large literal and then keep sending data, causing the decoder to buffer it without bound for the lifetime of the connection and exhaust memory, leading to denial of service. The issue occurs regardless of the advertised QPACK dynamic table capacity, including when the dynamic table is disabled. This issue affects proxygen versions prior to v2026.11.09.00.

items.title: An mvfst QUIC server retained CRYPTO frame data received at an encryption level (Initial or Handshake) that the TLS han…
items.description: An mvfst QUIC server retained CRYPTO frame data received at an encryption level (Initial or Handshake) that the TLS handshake had already moved past. Because the transport treated this data as delivered, it did not count against the CRYPTO stream buffer limit. A remote, unauthenticated client could complete a handshake, withhold its acknowledgment of the server's HANDSHAKE_DONE frame so that Handshake keys stay in use, and keep sending Handshake-level CRYPTO data at increasing offsets, causing unbounded memory growth on the server and leading to denial of service. This issue affects mvfst versions prior to v2026.11.09.00.

items.title: In proxygen's HTTP/3 session, when a HEADERS block referenced QPACK dynamic table entries that had not yet been receive…
items.description: In proxygen's HTTP/3 session, when a HEADERS block referenced QPACK dynamic table entries that had not yet been received, header decoding for that stream was paused, but the session continued to read the stream from the QUIC transport. The unread data bypassed the session's ingress buffer limit, returned flow-control credit to the peer, and was re-scanned in full on every read. With QPACK blocked streams enabled (the default), a remote, unauthenticated HTTP/3 peer could send a HEADERS block that references a dynamic table insert it never sends, followed by a continuous stream of data, causing memory growth until the request timed out and CPU usage that grows quadratically, leading to denial of service. This issue affects proxygen versions prior to v2026.11.09.00.

items.title: soapbar is a SOAP library for Python — client, server, and WSDL handling.
items.description: soapbar is a SOAP library for Python — client, server, and WSDL handling. Prior to version 0.13.0, verify_envelope_bsp() derived its trust anchor from the message it was verifying. It read the X.509 certificate out of the caller-untrusted wsse:BinarySecurityToken, validated only that certificate's not-before / not-after dates, and then verified the signature against that same certificate. There was no CA-chain validation, no issuer/subject allowlist, and no pinning. A successful verify_envelope_bsp() therefore proved only that the envelope was signed by whoever supplied the embedded certificate — never that it was signed by a trusted party. An attacker who mints their own certificate, signs a forged envelope, and embeds that certificate in the token passes verification. Any consumer that treats a successful BSP verification as authentication can be impersonated (signature forgery / authentication bypass). verify_envelope() (which pins a caller-supplied x509_cert) was not affected — the flaw was specific to the BSP variant whose trust anchor came from the message. This issue has been patched in version 0.13.0.

items.title: Calling the wide scanf family of functions (swscanf, fwscanf, wscanf, vswscanf, vfwscanf and vwscanf) with a %s or %[ c…
items.description:
Calling the wide scanf family of functions (swscanf, fwscanf, wscanf, vswscanf, vfwscanf and vwscanf) with a %s or %[ conversion without the 'l' length modifier in the GNU C Library version 2.2 to version 2.44 writes an extra null byte one past the end of the destination array when the converted multibyte string and its terminating null byte exactly fill that array.

These conversions store each wide input character into the caller's char array as a multibyte sequence.  The conversion ends with the sequence that returns to the initial shift state, which also stores the terminating null byte, and the functions then append a second null byte.  A destination sized for the converted string and one terminator, as the C standard requires the caller to provide, is therefore written one byte past its end.  The out-of-bounds byte is always a null byte, which may corrupt adjacent data or crash the process.  An attacker who supplies the input can trigger the overflow with a string whose converted length exactly fills the destination.

The narrow scanf functions, the %ls and %l[ conversions into a wchar_t array, and the 'a' and 'm' allocation modifiers are not affected, and storing a wide scanf conversion into a narrow char array is uncommon.  This issue affects all architectures and ABIs supported by the GNU C Library.

items.title: The regcomp and regexec functions in the GNU C Library version 2.3 to version 2.44 may read freed memory and free the s…
items.description:
The regcomp and regexec functions in the GNU C Library version 2.3 to version 2.44 may read freed memory and free the same heap block twice when a memory allocation fails while a regular expression is compiled or matched.  The re_dfa_add_node (the NFA node table) and build_range_exp (bracket ranges) grow several arrays with consecutive realloc calls and store the new pointers only after all of them succeed.  When a later call fails, the pattern buffer keeps pointers to blocks that were already freed, and the error cleanup frees them again.  In regexec, the back-reference cache (match_ctx_add_entry) frees its array when a realloc fails but keeps the pointer, which is freed again on the error path.

An attacker does not need to supply a crafted regular expression: patterns large enough to grow these arrays are common.  The failure has to hit a specific allocation, though, so the issue can only be reached when the system is already under memory pressure.  An attacker who supplies the pattern or the subject string has little control over which allocation fails, so the expected impact is a crash of the process.  This issue affects all architectures and ABIs supported by the GNU C Library.

items.title: The Ninja Forms - File Uploads add-on for WordPress is vulnerable to Arbitrary File Deletion (and arbitrary file read v…
items.description: The Ninja Forms - File Uploads add-on for WordPress is vulnerable to Arbitrary File Deletion (and arbitrary file read via S3/Dropbox/Google Drive exfiltration) in versions up to, and including, 3.3.36. The flaw spans NF_FU_Fields_Upload::process() in includes/fields/upload.php — which returns early (leaving the client-supplied files[] intact) whenever a public submission carries a nonempty extra.saveProgress — and NF_FU_External_Abstracts_Service::process_upload() in includes/external/abstracts/service.php, whose authoritative-path reload only fires when the client sends upload_id. By omitting upload_id, an attacker's data[file_path] survives into the Background Upload queue and is used by both upload_file_to_s3() (as SourceFile) and the maybe_delete_server_file() unlink() call in includes/external/abstracts/backgroundupload.php, with no canonicalization or upload-directory containment check (the plugin's own is_path_within_upload_dir() helper is only applied on admin paths). This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to delete arbitrary files on the affected site's server which may make remote code execution possible — specifically, deleting wp-config.php forces WordPress into its setup screen, enabling full site takeover.

items.description: A flaw was found in BusyBox. When extracting files using the cpio utility with path traversal protection enabled, hardlink target paths are not properly sanitized. items.title: Deserialization of Untrusted Data vulnerability in Apache Roller.
items.description: Deserialization of Untrusted Data vulnerability in Apache Roller. When Roller sends a weblog update ping, its XML-RPC client deserializes Java object data contained in the ping target's response, so a party that controls that response can run code in the Roller server process. This issue affects Apache Roller from 4.0 through 6.1.6. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 6.1.7, which removes the unsafe deserialization.

The entry editor checked the member's weblog role but not whether that role permits work on the entry.
Users are recommended to upgrade to Apache Roller 6.1.7 or later.

items.title: Uncontrolled Resource Consumption vulnerability in the sketch deserialization of Apache DataSketches Java.
items.description:
Uncontrolled Resource Consumption vulnerability in the sketch deserialization of Apache DataSketches Java.



Several deserializers trusted sizes and counts declared in the serialized input. A small crafted input could make an application allocate an excessive amount of memory, leading to an OutOfMemoryError. A crafted string passed to FrequentLongsSketch.getInstance(String) could also make deserialization, or a later update, loop indefinitely. Only applications that deserialize sketches from untrusted sources are affected.



This issue affects Apache DataSketches Java: through 9.0.0.



Users are recommended to upgrade to version 9.1.0, which fixes the issue.

items.title: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor in Apache Roller 4.0 through 6.1.6 allows an unauthenticated…

The entry preview checked that the user was logged in, but not that the user had a role in the weblog being previewed. The attacker must know the weblog name and the entry's link name.
