items.title: pgEdge Control Plane generates pg_hba.conf with trust authentication for local and loopback connections
items.description: pgEdge Control Plane is a distributed application for managing and orchestrating Postgres databases across multiple hosts. From 0.1.0 to 0.10.1, generated pg_hba.conf files began with hard-coded trust entries for Unix-socket and loopback connections. Because PostgreSQL evaluates the file from top to bottom, those entries also preempted operator-supplied rules in the pg_hba_conf field. Under the systemd orchestrator, any unprivileged operating-system account on a database host could authenticate as any PostgreSQL role, including the superuser, without credentials and obtain full control of the host's databases. Under Docker Swarm, reaching the container-local socket or loopback interface required code execution inside the database container. Publishing the PostgreSQL port to the host did not expose these trust rules because host connections did not appear to originate from 127.0.0.1 or ::1. This issue is fixed in version 0.11.0.

items.title: pgEdge Postgres MCP Server enables SQL queries against PostgreSQL databases through Model Context Protocol compatible c…
items.description: pgEdge Postgres MCP Server enables SQL queries against PostgreSQL databases through Model Context Protocol compatible clients. Prior to 1.1.0, deployments exposing the nondefault HTTP transport with authentication enabled used the leftmost caller-supplied X-Forwarded-For value as the client address for login rate limiting. ExtractIPAddress in internal/auth/middleware.go supplied that value to IsAllowed and RecordFailedAttempt in internal/auth/rate_limiter.go, allowing an unauthenticated caller to rotate addresses to evade throttling or assert another user's address to consume that user's limiter bucket. The published nginx configuration appended rather than replaced X-Forwarded-For, making the issue reachable without an operator misconfiguration. Username-keyed account lockout did not use the client address, but shipped defaults disabled that separate control through MaxFailedAttemptsBeforeLockout: 0. This issue is fixed in version 1.1.0.

items.title: pgEdge Postgres MCP Server enables SQL queries against PostgreSQL databases through Model Context Protocol compatible c…
items.description: pgEdge Postgres MCP Server enables SQL queries against PostgreSQL databases through Model Context Protocol compatible clients. Prior to 1.1.0, the where parameter of the count_rows tool accepted subqueries against tables other than the table named in the tool call. A caller could use predicates and the returned row count as an inference oracle to extract data from any other table that the connected database role could read. The database privilege boundary remained intact, and the flaw did not grant access to tables outside that role's existing SELECT privileges. This issue is fixed in version 1.1.0.

items.title: pgEdge RAG Server shared keyword index leaked results between concurrent unauthenticated requests
items.description: pgEdge RAG Server is an API server for retrieval-augmented generation over PostgreSQL content using pgvector. Prior to 2.0.0, the BM25 keyword index is a single per-pipeline object shared by the unauthenticated query endpoint, and concurrent requests lock its clear, refill, and search operations separately. This allows one request to search a corpus populated through another request's search filter, which can return documents belonging to a different tenant or customer without malformed input. The affected responses cannot be identified retrospectively from the server logs. This issue is fixed in version 2.0.0.

items.title: pgEdge Postgres MCP Server enables SQL queries against PostgreSQL databases through Model Context Protocol compatible c…
items.description: pgEdge Postgres MCP Server enables SQL queries against PostgreSQL databases through Model Context Protocol compatible clients. Prior to 1.1.0, the HTTP transport did not validate the Origin header on incoming requests. A user who visited an attacker-controlled page could be targeted through DNS rebinding, allowing the page to reach a locally running server and read schemas and query results from configured databases. The issue affected deployments with the HTTP transport enabled on a machine that also ran a browser, while the default stdio transport was not reachable through this path. This issue is fixed in version 1.1.0.

items.title: Improper Handling of Highly Compressed Data (CWE-409) in the ZIP loader of whatstk from 0.7.0 before 0.9.0 allows a par…
items.description: Improper Handling of Highly Compressed Data (CWE-409) in the ZIP loader of whatstk from 0.7.0 before 0.9.0 allows a party that supplies a chat export to exhaust the memory and the disk of the process that parses it, because _str_from_file() (whatstk/whatsapp/parser.py) calls zip_ref.extractall() with no bound on the size of the members and no check of the compression ratio, then reads the extracted file in full with f.read(). The only guard on the archive counts the extracted files and raises when there is not exactly one, but it runs after extractall() has already written them, so it does not prevent the cost. _clean_text() then passes the whole text through unicodedata.normalize("NFKD", text), which holds a second copy, and the parse builds a list of regular expression matches and a DataFrame over it, so peak memory is a multiple of the decompressed text rather than of the archive. A ZIP is a documented input of WhatsAppChat.from_source() and df_from_whatsapp(), and is the form in which WhatsApp exports a chat on iOS, so the attacker supplies the whole file. This results in a small upload costing hundreds of megabytes of memory and of disk, and in the process being killed where that exceeds what is available.

items.title: Web::Simple versions before 0.037 for Perl do not escape single quotes in HTML::Tags output.
items.description:
Web::Simple versions before 0.037 for Perl do not escape single quotes in HTML::Tags output.

HTML::Tags and XML::Tags escape a plain string value by replacing only &, ", < and > with entities. A value interpolated into a single-quoted attribute, as in <a href='$value'>, can therefore close the attribute and add new ones, such as an event handler. Double-quoted attributes are not affected.

An attacker who controls a value that an application interpolates into a single-quoted attribute can inject script into the generated page.

items.title: In Eclipse Kura version 5.0.0 to 5.6.2, the Web Console allocates a new HTTP session for every request to its built-in…
items.description: In Eclipse Kura version 5.0.0 to 5.6.2, the Web Console allocates a new HTTP session for every request to its built-in authentication endpoints (/admin/auth, /admin/login/password, /admin/login/cert) before checking the HTTP method, parsing the request, or validating any submitted credentials, and does not limit how many such sessions can be allocated. An unauthenticated client that sends requests to these endpoints without honoring the returned session cookie can cause the server to allocate an unbounded number of sessions, exhausting the JVM heap and crashing the Kura process.

items.title: In Kura versions <= 5.6.2, `CommandCloudApp.execute()` extracts a caller-supplied ZIP archive into a caller-supplied di…
items.description:
In Kura versions <= 5.6.2, `CommandCloudApp.execute()` extracts a caller-supplied ZIP archive into a caller-supplied directory inside the Kura JVM process before dispatching the command to the executor service. On a packaged Kura installation the JVM runs as `kurad` with `CAP_DAC_OVERRIDE`, while the configurable "Unprivileged" executor drops to the `kura` user via `su`.



A caller with permissions `rest.command` who is intentionally restricted to unprivileged command execution (`privileged.command.service.enable=false`, the default) can therefore set `workingDirectory` to `/` and use the ZIP body to write or overwrite arbitrary files on the device as `kurad`, completely bypassing the unprivileged sandbox the operator selected.



The command service is disabled by default since Kura 4.0.0 [1]. The issue does not apply when the command service is disabled.



[1] https://github.com/eclipse-kura/kura/blob/f9f969231892769a269876b23f19fa0e8173e3df/kura/distrib/RELEASE_NOTES.txt#L94

items.title: Missing Authentication for Critical Function in aggregation queries in Neo4j @neo4j/graphql 5.0.0 before 5.12.17 and 7.…
items.description: Missing Authentication for Critical Function in aggregation queries in Neo4j @neo4j/graphql 5.0.0 before 5.12.17 and 7.0.0 before 7.6.8 allows remote attackers to read protected data via GraphQL aggregation queries. Field-level @authentication is not enforced on string aggregates, which can return stored values verbatim, and connection-root aggregates bypass an entity's AGGREGATE authentication requirement, allowing unauthenticated callers to obtain aggregate results.

items.title: LiveDocs is a primary-source-first documentation for AI agents.
items.description: LiveDocs is a primary-source-first documentation for AI agents. items.title: rabbitmq-c is a C-language AMQP client library for RabbitMQ.
items.description: rabbitmq-c is a C-language AMQP client library for RabbitMQ. Prior to version 0.17.0, a heap buffer overflow exists in rabbitmq-c when the public amqp_send_frame() API is used to serialize an oversized AMQP_FRAME_BODY. The issue occurs because amqp_frame_to_bytes() copies frame.payload.body_fragment.len bytes into the connection outbound buffer without validating that the body fragment fits within the allocated frame buffer. An application that passes an oversized body frame to amqp_send_frame() can trigger a heap out-of-bounds write, resulting in process crash and memory corruption. This issue has been patched in version 0.17.0.

items.title: Group-Office is an enterprise customer relationship management and groupware tool.
items.description: Group-Office is an enterprise customer relationship management and groupware tool. Prior to versions 6.8.167, 25.0.102, and 26.0.27, the Contact/labels JMAP endpoint in GroupOffice accepts a fully attacker-controlled template string (tpl parameter) that is passed without restriction to TemplateParser::parse(). When the template contains an [assign] block whose expression includes a {{...}} variable reference, the engine calls eval() on the expanded expression after running it through a validateExpression() guard. The guard double-quotes unrecognized tokens, but PHP 7+ allows a string enclosed in parentheses to be invoked as a function ("system")("id") is valid PHP and calls system("id"). A single authenticated HTTP request is sufficient to execute arbitrary OS commands as the web server user (www-data). This issue has been patched in versions 6.8.167, 25.0.102, and 26.0.27.

items.title: Group-Office is an enterprise customer relationship management and groupware tool.
items.description: Group-Office is an enterprise customer relationship management and groupware tool. Prior to versions 6.8.172, 25.0.108, and 26.0.33, a low-privileged user can create manual reminders containing arbitrary HTML/JavaScript and assign them to any other user (including administrators). When the victim's browser polls for pending notifications, the payload renders unsanitized as innerHTML in the ExtJS notification panel, achieving Stored Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) leading to full Account Takeover (ATO) of the victim's session. This issue has been patched in versions 6.8.172, 25.0.108, and 26.0.33.

items.title: rabbitmq-c is a C-language AMQP client library for RabbitMQ.
items.description: rabbitmq-c is a C-language AMQP client library for RabbitMQ. Prior to version 0.17.0, the bounds check (*offset = o + len) <= encoded.len overflows when o + len > SIZE_MAX on 32-bit systems. len is a uint32_t read from the AMQP wire as a BYTES/UTF8 field length. The overflow wraps the check to a small value that passes, producing a decoded amqp_bytes_t with a multi-GB .len pointing into a small frame buffer. This results in an out-of-bounds read of up to ~4GB of process memory on 32-bit systems (ARM, MIPS, x86 ILP32, embedded IoT AMQP clients). Enabling information disclosure or denial of service. Not exploitable on 64-bit systems where size_t is 64-bit. This issue has been patched in version 0.17.0.

items.title: Gwenhywfar 4.99.8beta before 5.14.2 contains a stack-based buffer overflow in GWEN_TLV_Buffer_To_DB() in src/parser/tlv…

items.title: Gwenhywfar 5.14.2 contains a heap use-after-free vulnerability in GWEN_TLV_Buffer_To_DB() in src/parser/tlv.c, which fr…

Attackers can supply a constructed BER-TLV record with unparseable contents, such as via a malicious chip card read by libchipcard, to corrupt heap memory.

items.title: compose-lint: Workflow command injection through SARIF-directory errors triggered by pull request symlinks
items.description: compose-lint is a Docker Compose security linter that identifies dangerous misconfigurations before deployment. From version 0.30.0 until 0.32.0, the compose-lint GitHub Action prints the resolved directory from a failed sarif-file subdirectory creation without effective command suppression. Version 0.30.0 has no stop-commands window, while version 0.31.0 prints this error outside its stop-commands window. A pull request can place a committed symlink on that path to a directory whose name contains a newline followed by a workflow command, causing the SARIF-directory error to issue commands in the job log. Only the Action with sarif-file pointing into a subdirectory is affected; a workspace-root SARIF file, the compose-lint package, the pre-commit hook, and the Docker image do not expose this message. This issue is fixed in version 0.32.0.

items.title: compose-lint: Text in a pull request can still issue CI workflow commands through compose-lint 0.31.0's output
items.description: compose-lint is a Docker Compose security linter that identifies dangerous misconfigurations before deployment. In version 0.31.0, compose-lint escapes GitHub Actions workflow-command openers only after ASCII spaces and tabs, while the runner strips all leading Unicode whitespace before interpreting a line. Untrusted Compose values or repository paths beginning with Unicode whitespace followed by :: can therefore reach the text report, fix guidance, the fix dry-run diff, and stderr diagnostics as workflow commands when the package, pre-commit hook, or Docker image runs directly in CI. The GitHub Action is not affected because it disables command processing, and the flaw does not change the lint pass or fail result. This issue is fixed in version 0.32.0.

items.title: compose-lint: Text in a pull request can issue CI workflow commands through JSON and SARIF output on stdout
items.description: compose-lint is a Docker Compose security linter that identifies dangerous misconfigurations before deployment. In version 0.31.0, compose-lint does not sanitize the ##[ workflow-command opener inside strings written by --format json or --format sarif to stdout. A pull request can place that opener in a service name or other Compose value, and the GitHub Actions runner recognizes it even in the middle of a serialized line when the package, pre-commit hook, or Docker image prints JSON or SARIF to the job log. Writing the output to a file and using the compose-lint GitHub Action are not affected, and the flaw does not change the lint pass or fail result. This issue is fixed in version 0.32.0.

items.title: compose-lint: File paths embedded in pull requests can inject CI workflow commands through command-line error messages
items.description: compose-lint is a Docker Compose security linter that identifies dangerous misconfigurations before deployment. In version 0.31.0, compose-lint's argument parser writes rejected repository paths to stderr without the output sanitizer when a path is passed without a preceding -- separator. A pull request can supply a path containing workflow-command syntax; a carriage return can position that command at the start of a new line recognized by the GitHub Actions runner, allowing the package, Docker image, or a pre-commit hook with misconfigured args to issue the command in the job log. The default pre-commit configuration includes -- and is not affected, the GitHub Action is not affected, and the lint pass or fail result is unchanged. This issue is fixed in version 0.32.0.

items.title: compose-lint is a Docker Compose security linter that identifies dangerous misconfigurations before deployment.
items.description: compose-lint is a Docker Compose security linter that identifies dangerous misconfigurations before deployment. In version 0.31.0, compose-lint does not neutralize the Azure Pipelines ##vso[ logging-command opener on any output path. A pull request can place that opener in a Compose value or file name, allowing output from the package, pre-commit hook, or Docker image to issue logging commands when printed to an Azure Pipelines job log. The maintainer did not reproduce the behavior on an Azure Pipelines agent. The GitHub Action is not affected because it runs only on GitHub Actions, and releases before 0.31.0 are outside this advisory because they did not claim Azure Pipelines coverage. This issue is fixed in version 0.32.0.

items.title: When tarfile or zipfile command line interface (CLI) is used to decompress an archive, a Python script shadowing the st…
items.description:
When tarfile or zipfile command line interface (CLI) is used to

decompress an archive, a Python script shadowing the stdlib can be

created. Then if an error occurs during decompressing the next file,

the newly created Python script is executed. This is especially true

if the created Python is called traceback.py. The problem is that

Python adds the current directory to sys.path when python -m MODULE is

run, and the archive is also decompressed in the current directory.



The fix removes sys.path[0] in gzip, tarfile and zipfile command line

interface to prevent shadowing standard library modules from extracted

files.

items.title: In Eclipse Kura versions 5.4.0 through 5.6.2, the Service Listing V1 REST API read the JSON body of every request into…
items.description: In Eclipse Kura versions 5.4.0 through 5.6.2, the Service Listing V1 REST API read the JSON body of every request into memory, with no limit on its size. The endpoints parse the body before they check whether the caller is authenticated. A remote attacker without valid credentials can therefore send a few dozen large JSON requests at the same time, exhaust the Java heap with an `OutOfMemoryError`, and cause a denial of service. Likewise, a remote attacker, can send a deeply nested JSON request and trigger a `StackOverflowError` because of an unbound recursion in Service Listing V1.

items.title: In Eclipse Kura versions 5.1.0 through 5.6.2, the Configuration REST API v2 (org.eclipse.kura.rest.configuration.provid…
items.description: In Eclipse Kura versions 5.1.0 through 5.6.2, the Configuration REST API v2 (org.eclipse.kura.rest.configuration.provider) does not restrict access to the configuration of the UserAdmin persistence component to identities holding the kura.admin permission. An authenticated identity holding only the rest.configuration permission can read the password hashes of all identities, including administrators, which are stored as unsalted SHA-256 digests. The same identity can also modify identities and permission assignments, and restore previous configuration snapshots, which allows escalation to full administrative privileges. The issue is fixed in Eclipse Kura 5.6.3.

items.title: In Kura versions <= 5.6.2, the "Command" file-upload handler at `POST /admin/denali/file/command` extracts a client-sup…
items.description:
In Kura versions <= 5.6.2, the "Command" file-upload handler at `POST /admin/denali/file/command` extracts a client-supplied ZIP archive into the configured `command.working.directory`. The path-containment check `validateFileName()` compares canonical paths with `String.startsWith()` without appending a trailing path separator, so an entry that canonicalises to a sibling directory sharing the same string prefix (e.g. `/tmpevil/x` when the intended directory is `/tmp`) is accepted. The handler then calls `parent.mkdirs()` and `new FileOutputStream(newFile)`, creating directories and writing attacker-controlled bytes outside the intended extraction root.



The command service is disabled by default since Kura 4.0.0 [1]. The issue does not apply when the command service is disabled. The caller must be authenticated with `rest.command` permission.

items.title: Joomla Extension - j2commerce.com - Gift voucher and single-use coupon could pay for more than one order in J2Store 6.0…
items.description: Joomla Extension - j2commerce.com - Gift voucher and single-use coupon could pay for more than one order in J2Store 6.0.0 - 6.6.5 - A logged-in customer could redeem a single gift voucher, or a single-use coupon (`max_uses` / `max_customer_uses` = 1), on more than one order. By starting several checkout sessions and carrying each to the confirm step before submitting any of them, every order independently saw the voucher's full balance or the coupon's unused slot, because the balance/usage calculations and the final placement check both only looked at orders that had already left the "New" state.

items.title: The embedded HTTP server does not clear the security identity established during a request before its worker thread han…
items.description: The embedded HTTP server does not clear the security identity established during a request before its worker thread handles the next request. A remote unauthenticated attacker can have their request processed with the identity of a previously authenticated user, gaining that user's privileges. Only applications served by the embedded HTTP server that authenticate programmatically or via basic authentication are affected. Users are recommended to block network access to the embedded HTTP server from untrusted clients, or to migrate to the Tomcat based TomEE distributions.

items.title: The embedded HTTP server does not invalidate the previous session identifier when an application changes the session id…
items.description: The embedded HTTP server does not invalidate the previous session identifier when an application changes the session id, e.g. after login. An attacker who can plant a session identifier in a victim's browser can hijack the victim's authenticated session. Users are recommended to block network access to the embedded HTTP server from untrusted clients, or to migrate to the Tomcat based TomEE distributions.

items.title: The embedded OpenEJB HTTP server dispatches some requests to REST endpoints configured for HTTP Basic authentication wi…
items.description: The embedded OpenEJB HTTP server dispatches some requests to REST endpoints configured for HTTP Basic authentication without verifying credentials. A remote unauthenticated attacker can invoke protected resources, bypassing authentication. Only deployments that use the embedded HTTP server with Basic authentication are affected. Users are recommended to block network access to the embedded HTTP server from untrusted clients, or to migrate to the Tomcat based TomEE distributions.

items.title: When Hessian remoting endpoints are served by the embedded HTTP server, configured authentication and transport securit…
items.description: When Hessian remoting endpoints are served by the embedded HTTP server, configured authentication and transport security requirements are silently ignored. A remote unauthenticated attacker can invoke the exposed EJB methods without credentials or over an unencrypted connection. Only deployments that use the embedded HTTP server rather than Tomcat and rely on these settings are affected. Users are recommended to block network access to Hessian endpoints from untrusted clients, or to migrate to another remoting protocol.

items.title: When Hessian remoting is configured with BASIC authentication, the authentication check is not applied to Hessian endpo…
items.description: When Hessian remoting is configured with BASIC authentication, the authentication check is not applied to Hessian endpoints of applications deployed under a non-root context path. A remote unauthenticated attacker can invoke the exposed EJB methods without credentials. Users are recommended to block network access to Hessian endpoints from untrusted clients, or to migrate to another remoting protocol.

items.title: When an EJB is exposed over the optional Hessian protocol inside an existing web application, some configured authentic…
items.description: When an EJB is exposed over the optional Hessian protocol inside an existing web application, some configured authentication and transport security settings are silently not enforced. A remote unauthenticated attacker can invoke the exposed EJB methods. Only deployments using the Hessian module with such settings are affected. Users are recommended to block network access to Hessian endpoints from untrusted clients, or to migrate to another remoting protocol.

items.title: The embedded OpenEJB HTTP server does not restrict static resource paths to the configured resource directories.
items.description: The embedded OpenEJB HTTP server does not restrict static resource paths to the configured resource directories. A remote unauthenticated attacker can read arbitrary files accessible to the server process. Users are recommended to block network access to the embedded HTTP server from untrusted clients, or to migrate to the Tomcat based TomEE distributions.

items.title: The embedded Derby network service ignores its configured bind address and listens on all network interfaces.
items.description: The embedded Derby network service ignores its configured bind address and listens on all network interfaces. When the service is enabled, a remote attacker with network access can connect to the database server and read or modify data. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 10.3.0 or 11.0.0-M2, which fix the issue.

items.title: The EJBd remote protocol returns datasource connection details, including database credentials, to remote clients that…
items.description: The EJBd remote protocol returns datasource connection details, including database credentials, to remote clients that look up a datasource. A remote client able to reach the EJBd endpoint can obtain the database credentials and connect to the database directly. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 10.3.0 or 11.0.0-M2, which fix the issue.

items.title: In Eclipse Kura versions 3.1.0 to 5.6.2, the iBeacon and Eddystone advertisement decoders wrongly parse the AD-structur…
items.description: In Eclipse Kura versions 3.1.0 to 5.6.2, the iBeacon and Eddystone advertisement decoders wrongly parse the AD-structure length field of an over-the-air BLE advertising payload. Any unauthenticated attacker within BLE radio range can broadcast a two-byte advertising payload that drives the Kura beacon-scanner thread into a tight infinite loop, pinning a CPU core and permanently halting beacon ingestion until the gateway is restarted. To trigger the attack, the iBeacon/Eddystone scanner component should be installed and active. By default the components are not installed or enabled.

items.title: Apache TomEE running on JDK 21 or later skips EJB method authorization checks, allowing callers to invoke EJB methods w…
items.description: Apache TomEE running on JDK 21 or later skips EJB method authorization checks, allowing callers to invoke EJB methods without the configured access restrictions being enforced. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 10.3.0 or 11.0.0-M2, which fix the issue.

items.title: The embedded OpenEJB HTTP server does not limit the size of incoming request bodies or of multipart requests, and does…
items.description: The embedded OpenEJB HTTP server does not limit the size of incoming request bodies or of multipart requests, and does not remove the temporary files it creates for multipart parts. A remote unauthenticated attacker can cause excessive memory or disk usage, leading to denial of service. Deployments using the Tomcat connectors are not affected. Users are recommended to block network access to the embedded HTTP server from untrusted clients, or to migrate to the Tomcat based TomEE distributions.

items.title: The remote EJB client does not verify that the hostname of the server it connects to matches the server's TLS certifica…
items.description: The remote EJB client does not verify that the hostname of the server it connects to matches the server's TLS certificate. An attacker able to intercept network traffic between an EJB client and server can impersonate the server and read or modify the traffic, including credentials and invocation data. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 10.3.0 or 11.0.0-M2, which fix the issue.

items.title: Cleartext transmission of sensitive information in the Agent of Ivanti Endpoint Manager before version 2024 SU8 allows…
items.description: Cleartext transmission of sensitive information in the Agent of Ivanti Endpoint Manager before version 2024 SU8 allows a remote unauthenticated attacker to in a MITM position to read and modify HTTP traffic.

items.title: mailcow: dockerized before 2026-11 contains a server-side template injection vulnerability that allows domain administr…
items.description: mailcow: dockerized before 2026-11 contains a server-side template injection vulnerability that allows domain administrators to execute commands in the shared rspamd container by storing a malicious domain-wide footer. Attackers can embed a Jinja macro with an os.execute default value, rendered by the rspamd MOO_FOOTER prefilter, to read or inject mail for every tenant and disable filtering.

items.title: Aptabase before commit 61d4c01 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to…
items.description: Aptabase before commit 61d4c01 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to forge sign-in links by using the publicly known example AUTH_SECRET. Attackers can enumerate registered e-mails via /api/_auth/signin, forge HS256 JWTs redeemed by /api/_auth/continue, impersonate users, export analytics data, and transfer app ownership.

items.title: Nango before 0.71.3 contains an sql injection vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to execute arbitrary…
items.description: Nango before 0.71.3 contains an sql injection vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to execute arbitrary SQL by supplying a crafted task group key to the orchestrator API. Attackers can send a malicious group.key to POST /v1/immediate, which TaskEventsHandler.notify() interpolates into a Postgres NOTIFY statement, running stacked queries against the scheduler database.

items.title: Nodemailer 3.0.0 before 10.4.1 contains an address parsing flaw in addressparser that truncates domains at folding whit…
items.description: Nodemailer 3.0.0 before 10.4.1 contains an address parsing flaw in addressparser that truncates domains at folding whitespace or comments before a dot, allowing attackers to bypass recipient domain restrictions. Attackers can submit crafted to, cc, bcc or replyTo addresses that pass RFC 5322 domain checks but deliver mail to an attacker-chosen address under the application's sender identity.

items.title: ABP Framework 2.9.0 before 10.6.2 and 10.7.0 pre-releases before 10.7.0 contain a path traversal vulnerability in Defau…
items.description: ABP Framework 2.9.0 before 10.6.2 and 10.7.0 pre-releases before 10.7.0 contain a path traversal vulnerability in DefaultBlobFilePathCalculator that allows unauthenticated attackers to access files outside the blob container. Attackers can send %5C-encoded backslashes through the Blogging api/blogging/files/{name} endpoint on Windows hosts to read files like appsettings.json containing signing keys and connection strings.

items.title: postal-mime before 4.2.1 contains a parser differential vulnerability in its address parser that truncates the domain a…
items.description: postal-mime before 4.2.1 contains a parser differential vulnerability in its address parser that truncates the domain at folding whitespace or comments preceding a dot. Remote attackers can craft From headers that pass SPF/DKIM/DMARC alignment for their own subdomain while PostalMime.parse() reports a spoofed victim sender address.

items.title: Dolibarr 20.0.0 through 23.0.4 and 24.x before 24.0.2 contains an insecure direct object reference vulnerability in api…
items.description: Dolibarr 20.0.0 through 23.0.4 and 24.x before 24.0.2 contains an insecure direct object reference vulnerability in api_expensereports.class.php payment endpoints that lets authenticated users access other users' expense report payments. Attackers with only expense report read and create rights can call getAllPayments, getPayments, addPayment, or updatePayment to read, create, or modify payments, falsifying reimbursement state.

items.title: When JAX-WS or JAX-RS endpoints are published by the embedded OpenEJB HTTP server rather than Tomcat, some configured a…
items.description: When JAX-WS or JAX-RS endpoints are published by the embedded OpenEJB HTTP server rather than Tomcat, some configured authentication methods are silently ignored and the endpoint is published without authentication. A remote unauthenticated attacker can invoke the exposed operations without credentials. Only deployments that use the embedded HTTP server and rely on such an authentication method are affected. Users are recommended to block network access to the embedded HTTP server from untrusted clients, or to migrate to the Tomcat based TomEE distributions.

items.title: The embedded server generates HTTP session identifiers with a non-cryptographic random number generator by default.
items.description: The embedded server generates HTTP session identifiers with a non-cryptographic random number generator by default. A remote attacker who observes a session identifier can predict the identifiers issued to other users and hijack their sessions, if the application relies on HTTP sessions for authentication. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 10.3.0 or 11.0.0-M2, which fix the issue.

items.title: The Jakarta Security OpenID Connect authentication mechanism generates the state and nonce values with a non-cryptograp…
items.description: The Jakarta Security OpenID Connect authentication mechanism generates the state and nonce values with a non-cryptographic random number generator and insufficient entropy. A remote attacker who predicts these values can forge an authentication callback that logs a victim into the attacker's account, and the replay protection for ID tokens is weakened. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 10.3.0 or 11.0.0-M2, which fix the issue.

items.title: The Jakarta Security LDAP identity store accepts an empty password as valid if the directory server allows unauthentica…
items.description: The Jakarta Security LDAP identity store accepts an empty password as valid if the directory server allows unauthenticated binds, which some directory servers do by default. A remote attacker can then authenticate as any existing user without knowing the password. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 10.3.0 or 11.0.0-M2, which fix the issue.

items.title: With the default configuration and no users defined in the default user database, TomEE silently adds an administrative…
items.description: With the default configuration and no users defined in the default user database, TomEE silently adds an administrative user with a well-known password at startup. A remote attacker can use these credentials to authenticate to web applications that use the default realm and grant access to any authenticated user or to the TomEE administrative role. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 10.3.0 or 11.0.0-M2, which fix the issue.

items.title: In Eclipse Kura versions 5.4.0 through 5.6.2, the Identity REST APIs (identity/v1, and identity/v2 since 5.5.0, provide…
items.description: In Eclipse Kura versions 5.4.0 through 5.6.2, the Identity REST APIs (identity/v1, and identity/v2 since 5.5.0, provided by org.eclipse.kura.rest.identity.provider) do not check identity and permission management requests against the permissions of the requesting identity. An authenticated identity holding the rest.identity permission, but not kura.admin, can assign any permission to any identity, including kura.admin to itself. It can also change the password of, or delete, identities holding more privileges than its own, including administrators, and create or delete permissions. This allows escalation to full administrative privileges and can lock legitimate administrators out of the device. The issue is fixed in Eclipse Kura 5.6.3.

items.title: The optional request routing feature forwards requests to their configured destination without applying the security co…
items.description: The optional request routing feature forwards requests to their configured destination without applying the security constraints of that destination or the protection of the web application's private directories. If a route copies client-controlled parts of the request path into its destination, a remote attacker can reach protected resources or read application configuration and class files. Only installations with such a routing configuration are affected. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 10.3.0 or 11.0.0-M2, which fix the issue.

items.title: The admin service of the standalone OpenEJB server accepts stop requests without any authentication.
items.description: The admin service of the standalone OpenEJB server accepts stop requests without any authentication. Any local user or process able to connect to the admin port can stop the server, leading to denial of service; the admin service is enabled by default in the standalone server and bound to the loopback interface. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 10.3.0 or 11.0.0-M2, which fix the issue.

items.title: When MicroProfile JWT role-based access control is used, the access constraints of JAX-RS resources are not always enfo…
items.description: When MicroProfile JWT role-based access control is used, the access constraints of JAX-RS resources are not always enforced as declared: resources that declare an empty set of allowed roles are accessible to every caller, resource classes that inherit the same method from a common superclass share their constraints, and class-level constraints declared on a superclass are ignored. A remote attacker can invoke resources that should be denied to them, in some configurations without authentication. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 10.3.0 or 11.0.0-M2, which fix the issue.

items.description: After a successful WS-Security UsernameToken authentication, the caller identity stays associated with the worker thread once the request completes when web services are served by the standalone OpenEJB HTTP server. A remote unauthenticated attacker whose request is later processed on the same thread can invoke protected EJB methods with the identity of a previously authenticated user. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 10.3.0 or 11.0.0-M2, which fix the issue.

Users are recommended to block network access to the embedded HTTP server from untrusted clients, or to migrate to the Tomcat based TomEE distributions.

items.title: The development-time LiveReload support listens on all network interfaces without authentication and accepts websocket…
items.description: The development-time LiveReload support listens on all network interfaces without authentication and accepts websocket connections from any origin. A network attacker, or a web page visited by the developer, can observe the names of changed files in the watched folder and the server version, and reach the deployed applications through the additional port. This only affects LiveReload enabled in the embedded Maven plugin. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 10.3.0 or 11.0.0-M2, which fix the issue.

items.title: When resolving security roles of a realm-authenticated caller, the caller's user name is also treated as a role name in…
items.description: When resolving security roles of a realm-authenticated caller, the caller's user name is also treated as a role name in addition to the roles assigned by the realm. An authenticated attacker who can obtain an account whose user name equals a role name, for example through self-registration, is granted that role wherever authorization is evaluated through the Jakarta Authorization policy. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 10.3.0 or 11.0.0-M2, which fix the issue.

items.title: The embedded OpenEJB HTTP server does not isolate HTTP sessions between web applications.
items.description: The embedded OpenEJB HTTP server does not isolate HTTP sessions between web applications. A remote attacker can use a session established in one web application in another one, which then trusts session state set by the first application. Only deployments hosting several web applications on the embedded HTTP server are affected. Users are recommended to block network access to the embedded HTTP server from untrusted clients, or to migrate to the Tomcat based TomEE distributions.

Users are recommended to upgrade to version 10.3.0 or 11.0.0-M2, which fix the issue.

items.description: The JDBC based JAAS login module accepts a login without a password for accounts whose stored password is NULL. Only deployments using this login module with NULL passwords in the user table are affected. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 10.3.0 or 11.0.0-M2, which fix the issue.

items.title: Forge: Certificate signature verified with the issuer's RSA signature scheme
items.description:
### Summary

When verifying a certificate, node-forge chose the RSA padding scheme (PKCS#1 v1.5 or RSASSA-PSS) and PSS parameters from the issuer certificate's own signature algorithm instead of the certificate being verified. A certificate labeled as signed with RSASSA-PSS could pass `verifyCertificateChain()` with a PKCS#1 v1.5 signature. Fixed in node-forge 1.4.1.

### Details

`certificate.verify(child)` in `lib/x509.js` hashes the child's TBSCertificate with the digest of the child's signature algorithm, then calls `_verifySignature()` with the issuer certificate. `_verifySignature()` selected the padding scheme from that certificate's `signatureOid` and `signatureParameters`, so the child was verified with the issuer's own scheme rather than the one the child declares.

As a result, a child certificate whose signature algorithm says RSASSA-PSS was accepted with a PKCS#1 v1.5 signature when the issuer itself was signed with PKCS#1 v1.5. The outer `signatureAlgorithm` field of a certificate is not covered by the signature, so an existing PKCS#1 v1.5 (SHA-256) certificate can be relabeled as RSASSA-PSS and still pass verification. The signature itself must still be made with the issuer's private key over the certificate's contents; no certificate can be forged.

The same cause made correctly signed chains fail: a PKCS#1 v1.5 certificate issued by an RSASSA-PSS-signed certificate, or the reverse, was rejected.

The fix verifies with the child certificate's signature scheme and parameters and the issuer's public key.

### Patches
Fixed in node-forge 1.4.1. Certificate signatures are verified with the scheme of the certificate's own signature algorithm.

### Workarounds
Applications that make decisions based on a certificate's signature algorithm can verify the signature themselves with that algorithm's scheme and the issuer's public key.

### References
- https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc4055#section-3 (RSASSA-PSS signature algorithm in certificates)
- https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5280#section-4.1.1.2 (Certificate signatureAlgorithm)
- https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/347.html (CWE-347: Improper Verification of Cryptographic Signature)

### Severity
CVSS 3.1: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:L/A:N (3.7, Low)
CVSS 4.0 (informational): CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:P/PR:N/UI:N/VC:N/VI:L/VA:N/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N (6.3)
CVSS 4.0 rates this Moderate because its integrity weighting is higher; the severity rating follows CVSS 3.1.

### Credits
Reported by Brian Lee (@hibrian827, Georgia Tech SSLab, Team Atlanta), who also suggested the fix.

### Proof of concept

Create a CA certificate signed with sha256WithRSAEncryption, and a leaf certificate whose signature algorithm fields (outer and in the TBSCertificate) are RSASSA-PSS with SHA-256/MGF1-SHA-256/salt 32, but sign the leaf's TBSCertificate with the CA key using PKCS#1 v1.5 (`caKey.sign(sha256)`).

On 1.4.0, `forge.pki.verifyCertificateChain(forge.pki.createCaStore([ca]), [leaf])` returns `true`, although verifying the leaf's signature with RSASSA-PSS fails. On 1.4.1 it throws "Certificate signature is invalid.".

No private key is needed for the same result: take any certificate signed by the CA with sha256WithRSAEncryption and replace only its outer signatureAlgorithm (outside the signed TBSCertificate) with the RSASSA-PSS identifier above. On 1.4.0 it still verifies and reports `signatureOid` as RSASSA-PSS; on 1.4.1 it is rejected.

Regression tests are in tests/unit/x509.js ("signature scheme of the child certificate").

### Impact

Applications that rely on a certificate's declared signature algorithm, for example a policy that only accepts RSASSA-PSS-signed certificates, can be given a certificate labeled RSASSA-PSS whose signature was verified as PKCS#1 v1.5. The certificate must still have been signed by the trusted issuer's key, so the identity it certifies cannot be forged. There is no confidentiality or availability impact.

items.title: Forge: Incomplete PKCS#7 padding validation in AES/DES CBC and ECB decryption
items.description:
### Summary
`decipher.finish()` in CBC and ECB mode accepted malformed PKCS#7 padding: only the last byte was checked, against a limit of four blocks, so mismatched padding bytes, a zero count and oversized counts were accepted and up to four blocks of plaintext could be silently removed. Fixed in node-forge 1.4.1.

### Details
`modes.cbc.prototype.unpad()` and `modes.ecb.prototype.unpad()` in `lib/cipherModes.js` read the last decrypted byte as the PKCS#7 padding count, rejected it only if it was larger than `blockSize << 2` (64 for AES, 32 for DES), and then removed that many bytes. They did not reject a count of 0 or a count larger than one block, and did not check that every padding byte equals the count, as PKCS#7 (RFC 5652 section 6.3) requires. On the Wycheproof AES-CBC-PKCS5 test vectors, 69 of 144 invalid vectors decrypted successfully.

CBC and ECB without a MAC do not provide integrity: an attacker who can modify ciphertext can already make the final block decrypt to any padding. The effect of this bug is that malformed ciphertext is accepted as valid and that oversized counts silently truncate up to four blocks of plaintext. The fix does not protect against padding oracle attacks; applications that decrypt untrusted CBC data need to authenticate it (for example with an HMAC) or use AES-GCM.

The fix requires a count from 1 to the block size and checks every padding byte. Data with other padding schemes that only use the last byte as the count (ANSI X.923, ISO 10126, XML Encryption) now fails to decrypt with default unpadding; set `decipher.mode.unpad = false` before `finish()` and remove such padding in application code.

#### Patches
Fixed in node-forge 1.4.1. CBC and ECB decryption requires valid PKCS#7 padding.

#### Workarounds
Authenticate CBC/ECB ciphertext before decrypting it, or use AES-GCM. To check padding on 1.4.0, set `decipher.mode.unpad = false` and validate the padding in application code.

#### References
- https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5652#section-6.3 (PKCS#7 content-encryption padding)
- https://github.com/C2SP/wycheproof/blob/master/testvectors_v1/aes_cbc_pkcs5_test.json
- https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/354.html (CWE-354: Improper Validation of Integrity Check Value)

#### Severity
CVSS 3.1: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:L/A:N (3.7, Low)
CVSS 4.0 (informational): CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:P/PR:N/UI:N/VC:N/VI:L/VA:N/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N (6.3)
CVSS 4.0 rates this Moderate because its integrity weighting is higher; the severity rating follows CVSS 3.1.

#### Credits
Reported by Oren Yomtov (@orenyomtov, Fireblocks), @zebbern, and Brian Lee (@hibrian827, Georgia Tech SSLab, Team Atlanta), who also suggested the fix.

### Proof of concept
    var forge = require('node-forge');
    // Wycheproof aes_cbc_pkcs5_test tcId 26: zero padding instead of PKCS#7
    var d = forge.cipher.createDecipher('AES-CBC',
      forge.util.hexToBytes('db4f3e5e3795cc09a073fa6a81e5a6bc'));
    d.start({iv: forge.util.hexToBytes('23468aa734f5f0f19827316ff168e94f')});
    d.update(forge.util.createBuffer(
      forge.util.hexToBytes('aa62606a287476777b92d8e4c4e53028')));
    console.log(d.finish()); // 1.4.0: true; 1.4.1: false

Directly, `unpad()` on 1.4.0 also accepts a final block ending in `03 02 01 04` (removing 4 bytes) and a count of 0x20 on 16-byte blocks (removing 32 bytes).

Regression tests are in tests/unit/aes.js ("PKCS#7 padding checks").

### Impact
Applications that decrypt AES or DES data in CBC or ECB mode and use the result of `decipher.finish()` to decide whether the data is valid could accept malformed ciphertext, with up to four blocks of trailing plaintext removed. This also affects PKCS#7 EncryptedData/EnvelopedData decryption, PKCS#12 and encrypted private keys. Because CBC and ECB without a MAC are malleable, the additional capability given to an attacker is small. There is no confidentiality or availability impact.

items.title: Forge: X.509 pathLenConstraint not enforced by verifyCertificateChain() for CA certificates without keyUsage
items.description:
### Summary
`forge.pki.verifyCertificateChain()` enforces the `pathLenConstraint` of a CA certificate's `basicConstraints` extension only when that certificate also has a `keyUsage` extension. For a CA certificate with a `pathLenConstraint` and no `keyUsage`, chains with more intermediate CA certificates below it than the constraint allows are accepted. Fixed in node-forge 1.4.1.

### Details
In `pki.verifyCertificateChain()` (`lib/x509.js`), the path length check for a CA certificate was guarded by `keyUsageExt !== null && 'pathLenConstraint' in bcExt`. The `keyUsage` test was originally a proxy for "a basicConstraints extension exists". Since node-forge 1.4.0 (GHSA-2328-f5f3-gj25), basicConstraints is required for every certificate that reaches this check, so the only remaining effect of the guard is to skip `pathLenConstraint` enforcement for CA certificates without `keyUsage`.

RFC 5280 permits CA certificates without `keyUsage`, and path length processing in section 6.1.4 (l)-(m) does not depend on `keyUsage`; section 4.2.1.9 defines `pathLenConstraint` as part of basicConstraints only. For example, with a trusted root, an intermediate CA with `pathLenConstraint=0` and no `keyUsage`, a sub-CA issued by that intermediate, and a leaf issued by the sub-CA, node-forge accepts the chain. It correctly rejects the same chain when the intermediate has `keyUsage`.

The fix checks `pathLenConstraint` whenever the basicConstraints extension is present, regardless of `keyUsage` (based on PR #1142).

#### Patches
Fixed in node-forge 1.4.1. `pathLenConstraint` is now enforced for CA certificates without a `keyUsage` extension.

#### Workarounds
None in node-forge itself. Applications that pass an `options.verify` callback to `pki.verifyCertificateChain()` (or `verify` to `forge.tls.createConnection()`) can reject chains in which a CA certificate at `depth` d has `basicConstraints.pathLenConstraint < d - 1`. Re-issuing constrained CA certificates with a `keyUsage` extension that includes `keyCertSign` also restores enforcement.

#### References
- RFC 5280, sections 4.2.1.9 and 6.1.4: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5280#section-6.1.4
- Related: GHSA-2328-f5f3-gj25 / CVE-2026-33896 (basicConstraints bypass, fixed in 1.4.0)
- https://github.com/digitalbazaar/forge/pull/1142

#### Severity
CVSS 3.1: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:H/A:N (5.9, Moderate)
CVSS 4.0 (informational): CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:P/PR:N/UI:N/VC:N/VI:H/VA:N/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N (8.2)
CVSS 4.0 weights the attack preconditions differently and scores this higher; the severity rating follows CVSS 3.1.

#### Credits
@offset, @eddieran, also reported independently by Zion Boggan (@zionboggan) and @EchoSkorJjj.

### Proof of concept
Build the chain root <- int <- subCA <- leaf, where `int` has basicConstraints `cA=true, pathLenConstraint=0` and no `keyUsage`, `subCA` is a CA certificate issued by `int`, and `leaf` is issued by `subCA`:

```js
var caStore = forge.pki.createCaStore([root]);
forge.pki.verifyCertificateChain(caStore, [leaf, subCA, int]);
// <= 1.4.0: true (pathLenConstraint=0 ignored)
// 1.4.1: throws "Certificate basicConstraints pathLenConstraint violated."
```

The same chain is rejected on <= 1.4.0 when `int` also has a `keyUsage` extension with `keyCertSign`. The fix adds regression tests in `tests/unit/x509.js` and the reporter's PoC as `tests/pocs/ghsa-h46v-rmh6-fq4f.js`.

### Impact
Applications that verify certificate chains with `forge.pki.verifyCertificateChain()`, including TLS peer certificate verification in `forge.tls`, are affected when a CA they trust (directly or through a chain) has a `pathLenConstraint` and no `keyUsage` extension.

Exploitation requires such a path-length-constrained CA certificate that chains to a root the application trusts. The attacker must either hold that CA's private key or obtain a CA certificate from it. That CA can then create subordinate CAs, and certificates issued by those subordinate CAs are accepted by `pki.verifyCertificateChain()`. Public web PKI CA certificates normally include `keyUsage`. Private PKIs whose CA certificates were created without `keyUsage` are most likely to be affected.

items.title: Forge: ASN.1 resource exhaustion via BIT STRING decoding in asn1.fromDer
items.description:
### Summary
`asn1.fromDer()` decodes the contents of BIT STRINGs as ASN.1 by default. That decode ignored the `maxDepth` recursion limit (an incomplete fix of CVE-2025-66031) and also decoded nested BIT STRINGs, keeping a full copy of the decoded contents at each level, so small crafted DER or PEM inputs (certificates, keys, PKCS structures) use excessive CPU time and memory and can abort the Node.js process. Fixed in node-forge 1.4.1.

### Details
`asn1.fromDer()` attempts by default to decode the contents of primitive BIT STRINGs as ASN.1 (`decodeBitStrings`, default `true`). Two flaws in that decode in `lib/asn1.js` allow resource exhaustion:

1. `_fromDer()` started the BIT STRING decode with a new options object, `{strict: true, decodeBitStrings: true}`, that did not include `maxDepth`. Inside that decode the depth check compared against `undefined` and never triggered, so the recursion limit added for CVE-2025-66031 (GHSA-554w-wpv2-vw27) was not enforced for anything below a decoded BIT STRING. Both the global `asn1.maxDepth` (default 256) and the per-call `maxDepth` option were ignored there. Errors in this speculative decode, including stack overflows, are caught and the contents kept as raw bytes, so deep nesting is parsed instead of rejected. This is an incomplete fix of CVE-2025-66031.
2. BIT STRINGs nested inside decoded BIT STRING contents were decoded as well, and `asn1.create()` gives each decoded BIT STRING a deep copy of its decoded contents (`obj.original`, used by `toDer()` to detect changes). Memory use therefore grows quadratically with the nesting depth, even within the default depth limit.

No specification is violated; the parser lacks a resource limit.

The fix passes `maxDepth` to the BIT STRING decode, and decodes BIT STRING contents with `decodeBitStrings: false`, so only one level of BIT STRING contents is decoded. Contents that would exceed the limit, and BIT STRINGs inside decoded BIT STRING contents, are kept as undecoded BIT STRING values; `toDer()` writes their original bytes. Common structures such as SubjectPublicKeyInfo only use one level. Code that relied on nested decoding can decode the inner value explicitly with `asn1.fromDer()`.

#### Patches
Fixed in node-forge 1.4.1. The `maxDepth` limit now applies to ASN.1 decoded from BIT STRING contents, and only one level of BIT STRING contents is decoded.

#### Workarounds
Code that calls `forge.asn1.fromDer()` directly and does not need encapsulated BIT STRING contents decoded can pass `{decodeBitStrings: false}`. This changes the parsed structure. The higher-level PKI, PKCS and TLS APIs do not expose this option and rely on the decoded form. For those, the only remedy is upgrading.

#### References
- CVE-2025-66031 / https://github.com/digitalbazaar/forge/security/advisories/GHSA-554w-wpv2-vw27 (ASN.1 Unbounded Recursion, fixed in 1.3.2)
- https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/674.html (CWE-674: Uncontrolled Recursion)
- https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/400.html (CWE-400: Uncontrolled Resource Consumption)

#### Severity
CVSS 3.1: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H (7.5, High)
CVSS 4.0 (informational): CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:N/VI:N/VA:H/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N (8.7)
Both versions rate this High. The severity rating follows CVSS 3.1.

#### Credits
Reported by Ethan Kim (cremit.io), Youngjoon Kim (@acorn421) and Brian Lee (@hibrian827) of Georgia Tech SSLab, @arpitjain099, and Mike Read.

### Proof of concept
Input shape: n nested primitive BIT STRINGs (`03 <len> 00 <inner>`) around a NULL. For example:

    var asn1 = forge.asn1;
    var obj = asn1.create(asn1.Class.UNIVERSAL, asn1.Type.NULL, false, '');
    for(var i = 0; i < 2000; ++i) {
      obj = asn1.create(asn1.Class.UNIVERSAL, asn1.Type.BITSTRING, false, [obj]);
    }
    var der = asn1.toDer(obj).getBytes(); // 9,886 bytes
    asn1.fromDer(der, {maxDepth: 10});

On 1.4.0 (Node.js 24) this parses all 2,000 levels despite `maxDepth: 10`, taking about 0.5-1 s and 600 MB. One SEQUENCE holding 20 such chains (about 198 KB) aborts a process with the default heap with "FATAL ERROR: JavaScript heap out of memory", which the application cannot catch. Within the depth limit, 80 chains of 254 levels (92 KB) still use about 0.8 GB. The same inputs wrapped as PEM reach `pki.publicKeyFromPem()` and `pki.certificateFromPem()` (a 20 KB certificate PEM used 1.3 GB before being rejected). On 1.4.1 these inputs parse in a few milliseconds and about 55-65 MB.

Regression tests in tests/unit/asn1.js: "should limit depth in decoded BIT STRINGs (default)", "should limit depth in decoded BIT STRINGs (maxDepth)", "should only decode one level of BIT STRINGs" and "should not decode BIT STRINGs in many BIT STRINGs".

### Impact
A remote, unauthenticated attacker can supply a small DER or PEM structure with nested BIT STRINGs to any API that parses with `asn1.fromDer()` using default options. This includes `pki.certificateFromPem()`, `pki.publicKeyFromPem()`, the PKCS#7, PKCS#8 and PKCS#12 loaders, and server certificates received by forge's TLS client. Parsing such input consumes excessive CPU time and memory before the structure is rejected. On Node.js 24 a 10 KB input used about 600 MB and a 25 KB input about 1.4 GB. Inputs of about 25 KB abort a process limited to a 512 MB heap, and about 200 KB abort a process with the default heap, with a fatal out-of-memory error that the application cannot catch. Inputs that stay within the depth limit still reach about 0.8 GB at 92 KB and 1.8 GB at 231 KB. The result is denial of service. There is no confidentiality or integrity impact.

items.title: Effect: Cookie attribute injection via domain, path, and name fields in @effect/platform makeCookie()
items.description:
### Impact

The `name`, `domain`, and `path` fields of `makeCookie()` were validated with a regex that allows `;`, the attribute separator in `Set-Cookie` headers. Because `serializeCookie()` writes those fields verbatim, a caller who passes untrusted input into any of them can append arbitrary attributes to the header.

For example, a `domain` of `"legit.com; Domain=.parent.tld"` serializes to `session=token; Domain=legit.com; Domain=.parent.tld`. RFC 6265 §5.3 takes the last occurrence, so the injected domain wins and the cookie widens to the parent domain. The same trick sets `SameSite=None` or `Max-Age` when the caller has not set those options itself.

The `value` field is unaffected: it passes through `encodeURIComponent`, which encodes `;`. CR and LF are rejected by the existing regex, so header splitting is not possible.

### Patches

Fixed in #6763 (v4) and #6765 (v3): the shared regex is split into per-field validators that reject `;`, and `serializeCookie()` now validates before writing the header.

### Workarounds

Do not pass user input into `name`, `domain`, or `path`; set them from application constants.
