GPUStack: Missing authorization on several cluster and resource endpoints allows cross-user access and cluster takeover
items.description:
### Impact

An authenticated non-administrative user could access a Kubernetes cluster they are not authorized to access through GPUStack's Kubernetes API proxy.

The `cluster_apiserver_proxy` handler did not perform a resource-level authorization check before forwarding requests to the selected cluster. Requests were forwarded through a worker using its Kubernetes ServiceAccount credentials.

Depending on the permissions granted to that ServiceAccount, an attacker could read sensitive Kubernetes resources, create or modify workloads, or delete resources and disrupt services. Creating attacker-controlled workloads could result in code execution in the target cluster.

Exploitation requires a Kubernetes-provider cluster with a reachable worker. The operations available to the attacker are limited by the worker's ServiceAccount permissions.

### Patches

Fixed in `gpustack` `v2.2.2`.

### Workarounds

Restrict access to the GPUStack instance to trusted administrator accounts until upgrading.

items.title: GPUStack: SAML callback trusts an unverified SAMLResponse, allowing authentication bypass and account takeover
items.description:
### Impact

The callback Base64-decodes the posted XML, reads NameID and attributes, resolves or provisions the user, and mints a gpustack_session JWT — but never calls OneLogin_Saml2_Auth.process_response(), the step that verifies the signature, issuer, audience, destination, and time conditions.

No credentials are required, and SAML SSO does not even need to be configured. The callback processes the payload and issues a session regardless of whether SAML is set up, so every deployment is affected, not only SAML-enabled ones. Anyone who can reach the endpoint over the network can authenticate as an arbitrary identity by posting a response that names it:

- If the name matches an existing user (e.g. an administrator), the attacker receives that user's session — full account takeover, including administrator access.
- Otherwise, a new non-admin user is provisioned.

Administrator access grants full control over the deployment and the infrastructure it manages. Because Response/Assertion IDs are never consumed, a captured signed response also replays indefinitely.

Precondition: network reachability to /auth/saml/callback. SAML SSO configuration is not required. A full proof-of-concept is available privately to maintainers.


### Patches

Fixed in gpustack 2.2.2:
- The SAML callback now validates the response via OneLogin_Saml2_Auth.process_response() — signature, issuer, audience, destination, and time conditions — and rejects responses that fail, so forged or replayed assertions are no longer accepted.
- The SAML and OIDC login/callback routes are now gated to run only when that provider is the configured active provider, so a deployment that has not enabled the provider no longer parses attacker-supplied IdP payloads.

### Workarounds

There is no effective configuration-level workaround — disabling or not configuring SAML does not mitigate this on affected versions, since the callback runs regardless. Until upgraded, block network access to /auth/saml/callback (e.g. at a reverse proxy / ingress).

### Credit

Reported privately by Austin Chu, Sohee Kim, and Corban Villa (UC Berkeley
security research project), and independently, earlier, by a researcher who wishes to remain anonymous.

items.title: node-opcua: Namespace-Level RBAC Fail-Open - Anonymous Write/Call Bypass via Unbound `DefaultRolePermissions
gopacket: SCTP chunk sub-decoder out-of-bounds panics on crafted segments
items.description:
## Summary

gopacket decodes SCTP (IP protocol 132) by walking the chunk chain through per-chunk-type decoder functions (`decodeSCTPInit`, `decodeSCTPShutdown`, `decodeSCTPError`, `decodeSCTPSack`, in `layers/sctp.go`). Each of these reads fixed-size header fields and runs count-driven loops **without validating the chunk's declared length against the minimums those reads require**. A single crafted SCTP segment causes a runtime panic (out-of-bounds slice read, or inverted slice from unsigned length arithmetic) on any decode path that does not install gopacket's per-packet panic recovery (`gopacket.DecodeOptions.SkipDecodeRecovery: true`); with the default API the same input degrades to a per-packet decode error.

The defect is present in every released version through `v1.7.1` and at current `master` (18c5805). It is the SCTP component named - but not remediated - in CVE-2026-65819 (`GHSA-8mcr-459q-5mx2`, "Multiple layer decoders panic …", patched per advisory metadata in `v1.7.1`). The `v1.7.1` hardening commit `b772f56` ("layers:various: add protocol decoder length checks (#163)") added generic bounds to the chunk dispatcher and `decodeSCTPChunk`, but left every chunk *sub-decoder* without a per-type minimum-length check. The advisory's own description lists "SCTP chunk/parameter decoders (`sctp.go`)" among items "being confirmed; they should be remediated together with the above" - this report demonstrates that, at `v1.7.1` and `HEAD`, that remediation still does not exist.

## Patches

Fixed in **v1.7.2** by commit [`5080443`](https://github.com/gopacket/gopacket/commit/5080443) ("layers/sctp: bound chunk sub-decoders and parameters"). INIT/INIT-ACK, SACK and SHUTDOWN now check their chunk type's minimum length, SACK rejects gap-ack and duplicate-TSN counts the chunk can't hold, and `decodeSCTPParameter` rejects TLV lengths below 4 or beyond the buffer. Each case returns a decode error instead of panicking. The same commit fixes a panic on valid input, where a final parameter's padding lies outside the chunk length (RFC 9260 3.2). Regression tests: `TestDecodeSCTPChunkRegression` and `TestDecodeSCTPParameterPadding` in `layers/decode_oob_test.go`.

Upgrade with `go get github.com/gopacket/gopacket@v1.7.2`.

## Workarounds

Before v1.7.2, keep panic recovery on: use `gopacket.NewPacket` without `SkipDecodeRecovery`, and `DecodingLayerParser` with `IgnorePanic: false`. The crafted packet then fails to decode instead of crashing the process.

## Vulnerability Details

All line numbers refer to `layers/sctp.go` at commit `18c5805028329a6a8944f054d8d3f64ebc0f1373` (master, 2026-09-01; `v1.7.1-1-g18c5805`).

The shared entry point already present in `v1.7.1` validates only that a chunk is present and that its declared length is ≥ 4 and covered by real bytes:

```go
// sctp.go:129
func decodeSCTPChunk(data []byte) (SCTPChunk, error) {
	if len(data) < 4 { ... }
	length := binary.BigEndian.Uint16(data[2:4])
	if length < 4 { ... }
	actual := roundUpToNearest4(int(length))
	ct := SCTPChunkType(data[0])
	if ct == SCTPChunkTypeData && length < 16 { ... }   // only DATA gets a 16-byte minimum
	if len(data) < actual { ... }
	...
```

The Data-chunk minimum of 16 bytes is never applied to the other chunk types, and none of the sub-decoders re-check before indexing. Four independent panic paths result (each reproduced at `HEAD`):

**Defect 1 - INIT / INIT-ACK chunks (`decodeSCTPInit`, sctp.go:423):** reads `data[4:8]`, `data[8:12]` (line 431), `data[12:14]`, `data[14:16]`, `data[16:20]` (line 434), then slices `paramData := data[20:sc.ActualLength]` (line 436).
- Declared length 8–11, actual 8–12 -> `data[8:12]` reads past the chunk:
  `panic: runtime error: slice bounds out of range [:12] with capacity 8`
- Declared length 15, actual 16 -> `data[16:20]` past the chunk:
  `panic: runtime error: slice bounds out of range [:20] with capacity 16`
- Declared length ≤ 19 -> the `data[20:ActualLength]` slice is inverted (panic) or the subsequent parameter loop runs on attacker data without the `decodeSCTPParameter` length check (Defect 3).

**Defect 2 - SHUTDOWN chunks (`decodeSCTPShutdown`, sctp.go:670):** reads `binary.BigEndian.Uint32(data[4:8])` (line 677) on a chunk whose declared length is only validated as ≥ 4:
`panic: runtime error: slice bounds out of range [:8] with capacity 4` (4-byte chunk).

**Defect 3 - ERROR (and HEARTBEAT/INIT) parameter decoder (`decodeSCTPParameter`, sctp.go:193):** the crafted `Length` field is used to slice with no bound against the parameter buffer:

```go
// sctp.go:193
func decodeSCTPParameter(data []byte) SCTPParameter {
	length := binary.BigEndian.Uint16(data[2:4])
	return SCTPParameter{
		...
		Value:        data[4:length],   // line 198: no check length >= 4 or length <= len(data)
		ActualLength: roundUpToNearest4(int(length)),
	}
}
```

- `length < 4` -> inverted slice: `panic: runtime error: slice bounds out of range [4:0]` (reached from `decodeSCTPError` line 632 `paramData := data[4:sc.Length]`, and from the INIT (438) / HEARTBEAT (578) parameter loops).
- `length > len(data)` -> slice-bounds-check panic (Go's slice bounds check panics; the read never silently over-reads).

**Defect 4 - SACK chunk count loops (`decodeSCTPSack`, sctp.go:484):** `NumGapACKs` / `NumDuplicateTSNs` (attacker-controlled uint16 fields) drive loops that slice the remaining bytes with no bound:

```go
// sctp.go:512
bytesRemaining := data[16:]
for i := 0; i < int(sc.NumGapACKs); i++ {                       // line 513
	sc.GapACKs = append(sc.GapACKs, binary.BigEndian.Uint16(bytesRemaining[:2]))  // line 514
	bytesRemaining = bytesRemaining[2:]
}
for i := 0; i < int(sc.NumDuplicateTSNs); i++ {                 // line 517
	sc.DuplicateTSNs = append(sc.DuplicateTSNs, binary.BigEndian.Uint32(bytesRemaining[:4]))  // line 518
	bytesRemaining = bytesRemaining[4:]
}
```

A 16-byte SACK chunk declaring `NumGapACKs = 1` with no following bytes:
`panic: runtime error: slice bounds out of range [:2] with capacity 0`

Note this is not the sFlow/Diameter "unbounded allocation" family already covered by CVE-2026-54332/CVE-2026-54345; the SACK `make()` capacities are already capped against `ActualLength` (lines 505–510) - the *loop iteration counts* are not, so the panic is an out-of-bounds read, not an allocation.

**History / version range.** `decodeSCTPInit` and the chunk sub-decoders were introduced in commit `2fca351` (original full-featured SCTP implementation; at the time the file was named `layer_sctp.go` - the current `sctp.go` path dates from the rename in `dea6b39`). The sinks are present in every release from v1.0.0 through v1.7.1 and at `HEAD` (also confirmed at v1.6.0). `b772f56` (2026-07-08, included in v1.7.1) touched `layers/sctp.go` but only hardened the dispatcher (`decodeWithSCTPChunkTypePrefix`) and the generic `decodeSCTPChunk`/`decodeSCTPDataChunk` bounds; the four sub-decoder paths above are unchanged by it. The v1.7.1 regression-test commit `2220269` covers the advisory's other decoders, not SCTP chunk sub-decoders. Affected range is therefore every gopacket version: `<= 1.7.1`, plus current master `18c5805`. *(Maintainer update: fixed in v1.7.2, commit `5080443`; see Patches.)*

**Relationship to the published advisory (dedup context).** CVE-2026-65819 / GHSA-8mcr-459q-5mx2 (published 2026-07-27) declares `vulnerable_version_range: <= 1.7.0` / `patched_versions: 1.7.1`. Its description explicitly names "SCTP chunk/parameter decoders (`sctp.go`)" among decoder families "(on the recovering path only) … being confirmed; they should be remediated together with the above". Because the advisory metadata tells consumers that upgrading to 1.7.1 remediates the advisory, and this SCTP component was not actually fixed, the practical status of this finding is *incomplete remediation of a published advisory*: consumers of the 1.7.1 "patched" version remain exposed to the SCTP panic path. The finding is reported here so the maintainers can either complete the SCTP fix under the existing advisory or track it separately.

## Impact

An unauthenticated remote attacker can crash a gopacket-based decoder with a single crafted SCTP segment (IP protocol 132). A 54-byte Ethernet frame (`Ethernet -> IPv4 -> SCTP` with an 8-byte INIT chunk) is enough (see Reproduction Steps). Panic escapes for consumers that disable gopacket's built-in recovery:

- `gopacket.NewPacket(data, layerType, DecodeOptions{SkipDecodeRecovery: true})` - panic propagates to the caller, terminating the process if uncaught.
- Direct use of the registered SCTP decode chain without recovery.

Two gopacket entry points install recovery by default and are therefore NOT crash surfaces for this bug: `gopacket.NewPacket` with default options (deferred `recover` wraps the whole decode chain, converting the panic into a per-packet error, demonstrated in case B below), and `DecodingLayerParser.DecodeLayers` when `IgnorePanic` is false (`parser.go:306` - `if !l.IgnorePanic { defer panicToError(&err) }`); in both cases the packet simply fails to decode. Panic escape - and process crash - requires the non-recovering settings above. This mirrors exactly the reachability of the sibling advisories in the same family (GHSA-6h9g MPTCP, GHSA-8mcr): CVE-2026-65819 itself is scored with the same `AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N` vector while noting (per the GHSA advisory text) ~5.3 (Medium) for recovering-path-only consumers; the reporter scored the non-recovering consumer set at 7.5, which is the configuration used by high-throughput packet-analysis engines that set `SkipDecodeRecovery` to detect decode failures themselves.

The default API (`gopacket.NewPacket(..., gopacket.Default)`) installs `defer recover` and converts the panic into a per-packet decode error, so crash exposure is limited to non-recovering consumers (packet-analysis engines, IDS/NDR pipelines, capture-processing tools that set `SkipDecodeRecovery` or call decoders directly - the same consumer set described in the CVE-2026-65819 and CVE-2026-54332/54345 advisories).

Impact is availability only: no memory disclosure, no code execution, no allocation amplification. Severity: **CVSS 3.1 5.9 Medium - `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H`** (reporter proposed 7.5 with AC:L; maintainers set AC:H because a crash needs the consumer to disable panic recovery), primary **CWE-125** (out-of-bounds read), secondaries CWE-129 (improper validation of array index for the inverted slices).

Per-metric justification (primary vector):
- **Attack Vector (AV): Network** - a single crafted SCTP segment (IP protocol 132) delivered over the wire triggers the panic path; no local access needed.
- **Attack Complexity (AC): High** - the input is trivial (a 54-byte frame with an 8-byte INIT chunk), but a crash depends on a condition outside the attacker's control: the target must have disabled gopacket's panic recovery. Default configurations only produce a decode error.
- **Privileges Required (PR): None** - the decoding library processes untrusted captured/live packets with no authentication.
- **User Interaction (UI): None** - no victim action; the crash occurs during automated decode.
- **Scope (S): Unchanged** - the impacted security authority is the decoder's own process (the caller's application).
- **Confidentiality (C): None** - no data disclosure.
- **Integrity (I): None** - no data modification.
- **Availability (A): High** - non-recovering consumer process terminates (panic); the ~5.3 recovering-path-only alternative is disclosed above.

## Reproduction Steps

Environment: Go 1.25 toolchain (module requires `go 1.25.0`), `github.com/gopacket/gopacket` at `HEAD` 18c5805028329a6a8944f054d8d3f64ebc0f1373 (v1.7.1 + 1 commit). The same output is produced at tag `v1.7.1`.

```go
// repro_sctp.go - single static input, one deterministic observable (decode panic)
package main

import (
	"fmt"

	"github.com/gopacket/gopacket"
	"github.com/gopacket/gopacket/layers"
)

func main() {
	// One 54-byte frame: Ethernet -> IPv4(proto 132) -> SCTP -> INIT chunk (declared length 8)
	frame := []byte{
		// Ethernet
		0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0x00, 0x11, 0x22, 0x33, 0x44, 0x55, 0x08, 0x00,
		// IPv4, protocol 132 (SCTP), total length 40
		0x45, 0x00, 0x00, 0x28, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x84, 0x00, 0x84,
		0x0a, 0x00, 0x00, 0x01, 0x0a, 0x00, 0x00, 0x02,
		// SCTP common header (12 bytes)
		0x11, 0x11, 0x22, 0x22, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00,
		// INIT chunk: type=1, flags=0, length=8 (declared), body 4 bytes
		0x01, 0x00, 0x00, 0x08, 0xaa, 0xbb, 0xcc, 0xdd,
	}
	// same bytes as hex:
	// ffffffffffff00112233445508004500002800000000008400840a0000010a000002
	// 1111222200000000000000000100000008aabbccdd

	// A) Non-recovering decode (SkipDecodeRecovery: true) -> panic escapes
	func() {
		defer func() {
			if r := recover(); r != nil {
				fmt.Printf("A) SkipDecodeRecovery=true  -> PANIC: %v\n", r)
			}
		}()
		p := gopacket.NewPacket(frame, layers.LayerTypeEthernet,
			gopacket.DecodeOptions{Lazy: false, SkipDecodeRecovery: true})
		_ = p.Dump()
		fmt.Println("A) no panic (unexpected)")
	}()

	// B) Default (recovering) API -> per-packet error, process survives
	p := gopacket.NewPacket(frame, layers.LayerTypeEthernet, gopacket.Default)
	fmt.Printf("B) Default (recovering)    -> err=%v  layers=%d\n", p.ErrorLayer(), len(p.Layers()))
}
```

Build and run (module file `go.mod`):

```
module repro

go 1.25.0

require github.com/gopacket/gopacket v1.7.1

replace github.com/gopacket/gopacket => /path/to/clone/of/gopacket/gopacket  # at 18c5805 (or tag v1.7.1)
```

```
$ go build -o repro_sctp repro_sctp.go
$ ./repro_sctp
A) SkipDecodeRecovery=true  -> PANIC: runtime error: slice bounds out of range [:12] with capacity 8
B) Default (recovering)    -> err=Packet decoding error: runtime error: slice bounds out of range [:12] with capacity 8  layers=4
```

Observed stack (case A): `layers.decodeSCTPInit` at `layers/sctp.go:431` <- `SCTPChunkType.Decode` <- `decodeWithSCTPChunkTypePrefix` (`sctp.go:57`) <- `decodeSCTP` (`sctp.go:38`) <- `NewPacket`.

Additional one-input repros for the other three defect classes (same harness shape, decode root `LayerTypeSCTP` with `SkipDecodeRecovery: true`):

| Input | Panic (observed) | Sink |
|---|---|---|
| INIT-ACK chunk type 2, declared length 8 | `slice bounds out of range [:12] with capacity 8` | sctp.go:431 |
| INIT chunk declared length 15, 12-byte body | `slice bounds out of range [:20] with capacity 16` | sctp.go:434 |
| SACK chunk type 3, length 16, `NumGapACKs=1`, `NumDuplicateTSNs=1`, no trailing bytes | `slice bounds out of range [:2] with capacity 0` | sctp.go:514 |
| SHUTDOWN chunk type 7, declared length 4 | `slice bounds out of range [:8] with capacity 4` | sctp.go:677 |
| ERROR chunk type 9, length 8, 4-byte "parameter" with Length field 0 | `slice bounds out of range [4:0]` | sctp.go:198 |

## Recommendations

Complete the `v1.7.1` remediation by validating each chunk subtype's declared length against the fixed-size fields and loops that consume it, immediately after `decodeSCTPChunk` succeeds in each sub-decoder. Minimal correct changes in `layers/sctp.go`:

1. **`decodeSCTPInit`**: require `sc.ActualLength >= 20` before reading `data[4:20]` (return a decode error otherwise), then bound the parameter loop: `paramData := data[20:sc.ActualLength]` is safe once the chunk length is ≥ 20 *and* `decodeSCTPParameter` is hardened (below).
2. **`decodeSCTPShutdown`**: require `sc.ActualLength >= 8`.
3. **`decodeSCTPSack`**: require `sc.ActualLength >= 16`, and cap the loops - iterate `min(NumGapACKs, remaining/2)` and `min(NumDuplicateTSNs, remaining/4)`, returning an error (or silently stopping with `SetTruncated`) when a count exceeds the bytes available.
4. **`decodeSCTPParameter`** (shared by INIT/HEARTBEAT/ERROR): reject `length < 4` and `length > len(data)` before the `data[4:length]` slice, mirroring the bound style already used for TCP options (`tcp.go` `default` branch) - this closes Defect 3 at its root regardless of which loop calls it.

Optionally add regression tests in the style of `2220269` covering short INIT/SHUTDOWN/SACK/ERROR chunks.

## Resources

- Source at pin: `layers/sctp.go` @ https://github.com/gopacket/gopacket/blob/18c5805028329a6a8944f054d8d3f64ebc0f1373/layers/sctp.go (lines 129–136 dispatcher/chunk guard, 193–202 `decodeSCTPParameter`, 423–442 `decodeSCTPInit`, 484–521 `decodeSCTPSack`, 670–678 `decodeSCTPShutdown`, 623–636 `decodeSCTPError`)

- Regression-test commit: https://github.com/gopacket/gopacket/commit/2220269 (v1.7.1, "test(layers): add regression tests for the decoder panic advisories")

items.title: Stateful session bean identifiers are not generated from a cryptographically secure random source.
items.description: Stateful session bean identifiers are not generated from a cryptographically secure random source. A remote attacker with access to the EJB remote endpoint who holds one valid identifier can derive those of other clients' sessions and invoke methods on their beans, exposing or modifying other users' session state. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 10.3.0 or 11.0.0-M2, which fix the issue.

items.title: Docker Desktop before version 4.94.0 could write the signed-in user's Docker Hub access token (a JWT) in cleartext to a…
items.description: Docker Desktop before version 4.94.0 could write the signed-in user's Docker Hub access token (a JWT) in cleartext to application logs and diagnostics bundles. IPC payloads that were bare JSON strings or arrays were not redacted before logging, and a Docker Desktop component logged the token when it requested it from the backend. An attacker with read access to these files could obtain the token and use it to read and modify the user's Docker Hub data as that user while the token remains valid. Docker Desktop 4.94.0 redacts these payloads. The fix does not rewrite logs written by earlier versions, which can still contain tokens after upgrading.

items.title: A flaw was found in Podman.
items.description: A flaw was found in Podman. An attacker can trigger a Denial of Service (DoS) by supplying a container image containing crafted metadata labels. Podman's auto-update mechanism improperly trusts these image labels to determine which system services to restart. If a user runs the malicious container and auto-update processes it, arbitrary system services are restarted with the user's privileges, potentially allowing an attacker to shut down the host system when Podman runs with administrative privileges.

items.title: In Eclipse Kura versions 5.0.0 through 5.6.2, the Wire Graph update functionality of the Kura Web UI, and the Wire Serv…
items.description: In Eclipse Kura versions 5.0.0 through 5.6.2, the Wire Graph update functionality of the Kura Web UI, and the Wire Service REST API v1 (available since 5.1.0, org.eclipse.kura.rest.wire.provider), determine whether a configuration update targets a Wire Component, Driver or Asset from the factory identifier supplied in the request, instead of the actual factory of the existing component. An authenticated identity holding only the Wires management permission (kura.wires.admin for the Web UI, rest.wires.admin for the REST API) can therefore modify the configuration of existing components that are not part of the Wire Graph, including security-relevant ones, or replace existing components. The issue is fixed in Eclipse Kura 5.6.3.

items.title: Eclipse Kura downloads deployment packages (DPs) from a remote URL without any limit on the size of the data it receive…
items.description:
Eclipse Kura downloads deployment packages (DPs) from a remote URL without any limit on the size of the data it receives. A malicious or compromised HTTP(S) server, or an attacker able to tamper with a plain-HTTP download, can stream an arbitrarily large (or endless) response. Kura writes the response to local storage until the filesystem is full. On gateways the temporary directory is often a RAM-backed tmpfs, so this can also exhaust memory. The result is denial of service of the device: failed configuration persistence, failed logging and possible crashes of the framework or other services.



The same missing size limit is present in the REST upload endpoint `POST /deploy/v2/_upload`, which copies the request body to the temporary directory with no limit.



Workarounds: only install DPs from trusted HTTPS sources, restrict who can install packages (Web UI `kura.packages.admin` permission, REST `kura.permission.rest.deploy`, cloud DEPLOY-V2 access).

items.title: The Jakarta Security LDAP identity store does not neutralize special characters in the caller name before using it in d…
items.description: The Jakarta Security LDAP identity store does not neutralize special characters in the caller name before using it in directory queries. A remote unauthenticated attacker can alter the queries to enumerate accounts, infer directory attribute values, or influence which directory entry the login is validated against. Only applications using the LDAP identity store are affected. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 10.3.0 or 11.0.0-M2, which fix the issue.

items.title: V programming language standard library net.http through version 0.5.2 prior to commit 4077484 contains a TLS certifica…
items.description: V programming language standard library net.http through version 0.5.2 prior to commit 4077484 contains a TLS certificate validation bypass vulnerability that allows on-path attackers to intercept HTTPS traffic by exploiting the default false value of SSLConnectConfig.validate and FetchConfig.validate, which completes TLS handshakes without verifying certificates in both the mbedtls and OpenSSL backends. Attackers can present an expired, self-signed, wrong-hostname, or untrusted-root certificate to successfully complete the handshake via http.get, http.post, or http.fetch, enabling interception or modification of HTTPS traffic unless validate: true is explicitly configured.

items.title: Summary Cloudflare tokio-quiche was found to contain an uncontrolled resource consumption vulnerability in its HTTP/3 D…
items.description:
Summary


Cloudflare tokio-quiche was found to contain an uncontrolled resource consumption vulnerability in its HTTP/3 DATAGRAM handling. For every previously unseen flow identifier (quarter stream ID) received in a DATAGRAM frame, tokio-quiche creates and retains new, per-flow state. A remote peer can send DATAGRAMs with many distinct identifiers, causing the per-connection flow map and associated channel state to grow without bound.

Impact


Exploitation can exhaust process memory and cause a denial of service. The vulnerable code is used in both client and server configurations, so either role can be affected by a malicious peer. QUIC DATAGRAM support in tokio-quiche is enabled by default through QuicSettings::enable_dgram; applications can disable it by setting this field to false. The vulnerable HTTP/3 path is reachable only when DATAGRAM support is negotiated with the peer. Core quiche and HTTP/3 deployments without DATAGRAM support are not affected. 






Mitigation


Disable DATAGRAMs in tokio-quiche’s QuicSettings::enable_dgram.






Remediation


Upgrade to tokio-quiche version 0.23.0 or later. The fixed code creates flow state only for valid DATAGRAM-capable request streams, which are bounded by QUIC’s stream limits. To tolerate packet reordering, servers retain early DATAGRAMs in a bounded, expiring buffer, while clients discard DATAGRAMs for unknown flows.

items.title: The sourcecache expansion module in MISP Modules (misp-modules) contains a Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) vulnerabi…
items.description: The sourcecache expansion module in MISP Modules (misp-modules) contains a Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) vulnerability. When a user with permission to create or modify attributes of type 'link' or 'url' submits an attribute value, the module passes the URL directly to its internal archiving function without any validation of the target address. An attacker can therefore craft a URL pointing to loopback addresses (e.g., 127.0.0.1), private network ranges, link-local addresses, or cloud metadata endpoints (e.g., 169.254.169.254). The MISP server will issue an HTTP request to that target and store the response body in the event, effectively exfiltrating data from internal services to the attacker through the MISP interface. Non-HTTP schemes such as file:// are also accepted, potentially allowing local file disclosure. The vulnerability requires an authenticated MISP user with the ability to create or edit attributes of the affected types. The security impact is information disclosure from internal services reachable by the MISP server, including sensitive data such as cloud credentials, internal application data, or local files.

items.description: A flaw was found in BusyBox. Successful exploitation may allow an attacker to execute arbitrary code or crash the application, resulting in a denial of service (DoS).

items.title: The Vaadin Rich Text Editor exports a video embed without escaping its value, and then parses the resulting HTML into l…
items.description:
The Vaadin Rich Text Editor exports a video embed without escaping its value, and then parses the resulting HTML into live DOM. A value crafted to break out of the href attribute therefore runs script in the viewer's browser. An attacker who can edit shared content pastes a video embed carrying the payload, the delta is stored, and the script runs when any user opens the page, including in read only mode.

Only content persisted through asDelta() is affected. The default HTML value, set and read through setValue and getValue, is sanitized on the server with a safelist that has no iframe, so the embed does not survive that path. Vaadin 24 and older are not affected: they build the HTML value from the editor's own innerHTML, which the browser escapes.

Users of affected versions should apply the following mitigation or upgrade. Releases that have fixed this issue include:

Product version
Vaadin 25.0.0 - 25.0.13
Vaadin 25.1.0 - 25.1.13
Vaadin 25.2.0 - 25.2.12
Vaadin 25.3.0 - 25.3.4

Mitigation
No fixed release on this line, upgrade to 25.2.13 or newer
No fixed release on this line, upgrade to 25.2.13 or newer
Upgrade to 25.2.13
Upgrade to 25.3.5

items.title: DownloadEvent.setFileName(String) in Vaadin Flow writes the download file name into the Content-Disposition header with…
items.description:
DownloadEvent.setFileName(String) in Vaadin Flow writes the download file name into the Content-Disposition header without escaping it. When the name is pure US-ASCII the header is built as attachment; filename="<name>" with the name inserted verbatim, so a double quote in the name ends the quoted string early and the rest of the name is read by the browser as further header parameters. The inline(String) variant, present from Vaadin 25.0, builds the name the same way. An application that passes an untrusted file name to either method, for example when re-serving a file under the name it was uploaded with, lets an attacker add a filename* parameter. Browsers prefer filename* over filename, so the file is saved under a name and extension of the attacker's choosing, which defeats any file name or extension restriction the application enforces. The attacker cannot change the attachment or inline disposition itself and cannot split the header.

Users of affected versions should apply the following mitigation or upgrade. Releases that have fixed this issue include:

Product version
Vaadin 24.8.0 - 24.8.17
Vaadin 24.9.0 - 24.9.25
Vaadin 24.10.0 - 24.10.13
Vaadin 25.0.0 - 25.0.13
Vaadin 25.1.0 - 25.1.13
Vaadin 25.2.0 - 25.2.12
Vaadin 25.3.0 - 25.3.4

Mitigation
No fixed release on this line, upgrade to 24.9.26 or newer
Upgrade to 24.9.26
Upgrade to 24.10.14
No fixed release on this line, upgrade to 25.2.13 or newer
No fixed release on this line, upgrade to 25.2.13 or newer
Upgrade to 25.2.13
Upgrade to 25.3.5

Vaadin versions below 24.8 are not affected: the DownloadEvent API does not exist in them.

items.title: Improperly Controlled Modification of Dynamically-Determined Object Attributes vulnerability in the device API, device…
items.description:
Improperly Controlled Modification of Dynamically-Determined Object Attributes vulnerability in the device API, device forms, signing key and product forms and JITP settings in nerves-hub nerves_hub_web allows an authenticated user who manages devices in any organization to write into other organizations via submitted org_id, product_id and deployment_id fields. The device API create and update actions and the dashboard device forms pass the request parameters to NervesHub.Devices.Device.changeset/2, which casts the organization, product, deployment group and update state as given. The signing key and product forms merge the session's organization into the submitted parameters so that a submitted org_id wins, and the JITP changeset accepts any product_id. Each request requires the manage role only in the user's own organization, and any account can create one.

A device placed on another organization's deployment group, or moved into its product, is sent that organization's firmware with a download URL. The user cannot change or control devices that already belong to the other organization, and cannot upload firmware to it.

This issue affects nerves_hub: from 1.0.0 before 2.5.3.

items.title: Improper Authentication vulnerability in Google sign-in and email confirmation in nerves-hub nerves_hub_web allows an a…
items.description:
Improper Authentication vulnerability in Google sign-in and email confirmation in nerves-hub nerves_hub_web allows an attacker who registers another person's email address to share that person's account once they sign in. NervesHub.Accounts.update_or_create_user_from_ueberauth/1 signs a Google user in to any account carrying the same email that is not yet linked to a Google account, links it and marks the email confirmed, without the account's owner ever having proved they own the address. NervesHubWeb.SessionController.confirm/2 likewise signs in whoever follows a confirmation link. An attacker registers the address from the sign-up form, changes their own account's email to it, or registers it as an organization admin from an invite link, and keeps the password; when the address's owner signs in with Google or follows the confirmation link, they land in that account.

The Google path also creates accounts with registrations closed and never checks Google's email_verified claim, and the API's password sign-in in NervesHubWeb.API.UserController issues tokens to accounts whose email was never confirmed. The attacker gains only what the victim is granted afterwards, and nothing on accounts whose owners never use either path.

This issue affects nerves_hub: from 2.3.0 before 2.5.3.

items.title: Improper Session Invalidation vulnerability in the dashboard pages, device console and local shell channels in nerves-h…
items.description:
Improper Session Invalidation vulnerability in the dashboard pages, device console and local shell channels in nerves-hub nerves_hub_web allows an organization member who is removed or given a lower role to keep acting at their old role through anything they had open at the time. The dashboard reads the member's role once when a page mounts, in the assign_org_to_scope hook of NervesHubWeb.Auth, and the console, local shell and device event stream channels check membership once at join. Removing a member or changing their role tells none of them, so open pages keep carrying out actions and open consoles keep running commands on the device until the page reloads or the socket disconnects.

The dashboard also opens consoles over NervesHubWeb.UserSocket with a token that holds only the user's id, is accepted for 24 hours, and is not revoked by signing out, which disconnects only the session's LiveViews. Whoever holds a token taken from a page can open consoles as that user, within the user's current membership, until it expires.

This issue affects nerves_hub: from 1.0.0 before 2.5.3.

items.title: Incorrect Authorization vulnerability in the devices page bulk move in nerves-hub nerves_hub_web allows an authenticate…
items.description:
Incorrect Authorization vulnerability in the devices page bulk move in nerves-hub nerves_hub_web allows an authenticated user with the manage role in one organization and only the view role in another to move devices into the second organization's product via the "Move device(s) to product" action. The target-product event in NervesHubWeb.Live.Devices.Index looks the product up with NervesHub.Products.get_by_id/2, which checks that the user is a member of the product's organization at any role, and move-devices-product then changes each selected device's organization and product. The device API's move requires manage in the target organization, and an earlier fix added the check on the organization the devices leave but not on the one they enter.

A moved device keeps its key and certificate, joins the target organization's matching deployment groups, and is sent their firmware with a download URL, which the view role cannot otherwise obtain. The user cannot change or control devices that already belong to the other organization.

This issue affects nerves_hub: from 1.0.0 before 2.5.3.

items.title: Missing Authorization vulnerability in the device and deployment group pages in nerves-hub nerves_hub_web allows an aut…
items.description:
Missing Authorization vulnerability in the device and deployment group pages in nerves-hub nerves_hub_web allows an authenticated organization member with the view role to change devices and deployment groups via LiveView events reserved for the manage role. The event handlers that add and delete device certificates, add and remove tags, overwrite or clear a device's manual location, remove a device from its deployment group, move matched devices into a deployment group or remove unmatched ones, import devices from a CSV, and start, retry or delete firmware delta builds carry out the change without calling authorized!/2, and the pages render the controls to every member.

A view member can add a certificate that lets whoever holds its key connect as the device, delete a certificate so the device can no longer authenticate with it, and change which deployment group, and so which firmware release, a device receives. Everything stays within the organizations the member belongs to.

This issue affects nerves_hub: from 1.0.0 before 2.5.3.

items.title: Session Fixation vulnerability in the CLI login flow in nerves-hub nerves_hub_web allows an unauthenticated attacker to…
items.description:
Session Fixation vulnerability in the CLI login flow in nerves-hub nerves_hub_web allows an unauthenticated attacker to obtain an API token for another user's account via a crafted login link. Starting a CLI login with POST /api/auth/cli_session needs no authentication and returns a polling token, a confirmation URL that carries that token, and a confirmation code. When a signed-in user opens that URL and clicks Confirm, NervesHub.Accounts.verify_cli_session_token/2 creates an API token for the user's account and stores it on the login, and the next poll of GET /api/auth/cli_session/<token> returns it to whoever started the login.

The confirmation code is only displayed and is never compared with anything, so it cannot show that the person confirming is the one who started the login. The confirm form carries a CSRF token and the page cannot be framed, so the attacker has to persuade the user to open the link and click the button themselves.

items.description: The agent_memory module accepts a caller-supplied tenant parameter in create_client(tenant=...). items.title: The WPML Multilingual CMS plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Authentication Bypass via Race Condition in versions up…
items.description: The WPML Multilingual CMS plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Authentication Bypass via Race Condition in versions up to, and including, 4.9.7. This is due to the `process_iframe_request` function's language-per-domain SSO handler generating the cross-domain sign-in token via `wp_create_nonce('wpml_sso')` on the logout landing page, where the browser has already discarded its authentication cookies — so `wp_get_session_token()` returns an empty string and the token collapses to the shared anonymous nonce for the current 12-hour tick rather than a user-bound secret — and then storing it in the `wpml_sso_user_<token>_<sha256('wpml_sso'.$domain)>` transient mapped to the victim's `user_id` with no binding to the specific sign-out action or requesting client. Because an unauthenticated attacker can independently derive the identical token by triggering the logout confirmation flow on `wp-login.php?action=logout`, and because the `is_iframe_request()` gate conditions (the per-domain SSO `started` transient and domain-hash derived from the public constant `SSO_NONCE`) are fully computable within the 60-second `SSO_TIMEOUT` window, an unauthenticated attacker can submit the forged `wpml_sso_token_domain` parameter with a `wpml_user_signed_in` status to a secondary language-domain endpoint before the legitimate `wpml_user_signed_out` iframe fires, causing WordPress authentication cookies to be issued for the victim. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to gain access to accounts of users — including administrators — who are actively in the process of logging out during the race window.

items.title: The Avada (Fusion) Builder plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via Form Notification Dyna…
items.description: The Avada (Fusion) Builder plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via Form Notification Dynamic-Data action_hook → Media Upload Chain (ID3 Metadata / html_attributes) in all versions up to, and including, 3.16.1 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Exploitation requires that a Fusion Form is embedded on an admin-authored page (granting manage_options context to the Dynamic Data action hook callback), and that a Post Cards element configured to display attachment post types is present on a publicly accessible page so the planted shortcode payload is rendered.

items.title: The Everest Forms – Contact Form, Payment Form, Quiz, Survey & Custom Form Builder with AI plugin for WordPress is vuln…

items.description: The SAP Cloud SDK for Python contains an improper cryptographic signature verification vulnerability (CWE-347) in IASContextProvider, the runtime-context provider registered by default via bootstrap(app).IASContextProvider extracted the app_tid, sap_gtid and user_uuid claims from the IAS JWT in the Authorization header using an unverified decoder and wrote them into the request-scoped RuntimeContext without validating the token signature. items.title: The Node.js web service on VOS (previously Versa FlexVNF) is used for URL-based Zero Touch Provisioning (ZTP) of the VO…
items.description:
The Node.js web service on VOS (previously Versa FlexVNF) is used for URL-based Zero Touch Provisioning (ZTP) of the VOS appliance and is not required after provisioning is complete. This service generates session identifiers using UUID version 1 (UUIDv1), which is derived from the system’s date and time and its MAC address. As a result, successive identifiers differ only slightly and can be predicted. An attacker who can predict a user’s session ID could hijack that user’s session. 

Versa’s security hardening guide for Hubs, Branches, and Controllers recommends disabling the Node.js web service after the initial provisioning of the VOS device. This vulnerability is not exploitable on VOS devices where the Node.js web service has been disabled.

items.title: The Node.js web service on VOS (previously Versa FlexVNF) is used for URL-based Zero Touch Provisioning (ZTP) of the VO…

This service authenticates users and administrators to its web interface during initial provisioning using default credentials and HTTP Basic Authentication. An attacker with network access who knows the default credentials could authenticate to the service and perform provisioning actions on the VOS appliance.

items.title: The Node.js web service on VOS (previously Versa FlexVNF) is used for URL-based Zero Touch Provisioning (ZTP) of the VO…
items.description:
The Node.js web service on VOS (previously Versa FlexVNF) is used for URL-based Zero Touch Provisioning (ZTP) of the VOS appliance and is not required after provisioning is complete. The express-session middleware in server.js is configured with a hardcoded secret that is identical across all VOS appliances and is used to sign session cookies. An attacker who obtains a valid session ID from any source can compute the correct HMAC-SHA256 signature and forge a session cookie that the server accepts as legitimate. Because the secret is shared across all VOS appliances, a forged cookie is accepted by any VOS appliance in the deployment. 

Versa’s security hardening guide for Hubs, Branches, and Controllers recommends disabling the Node.js web service after the initial provisioning of the VOS device. This vulnerability is not exploitable on VOS devices where the Node.js web service has been disabled.

items.title: The Node.js web service on VOS (previously Versa FlexVNF) is used for URL-based Zero Touch Provisioning (ZTP) of the VO…
items.description:
The Node.js web service on VOS (previously Versa FlexVNF) is used for URL-based Zero Touch Provisioning (ZTP) of the VOS appliance and is not required after provisioning is complete. The /decryptTest endpoint of this service is registered in server.js before the session authentication middleware and creates an authenticated session whenever it receives a token that decrypts successfully. Because the key and initialization vector (IV) used for decryption are hardcoded and identical across all VOS appliances, an unauthenticated attacker with network access can compute a valid token, submit it to /decryptTest, and obtain a fully authenticated session without providing any credentials.  

Versa’s security hardening guide for Hubs, Branches, and Controllers recommends disabling the Node.js web service after the initial provisioning of the VOS device. This vulnerability is not exploitable on VOS devices where the Node.js web service has been disabled.

items.title: Versa has confirmed a buffer overflow vulnerability in the IPsec implementation on VOS, aka Versa FlexVNF.
items.description:
Versa has confirmed a buffer overflow vulnerability in the IPsec implementation on VOS, aka Versa FlexVNF. 
 
 Buffer Overflow Vulnerability Description 
 
When a maliciously crafted IKE Auth packet is sent to VOS, the vsmd process crashes, thereby resulting in a Denial of Service. An attacker can create a Denial-of-Service attack on the VOS appliances by crafting a malicious IKE Auth packet and sending it to the WAN interfaces on the VOS. 
 
During the IKE Authentication phase, if the IKE SA negotiation fails, and the size of the Remote ID is larger than the buffer size used to process the Remote ID, it will result in a crash of the vsmd process on the VOS appliance. 
 
What is impacted? 
 
VOS nodes configured with IPsec VPN profiles of type controller-staging-sdwan or remote-access-server using a WAN interface as the IPsec endpoint are vulnerable. (IPsec profiles configured with an overlay interface as the IPsec endpoint are not affected.) This configuration typically applies to all Controllers, Hub Controllers, and SSE Gateways. Additionally, site-to-site VPN profiles configured without a peer IP address, hostname, or FQDN are also vulnerable. 
 
What is not impacted?  
 
The VOS nodes listed above are not vulnerable if they are not accessible from the Internet.

items.title: The Node.js web service on VOS (previously Versa FlexVNF) is used for URL-based Zero Touch Provisioning (ZTP) of the VO…
items.description:
The Node.js web service on VOS (previously Versa FlexVNF) is used for URL-based Zero Touch Provisioning (ZTP) of the VOS appliance and is not required after provisioning is complete. The /authenticate endpoint of this service passes user-supplied username and password values to child_process.exec() through a sanitizer (escapeRegExp) that removes regular expression metacharacters but not newline characters. An unauthenticated attacker can inject a newline character into the username field to execute arbitrary shell commands as the versa OS service user. No credentials are required; the attacker needs only a CSRF token, which can be obtained from an unauthenticated page load. 

Versa’s security hardening guide for Hubs, Branches, and Controllers recommends disabling the Node.js web service after the initial provisioning of the VOS device. This vulnerability is not exploitable on VOS devices where the Node.js web service has been disabled.

items.title: Mongoose: sanitizeFilter not applied on countDocuments
items.description: Mongoose is a MongoDB object modeling tool designed to work in an asynchronous environment. Prior to 6.13.11, 7.8.12, 8.24.3, and 9.9.2, Mongoose countDocuments() does not apply the configured sanitizeFilter query selector injection defense. An application that enables sanitizeFilter and passes attacker-controlled filter values to countDocuments() can therefore process query operator objects as operators rather than literal values, causing the count to include documents that should not match and potentially undermining authorization or application logic based on that count. This issue is fixed in versions 6.13.11, 7.8.12, 8.24.3, and 9.9.2.

items.title: Mongoose walks into inherited properties when hydrating, setting, and merging, allowing overwrites of built-in functions (denial of service) and shared schema state
items.description: Mongoose is a MongoDB object modeling tool designed to work in an asynchronous environment. Prior to 6.13.12, 7.8.13, 8.24.7, and 9.11.4, Mongoose can descend into inherited properties while loading database documents in init(), setting dotted paths in $__set, and merging update documents in utils.mergeClone. Attacker-controlled keys such as toString or valueOf can therefore cause Mongoose to write into shared built-in functions instead of an own property. A crafted document, Mixed path, non-strict document or subdocument, findOneAndReplace() replacement, chained update, or Query.prototype.merge() source can overwrite Object.prototype.toString.call, causing later queries on unrelated models to fail until the process restarts. Separately, when an attacker controls the dotted path passed to doc.set(path, value) for a subdocument configured with strict: false, descent through $__set can reach $__schema and alter shared validators or schema options for later documents. Mongoose already blocks __proto__, constructor, and prototype, so this issue overwrites properties on reachable shared objects rather than adding new properties directly to Object.prototype. This issue is fixed in versions 6.13.12, 7.8.13, 8.24.7, and 9.11.4.

items.title: Mongoose: Connection-level sanitizeFilter not applied
items.description: Mongoose is a MongoDB object modeling tool designed to work in an asynchronous environment. From 6.0.0 until 6.13.12, 7.8.13, 8.24.7, and 9.11.4, Mongoose stores the connection-level sanitizeFilter option in Connection.config, but Query.prototype._castConditions() and query casting check other option locations and do not read that configuration. An application that enables sanitizeFilter through mongoose.connect() or createConnection() and passes an attacker-controlled object into a query filter therefore receives a connection that reports the defense as enabled while query selector objects remain unsanitized. A crafted password value using a query operator can match an account record without the expected literal password, while global configuration through mongoose.set('sanitizeFilter') and per-query Model.find().sanitizeFilter() remain unaffected. This issue is fixed in versions 6.13.12, 7.8.13, 8.24.7, and 9.11.4.

items.title: Mongoose: Prototype pollution via Schema.prototype.virtual()
items.description: Mongoose is a MongoDB object modeling tool designed to work in an asynchronous environment. Prior to 6.13.12, 7.8.13, 8.24.7, and 9.11.4, Schema.prototype.virtual() builds nested virtual paths without applying the special-property validation already used by Schema.path() and Schema.add(). An attacker who can influence virtual field names in dynamic schemas, content-management form builders, or schema-as-code systems can supply path segments such as __proto__, constructor, or prototype, causing the virtual-path reducer to write enumerable properties to Object.prototype or Function.prototype. The resulting prototype pollution can spoof inherited property checks such as authorization flags and can provide function-prototype gadget state to other server-side JavaScript code. This issue is fixed in versions 6.13.12, 7.8.13, 8.24.7, and 9.11.4.

items.title: Novu provides an API for sending notifications through multiple channels.
items.description: Novu provides an API for sending notifications through multiple channels. Prior to 3.15.0, the conditions filter webhook in libs/application-generic/src/usecases/conditions-filter/conditions-filter.usecase.ts passes the user-configured child.webhookUrl directly to axios.post without calling validateUrlSsrf. Evaluating a workflow condition can therefore make the worker send a POST request to a private or link-local service and return the response data for condition evaluation. The response is stored in execution details and exposed through GET /execution-details, which can disclose credentials from POST-capable metadata services or data from internal services, although metadata endpoints that require GET are not reachable through this path. This issue is fixed in version 3.15.0.

items.title: Novu provides an API for sending notifications through multiple channels.
items.description: Novu provides an API for sending notifications through multiple channels. Prior to 3.17.0, validateUrlSsrf in libs/application-generic/src/utils/ssrf-url-validation.ts uses the isPrivateIp deny-list without covering the RFC6598 100.64.0.0/10 shared address space or its IPv4-mapped IPv6 forms. The workflow HTTP request step and webhook filter condition can therefore send server-side requests when a configured literal address or resolved hostname falls in that range. In Alibaba Cloud, 100.100.100.200 may expose instance metadata, while self-hosted and multi-tenant deployments may expose provider-internal services, private infrastructure, service meshes, or VPN resources reachable through CGNAT addressing. This issue is fixed in version 3.17.0.

items.title: The XRootD project provides a high-performance, fault-tolerant, and secure solution for handling large amounts of data…
items.description: The XRootD project provides a high-performance, fault-tolerant, and secure solution for handling large amounts of data distributed across multiple storage resources. Prior to version 5.9.2, XRootD's rpCheck() function in src/XrdXrootd/XrdXrootdXeq.cc rejects a parent-directory component only when two dots are followed by a slash and does not reject a terminal two-dot component. An unauthenticated attacker can append /.. to an exported path in xrdfs ls or an HTTP PROPFIND request, bypass the all.export directory scope, and cause directory and filename enumeration in the parent directory under oss.localroot. The demonstrated vector does not permit file download or disclose file contents. This issue is fixed in version 5.9.2.

items.title: Mongoose: Discriminator key values matching inherited properties (e.g. __t: 'constructor') bypass schema casting and can poison collections
items.description: Mongoose is a MongoDB object modeling tool designed to work in an asynchronous environment. Prior to 6.13.12, 7.8.13, 8.24.7, and 9.11.4, Mongoose uses attacker-controlled discriminator key values, including the default __t field, to index plain-object registries such as Model.discriminators and schema.discriminators without requiring an own property. Values such as constructor, toString, or hasOwnProperty can therefore resolve to inherited built-in functions instead of a registered discriminator, causing type confusion in model construction, document creation, hydration, query and update casting, embedded discriminators, and populate operations. In the bulkWrite() insertOne path with skipValidation enabled, a constructor value can cause a raw input object to be stored without schema casting or strict filtering, and a stored poisoned document can make every query that hydrates it fail until the document is removed. The weakness reads inherited properties but does not modify Object.prototype and is not prototype pollution. This issue is fixed in versions 6.13.12, 7.8.13, 8.24.7, and 9.11.4.
